issue:1000.body:
## Context

Split from #439 (closed). The two non-UI asks from that issue are already done: unbuffered long-running launches (#611) and the agent documentation (`skills/code-engineer/SKILL.md`). The remaining ask is tracked here.

## What's wanted

The session/job UI should show a process-level heartbeat for long-running work — live CPU, RSS, and last-output time — rather than relying on log-file mtime (or a quiet log) alone. Today a long job whose output is block-buffered looks stuck even while the process is busy.

## Scope / approach

TBD — the UI interaction still needs to be decided: where the telemetry lives, what granularity, how often it samples. Design to be confirmed before implementation.

Related: #434, #439.

issue:1006.body:
## What happens

The `Binary release (x86_64)` job fails at the very last step, after the artifact is built successfully:

```
Built /home/runner/work/sciencediscovery/sciencediscovery/dist/binary-release/ScienceDiscovery-d255bc9-linux-x86_64 (696.9 MiB, payload f381e6e7b55448e4f127d6fef344dc30)
Release artifact leaks a build-machine path: /home/runner
```

Two occurrences today, both in merge-queue runs for a PR that does not touch packaging (PR #999, which changes `apps/desktop` + `services/api` export saving):

| run | head | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [42491940459](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42491940459) | `fa9878e` | failed, same line |
| [42503143754](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754) | `1c585656` | failed, same line |

The same job passed minutes earlier and later on sibling queue runs ([42505053918](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42505053918) for #1004, [42496441065](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42496441065) for #992), so it is intermittent rather than tied to a head.

Both times the payload scan before it passed: `Payload scan: no build-machine paths found.`

## Why this looks like the gate's own false positive

The gate is `assert_no_release_build_paths()` in `scripts/package-binary-release.sh:94-112`. It greps the whole single-file artifact for `$repository_root`, `$output_dir`, `$HOME` and `$USERPROFILE`. On a GitHub-hosted runner `$HOME` is `/home/runner`.

The payload inside that artifact has already been checked by `assert_no_build_paths()` in `scripts/binary-release/build-payload.sh:144-191`, which deliberately allows two things the artifact-level check cannot:

1. For the `$HOME` needle it excludes `jiuwenswarm/` and `adapter/` (that dependency closure legitimately mentions `/home/runner`).
2. It passes two supplier SBOMs through `scripts/binary-release/filter-upstream-sbom-paths.mjs`, because `pydantic_core-*.dist-info/sboms/pydantic-core.cyclonedx.json` and `watchfiles-*.dist-info/sboms/watchfiles_rust_notify.cyclonedx.json` carry upstream references of the form `path+file:///home/runner/work/pydantic/...` and `path+file:///home/runner/work/watchfiles/...`.

So the payload scan passing tells us the only `/home/runner` occurrences in the payload are the ones it has already ruled acceptable. The artifact-level scan then re-checks those same bytes with no allowance and no way to exclude a subtree, and the only needle that can match is the generic `$HOME` — a bare `/home/runner`, not this build's repository root.

Intermittency fits the layout: the artifact is the pinned `node` binary plus an injected SEA blob plus a `tar | zstd` payload plus a 48-byte footer (`scripts/binary-release/build-binary.mjs:232-262`), so the approved SBOM bytes only appear verbatim when zstd emits that region as a stored block.

## Impact

It blocks the merge queue for PRs that never touch packaging, and each occurrence costs a full payload build (about 9 minutes) plus a queue round-trip. #999 has been kicked out twice today; `merge-gate` goes red as collateral.

## Suggested fix

- Keep the artifact-level check for the build-specific needles only (`$repository_root`, `$output_dir`) — a match there cannot be an upstream coincidence — and drop `$HOME`/`$USERPROFILE` from it, since `build-payload.sh` already covers those with the allowances that a single compressed blob cannot apply.
- Or run the artifact-level check against the decompressed payload (the `--keep-payload` tree) so the SBOM filter can apply to it as well.
- Worth a case in the existing `scripts/binary-release/*.test.mjs` suite: a payload whose only `/home/runner` hits are the two approved SBOM references must pass both checks.

To confirm locally: build with `--keep-payload` and grep the payload tree for `/home/runner`; the hits should be exactly those two SBOMs plus anything under `jiuwenswarm/` or `adapter/`.

issue:1007.body:
## What happens

The `UT` job fails intermittently with one test short of the plan, always in the same place:

```
- ut: status FAIL
- ut: passed 6939 of 6940 planned
- ut: 1 failed
- ut: NODE_WORKER_FAILED: worker-1
- ut: NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED: services/api/src/server.test.ts
- ut: FAIL: services/api/src/server.test.ts::updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password@linux/amd64
```

`services/api/src/server.test.ts` has already logged `Done 512/605: services/api/src/server.test.ts (180712ms)` earlier in the same run, so the failure is not at an assertion in the test body: it is the file's teardown.

## Occurrences

Four times in one afternoon, on three unrelated PRs, every one of them a different head:

| PR | run | attempt | UT job | named test | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #999 | [42487399804](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42487399804) (merge queue) | 1 | [128752365509](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42487399804/job/128752365509) | `Workspace HTTP writes wait for the active writer and publish refs before returning` | 6909/6910 |
| #734 | [42482149231](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42482149231) | 1 | [128736356154](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42482149231/job/128736356154) | `updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password` | 6939/6940 |
| #1004 | [42485316924](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42485316924) | 1 | [128745961451](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42485316924/job/128745961451) | `Workspace HTTP writes wait for the active writer and publish refs before returning` | 6906/6907 |
| #999 | [42503143754](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754) (merge queue) | 1 | [128800209585](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754/job/128800209585) | `updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password` | 6935/6936 |

`#734` attempt 2 and `#1004` attempt 2, on the same commits, passed. Two of the four blocked the merge queue (`merge-gate` goes red as collateral), so each one costs a queue round-trip plus a nine-minute payload/CI re-run.

## Why this is the harness, not the PR under test

- `NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED` is emitted only for a `test:fail` event that carries no per-test token — a file-scope hook or a collection failure, by construction: `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs:128`.
- `NODE_WORKER_FAILED: worker-1` means the `node --test` worker process for that file exited non-zero: `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs:195`. So the process died, and the "1 failed" test is the plan's attribution of that, not a failed expectation.
- The named test changes between runs while the file is byte-identical, which a genuine assertion failure in one specific case would not do.
- The four runs span three PRs whose diffs never touch `services/api/src/server.test.ts`, the SSH credential path or the workspace writer path: #734 is configuration capabilities, #1004 is shell-execution settlement, #999 is desktop/API export saving.
- Every occurrence passes on a plain re-run of the same commit.

## Suggested fix

- `server.test.ts` registers many teardown hooks as `context.after(() => new Promise((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve())))` (`:868`, `:872`, `:2578`, `:2582`, `:1933`, ...). `server.close()`'s callback does not fire while an idle keep-alive client socket is still open, so such a hook can hang and take the worker down with it. The file already has the shared `closeApiServer()` helper (`:152`, `:160`) that the rest of the file uses; those hooks should use it too, or pair each `close()` with `closeAllConnections()` the way `:591` does for the adapter.
- The two named tests both start a probe against a stub server. Ending that probe explicitly in the test's own `after` hook, and awaiting it, removes the most likely lingering handle.
- Give the hooks a timeout so a stuck teardown reports the hook and the file by name, instead of surfacing as a worker exit with no reason attached.
- Complementary: have the coordinator include the worker's exit code and signal in the `NODE_WORKER_FAILED` annotation. Right now the only thing a reader gets is `worker-1`, which is what makes every occurrence cost a manual log dig.

Reported from PR review triage; not tied to any single PR.

issue:1029.body:
## Summary

The containment added by #857 stops an escaped scheduler write from killing the API (the #816 defect), but two recovery gaps around it remain. Both were raised as `medium, suggestion` in the 2026-11-09 review of `9bf5077f7b4104564bdee110c4f001f7b1d4a403` (F5 and F4), and neither is implemented here.

### 1. An escape raised while re-reading the run list skips the backoff entirely

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3738` is the file's own `finally`:

```ts
    } finally {
      scheduledSessions.delete(sessionId);
      const remaining = await store.listSessionRuns(sessionId);
```

If that read rejects (an unreadable `session-runs/` directory — the same ownership/ACL misconfiguration the cap path exists for), the promise rejects before `schedulerEscapes` is touched or `setTimeout` is reached. The `.catch` at `:3762` logs `run_scheduler_failed` and that is all: no timer, no counter, no `run_scheduler_stopped`. The comment at `:3767-3773` names this read as one of the escape sites and states the reschedule "is delayed and capped", which is not true for it.

Measured on `9bf5077f` with `listSessionRuns` mocked to reject: exactly 2 calls, no retry, no rejection reaches the process. The session silently stops scheduling while a run is still `queued`.

**Fix shape suggested in the review:** make the `finally` body tolerant so the escape still takes the backoff branch.

```ts
      let remaining: SessionRun[] = [];
      try { remaining = await store.listSessionRuns(sessionId); } catch { /* fall through with escaped already set */ }
```

### 2. After the cap, the queued run has only a server log

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3747`: the sixth consecutive escape (delays 500 + 1000 + 2000 + 4000 + 8000 ms ≈ 15.5 s) logs `run_scheduler_stopped` and stops. The run stays `queued` on disk, and nothing schedules it again in process — `recoverSessionRuns` only handles `running`/`blocked`, so recovery depends on the bootstrap sweep (`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:747-770`) or another HTTP-triggered `scheduleSessionRuns`.

Measured on `9bf5077f` with `updateSessionRunStatusIfCurrent` made to fail and then to succeed: **6** transition attempts and **12** `listSessionRuns` calls in 19.5 s, then **0** attempts after the fault cleared, with the run still `queued`. Realistic causes are an ownership/ACL problem that outlives 15 s, a full disk, or a long scanner hold.

**Impact:** the chat never starts and the user sees neither a failure nor a message, while #816's expected result asks for an actionable error on the affected run when persistence cannot recover.

## What it should do

- An escape raised inside the `finally` must take the same delayed-and-capped path as an escape raised inside the loop; the comment already promises it.
- After the cap, the affected run should carry an error the API returns (mark it `failed`, or `interrupted` with a reason), or the stop should become a slow fixed retry — `SCHEDULER_RETRY_MAX_MS` already allows 30 s.

## Why this is not in #857

The review classified both as `medium, suggestion`, and the second is marked `[Needs a person]`: choosing between "fail the run with an actionable error" and "retry slowly forever" changes what a user sees after an unrecoverable state write, so it is a decision, not a mechanical fix. #857 carries only its must-fix (the retry closure dropped `executionGovernance`).

## Not implemented

Nothing in this issue is implemented and no pull request is open for it.

## What happens

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts` → **"Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs"** (test declared at `:203`, step 6 `等待修复并恢复调用`, body at `:314`) fails at `test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:332`:

```
  1) [mocked] › ../test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:203:1 › journey-custom-mcp.spec › Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs › 6. 等待修复并恢复调用

    Error: expect(received).toBeGreaterThan(expected)

    Expected: > 2
    Received:   2

      330 |       expect(terminal.status, terminal.error).toBe("completed");
      331 |       const recovered = await invocations();
    > 332 |       expect(recovered.length).toBeGreaterThan(before);
          |                                ^
```

Everything before the assertion in step 6 succeeds: the repair card `执行受阻` shows `等待 MCP 修复` with the disabled source id, `GET /api/sessions/<id>/mcp/invocations` stays at 2 while blocked, the server is re-enabled, `已修复，重新检查` is clicked, and `waitForRunTerminal` returns `completed`.

What the run then shows: the assistant's last message in that run is `MCP RECOVERED`, which the scripted model only emits **after** its `mcp_recovered_call` step (`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:243-247`):

```ts
[
  { tool: "mcp_readiness", arguments: { action: "wait", reason: "This task requires the selected echo source", sourceIds: [second.id] } },
  { tool: "mcp_recovered_call", arguments: { sourceId: second.id, toolId: second.toolId, input: { text: "mcp recovered" } } },
  { text: "MCP RECOVERED" },
],
```

So the scripted model did emit `mcp_recovered_call`, and the run continued past it, but no MCP invocation was recorded for that turn: `/api/sessions/<id>/mcp/invocations` still lists exactly the 2 invocations from the earlier runs (`custom-cbf8e…`, `custom-cea28…`), and the captured trace resource `0000f751….json` holds the same 2. The recovered call therefore never reached `McpSourceCatalog`/broker (`packages/artifact-manager/src/mcp-workspace-tools.ts` `mcpReadiness.invoke`), and the failure is silent to the user: the run completes and the message claims recovery.

## Where it is seen (evidence only)

The same journey, same assertion, fails on three unrelated heads:

| run | job | head | shard window (UTC) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [42619667305](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42619667305) | [129188246374](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42619667305/job/129188246374) | `9bf5077f7b` (#857 tip) | 13:38–13:58 failure |
| [42622133086](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42622133086) | [129181494939](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42622133086/job/129181494939) | `87c5da950b` (`codex/conversation-proxy-resources`) | 13:39–13:59 failure |
| [42615122979](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42615122979) | [129160327871](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42615122979/job/129160327871) | `127bb1fdef` (merge queue, `pr-1005`) | 12:34–12:54 failure |

It also passes on other heads in the same window, including main running the journey while the two 13:3x failures were in flight:

- main `c3678320ac`: run [42621321893](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42621321893) job [129188930633](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42621321893/job/129188930633), `✓ 21 … Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs (44.4s)` at 13:39:17Z, shard success (13:34–13:49).
- main `9feafa2730`: run [42562181452](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42562181452) job [128981184690](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42562181452/job/128981184690), `✓ 21` at 04:38:35Z. That shard job is red overall because of a different journey (`journey-first-run.spec.ts:59`), so the shard verdict alone does not describe this journey.

`L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)` outcomes for completed runs created between 11:30Z and 14:00Z (jobs read one by one; cancelled runs excluded): **3 failure / 16 success**, and the three failures are the table above. Two of the green runs are `dev2/fix/upload-windows-reserved-names` `0c5f26ab03` (13:33:34Z) and `dev/884-bug-comparing-two-binary-artifact-versio` `cefe1ebd79` (13:25:34Z).

## Not caused by the #857 diff

#857 (`9bf5077f7b`) changes exactly two files, `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` and `services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts` (+210/−23); the merge ref `fdf61b56798086e573368bc82120e91e8c5cc52b` for its failing job has parents `9feafa27` + `9bf5077f` and nothing else. The two other failing heads carry none of that diff. The failing journey exercises custom-MCP registration, the repair wait and `mcp_recovered_call` — not the scheduler's delayed retry pass. #857 is linked only because its shard run is one of the three observations, not as the cause.

## What is not yet known

Whether this is a product race (the recovered call is dropped or rejected after `catalog.refresh`, so a real user also loses the recovered invocation while the message claims it ran) or a test that stops waiting too early (it asserts the invocation list immediately after the terminal state). The two need different fixes, and the 3-of-19 rate above is the only discriminator so far: a deterministic loss is a product gap, an occasional one points at the wait.

Not run: local reproduction of the journey (20 consecutive runs on a local stack). The stack could not be started in the reporting environment — the pnpm store lives on a read-only home, the pinned Chromium download did not complete, and the JiuwenSwarm virtualenv install had not finished when this was filed. No code was changed for this report.

issue:107.body:
## Background

ScienceDiscovery is strengthening its end-to-end test coverage. We want to collect the complete user journeys that the community believes must remain continuously protected.

This RFC does not prescribe an implementation. It focuses on four questions: **What task is the user trying to complete? What outcomes must be observable? Does the scenario require a real model? Should it run as a pull-request gate or as a scheduled test?**

## How to contribute

Copy the comment template below and add one row for each proposed test scenario. Maintainers will periodically consolidate actionable feedback into the main table.

Guidelines:

- **Test scenario**: describe a complete flow from the user's goal, rather than an internal function or an isolated component.
- **Observations**: list user-visible outcomes and critical states, such as the final answer, tool calls, permissions, artifacts, citations, and recovery after a refresh.
- **Test method**: use `Mock LLM`, `Real LLM`, or `Both`, and explain why a real model is necessary when applicable.
- **Estimated token usage**: use `0 (scripted)` for Mock LLM cases; for Real LLM cases, estimate total input and output tokens for one run.
- **Estimated duration**: give the target duration for one case, excluding first-time dependency installation.
- **Priority**: use `P0` for basic platform availability, `P1` for core scientific capabilities, and `P2` for enhancements or corner cases.
- **Notes**: record environment requirements, external services, credentials, cost, side effects, candidate benchmark sources, or stability risks.

## Initial candidates

The following entries are both examples of the requested format and an initial backlog. The community is welcome to refine their priority, observations, estimates, and execution method.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Basic multi-turn conversation and refresh recovery | The run completes; the second turn uses conversation history; message order, terminal state, and refreshed content remain consistent | Mock LLM | Session, Agent Loop, History, SSE | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | No external network |
| Tool call, permission, and continued reasoning | Permission moves from pending to allowed; the tool executes once; its result returns to the model; the Agent continues and finishes | Mock LLM | Tool, Permission, Runner, Agent Loop | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a safe local tool fixture |
| Plan creation, update, and completion | Plan and step states remain ordered and correct; updates do not block tools; the final state persists and recovers | Mock LLM | Plan, Context, Workspace UI | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a deterministic tool-call sequence |
| Subagent delegation and result return | The child Agent lifecycle is complete; tool ownership is correct; the result returns to the lead Agent; reasoning continues; refresh restores the state | Mock LLM | Subagent, Team, Tool, Context | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | No external provider |
| Generate and deliver an artifact | The file exists; deliverables are distinct from temporary files; preview and download work; provenance is traceable; the final answer references the artifact | Mock LLM | Workspace, Artifact, Provenance, Tool | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | Use a local Python or Shell environment |
| Literature review | The Agent searches multiple sources, retrieves and extracts selected papers, produces traceable citations, handles source failures, and delivers a review artifact | Both | MCP, Literature Sources, Governed Download, PDF Extraction, Citation, Review | 0 mocked; 20k–60k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Real run requires network access and may depend on source availability |
| Evolve a solution | The Agent defines an objective and evaluation, runs iterative candidates, preserves checkpoints and logs, compares results, and delivers the best reproducible solution | Both | Evolve, Runner, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Candidate source: Terminal-Bench-Science |

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** Three real cases die within seconds to a few minutes with the same gateway message, even though the gateway had already answered `200` and was streaming:

```text
Error: Main run must complete with readable, nonempty declared final artifacts;
delivery_status=failed; run_status=failed; delivered_artifacts=0;
run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

Shards and durations on Nightly run [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462) (sha `4bb737c2`):

| shard | case | duration |
|---|---|---|
| research-1 | DRB-58 medium-hard Swarm research integration | 51.5 s |
| research-2 | DRB-59 easy Swarm research integration | 3.9 min |
| research-5 | DRB-75 very-hard Swarm research integration | 50.8 s |

**Evidence that the stream, not the product, broke.** `stack.log` of shard `research-1` (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-1`, id 13805059079) records that request as:

```json
[model-sse-summary] {"requestId":"model-f758639a-...","httpStatus":200,"attempts":1,"retries":0,
  "elapsedMs":29176,"sseRecords":1208,"error":{"classification":"network"}}
```

So: headers `200`, 1208 SSE records delivered over ~29 s, then the transport died; `attempts:1, retries:0` — the API never retried. The previous Nightly (`c95f080`, run 42519625781) failed the same way on `research-4` (`read ECONNRESET`) and `research-6` (`other side closed`), so this is a recurring class, not a one-off.

**Why it is scored as the product's fault.** `.ci` accounting for this run reports:

```text
Planned 21; executed 21; passed 15; provider faults 0.
```

`test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs:126-146` classifies a provider fault only when the text carries a 5xx status **or** one of `no available channel` / `model_not_found` / `new_api_error`. `APIError: read ECONNRESET` and `other side closed` carry neither, so these three failures stay plain `FAIL` and the gate treats them as regressions.

**Expected / decision needed.** Two separate questions:

1. **Retry (code):** a mid-stream transport break after `200` currently ends an 8–50 minute case. A bounded retry (one attempt, only when no tool result has been committed yet) would turn most of these into passes. This is a behaviour change and needs sign-off.
2. **Accounting (gate semantics):** should a failure whose only evidence is a broken transport, with no HTTP status, be recorded as `PROVIDER_FAULT`? Today it cannot be, and the result is a red Nightly for a provider outage.

Recommendation: land (1) as its own change and keep (2) separate, because (2) changes what "green Nightly" means.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`.
- GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`; Nightly (`profile: daily`) real E2E, run started 2026-11-10T21:44:15Z (2026-11-11 05:44 CST).
- Model endpoint `https://api-4-agent-ci-infra.llmbots.co/v1`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-flash`, `E2E_LLM_API_VARIANT=deepseek`, thinking mode enabled/low.
- Same failure class on the 2026-11-08 Nightly (`c95f080`, shards `research-4`/`research-6`).

### Additional Information

Shard `research-3` on the same run (`DRB-62`) failed differently — `run_error=interaction round execution failed` from `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` — and its `stack.log` does not retain the inner cause, so it is **not** claimed as the same root cause here. It is mentioned only so the two are not merged by mistake.

### Version Information

- `main` @ `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`
- Nightly run 42907916462; artifacts `real-e2e-evidence-research-1` (13805059079), `-2` (13805882980), `-5` (13806203752)
- Previous occurrence: Nightly 42519625781 (`c95f080`), shards `research-4`, `research-6`

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** The mocked E2E suite is `87/88` and the one red case fails not on product behaviour but on a browser console error raised by the suite's own teardown:

```text
Error: no console/page errors expected, got:
[error] Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
  @ http://127.0.0.1:4410/api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6/research-package/preview?sessionId=6bcfc3e0-...
```

Case: `test/agent-run-componentization.spec.ts:380` — `S2b subagent 首个受控工具的权限卡也出现在主对话最外层`. Job `Gate / L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)` (job id 130151439627) on Nightly run [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462), sha `4bb737c2`.

**Evidence.** The mocked stack's `stack.log` (in `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys`, artifact id 13807782121) shows the request arrives **after** the project was deleted by teardown:

```text
GET  /api/evolve/status HTTP/1.1 200 OK
DELETE /api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
POST /cleanup/project HTTP/1.1 200 OK
DELETE /api/models/4eea8f0a-... HTTP/1.1 200 OK
GET  /api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6/research-package/preview?sessionId=6bcfc3e0-...&defaults=1 HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

The same log carries **59** such `404` responses on `research-package/preview`, and in another case the deleted Session is still polled directly:

```text
GET /api/sessions/c6603f8c-e86e-46dd-a455-b87ff206c4fd/runs HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
GET /api/sessions/c6603f8c-e86e-46dd-a455-b87ff206c4fd/agent-activity HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

So the panel keeps polling a project/session that teardown has just removed. The browser logs every 404 as a console error, and the journey's "no console errors" assertion turns that into a failed case.

**Expected.** One of these, whichever the team prefers:

1. A mounted panel stops polling once its project/session is deleted (listen for the deletion the test performs, or cancel the poll on unmount).
2. The preview read treats "project gone" as a normal end of polling and does not surface it as a console error (checked request + handled 404, instead of an unhandled resource load).
3. The assertion is scoped to the case's own session being alive.

(1) is the honest fix: the product should not keep asking the API about a project it has removed.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`.
- Mocked E2E (`profile: daily`, `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)`), 88 planned / 87 passed / 1 failed; run started 2026-11-10T21:44:15Z (2026-11-11 05:44 CST).
- Stack: adapter 4410 → Node API 4510, runner 4411, memory-graph 17774; no real model calls in this job.

### Additional Information

This is a harness/teardown race rather than a user-facing delivery failure, but it reds the mocked gate on its own. It is unrelated to the four real-E2E failures on the same run (see the linked issues).

### Version Information

- `main` @ `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`
- Nightly run 42907916462; job 130151439627; artifact `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys` (13807782121)

### Checklist

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Split out of #1049, which this issue does not replace: #1059 fixes the download path (the OA bucket locator and the misattributed "record not found"), and this issue is the other half of §5 — the readiness signal.

**What is still true after #1059.** `services/api/src/plugins/catalog.ts` never probes a provider. A configured integration can be completely dead — every call fails with a provider-side outage — and the readiness/health view still reports it as ready, because readiness only reads configuration, never a probe result. In that state the only way anyone learns the integration is down is an agent that actually calls the tool and reports the `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` guidance back to the user.

**Why it matters.** The issue that produced #1049 was found exactly this way: the failure was visible only in a run's tool result, not in the surface a maintainer would check first. §10 of #1049 repeats this: the product kept reporting ready while the download path was dead.

**Expected.** An endpoint-level failure that the gateway already classifies (`ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE` / `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`) should reach the readiness view, so a dead integration is visible before an agent stumbles into it. How long such a signal stays authoritative, and whether it is a probe or a last-failure timestamp, needs a decision here — the download fix in #1059 does not depend on it.

### Additional Information

The classification this issue builds on is the one #1059 lands: `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/http_errors.py` and the broker's `upstreamError` mapping. Readiness (`catalog.ts`) is untouched by #1059 on purpose, so the two changes can be judged separately.

issue:1090.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Issue #817 defined four acceptance criteria across three CI engineering capabilities: test coverage gating, CI stability, and release CI efficiency (`<5h`). Three pull requests have since landed on `main`:

- **PR #951** (`2c33bc5017`): migrated 11 previously unscheduled Playwright specs (41 case identities) onto the shared PR plan (`L2` mocked E2E) and removed the `legacy` Playwright project (`status:legacy`, `ci:e2e:legacy`, `test:legacy*`, `CI_ALLOW_LEGACY`).
- **PR #940** (`360e6b664f`): preserved `reasoning_effort: low` across Evolve and search paths, added bounded upstream transport retries (502/503/504/524 and mid-stream socket resets) for streaming model completions, and configured Nightly model and judge calls to run with `low` effort in `nightly-research` with a 75-minute research-team timeout.
- **PR #971** (`1db615cdd2`): narrowed the active BiomniBench-DA L5 execution set from 50 to 45 cases (64 total real L5 cases), pinned Biomni generator and rubric judge thinking to `enabled` with `low` effort, scaled additive resource baselines by `45/50`, and recovered `da-11-1` when a stream ends cleanly inside truncated tool-call JSON.

### Audit of #817 Acceptance Criteria on Current `main`

Measured against the latest completed `main` CI run [42968972446](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42968972446) (`679038182e`) and recent L5 / Release runs:

#### 1. Coverage thresholds and gating
- **1.1 Coverage gate enforcement**: **Not met** — `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs` and `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` remain informational only (`Coverage is informational. No minimum percentage is enforced`), and the Coverage job still merges only `ut` and `st` (mocked browser E2E is not measured).
- **1.2 Whole-repo line coverage ≥80%**: **Met** — **80.82%** (`203,344 / 251,596`; Node.js `81.18%`, Python `73.93%`, up from the `73.11%` baseline at `6d3c49a`).
- **1.3 Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70%**: **Not met** — **59.86%** (`98,788 / 165,035`; Node.js `59.80%`, Python `62.06%`), **10.14 percentage points** below the `70%` target.
- **1.4 Function coverage ≥80%**: **Met (Node.js)** — **80.08%** (`13,142 / 16,411`; Python function coverage is not separately reported).
- **1.5 Statement coverage ≥80%**: **Not implemented** — `summary.json` reports `lines`, `branches`, and `functions` only.
- **1.6 New / changed code (PR diff) coverage ≥80%**: **Not implemented** — no PR diff coverage calculation, summary comment, or gate check exists in CI.
- **1.7 Per-package coverage floor ≥60%**: **Partially met** — `apps/web` (`62.89%`) and Node `services/runner` (`88.55%`) now exceed `60%`, while `packages/idea-tree` (`45.94%`), `packages/schema` (`57.89%`), and Python `services/runner` (`0%`) remain below `60%`.
- **1.8 Core-path coverage ≥90%**: **Partially met** — `services/api` (`94.84%`), `packages/sandbox-capability` (`100%`), and `packages/model` (`96.48%`) exceed `90%` line coverage, while `services/gateway` (`75.23%`) and `services/runner` (`88.55%`) are below `90%`, and no dedicated core-path gate is enforced.

#### 2. Case-level profile and module coverage
- **2.1 No case outside every profile**: **Partially met** — PR #951 eliminated all 42 `status:legacy` dead cases by moving 41 valid browser identities into the `pr` (`L2`) profile. Remaining cases outside `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` rules are 79 `status:external` UT/ST cases, 1 `status:quarantined` case (`test/literature-review.spec.ts`), 1 `npu:required` case, 1 `category:st + model:real` case, and 6 `os:macos` cases; `ci:catalog:check` does not yet fail on profile-unreachable tags.
- **2.2 Every module mapped to an executing gating case**: **Not implemented** — the tagged catalog does not yet carry an explicit case-to-module ownership mapping or fail when a module has no executing case.

#### 3. CI stability and flake governance
- **3.1 Automated flake identification and quarantine**: **Not implemented** — no rolling failure-rate detector, automatic quarantine transition, or tracking-issue workflow is in place.
- **3.2 Infrastructure-only retries for network/gateway faults**: **Partially met** — PR #940 and PR #971 implemented bounded transport/stream retries and clean-EOF tool-argument recovery without retrying product defects, but per-case infrastructure retry counts and gateway-outage separation are not yet surfaced in the CI summary.
- **3.3 Thinking-mode (`low` / off) A/B experiment and CI configuration**: **Partially met** — PR #940 and PR #971 pinned Nightly and Biomni L5 runs to `reasoning_effort: low` without changing product defaults, while a formal multi-run A/B pass-rate and variance comparison report remains open.

#### 4. Release CI efficiency (`<5h`)
- **4.1 L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours**: **Not met** — after PR #971 landed, the `main` L5 run [42380603816](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42380603816) (`l5 · parallel=4 · nightly-research`) ran for **15h 39m** (2026-11-07 14:13Z to 2026-11-08 05:52Z, failed); prior branch L5 runs [42340397412](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42340397412) and [42236770100](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42236770100) took **8h 49m** and **7h 30m**; the latest `Release` workflow run [41196686771](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41196686771) took **25h 01m**.
- **4.2 In-pipeline duration budget tracking and over-budget alerts**: **Not implemented** — no 5-hour budget table or alert check is wired into `release.yml` or `ci.yml`.
- **4.3 Bulk data downloads managed via cache/prefetch with zero redundant downloads on cache hit**: **Not implemented** — bulk downloads across jobs are not yet uniformly cached/prefetched and timed against the budget.
- **4.4 Real-model journeys running at lowest thinking effort with latency gain recorded**: **Partially met** — `low` effort is active for Nightly and Biomni L5, but before/after per-case p50/p95 latency gain reports have not been published.

---

### Scope of Follow-up Work Tracked by This Issue

Based on the audit above, the following four deliverables require continued development:

1. **Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70% (Item 1.3)**: raise combined Node.js + Python branch coverage from the current **59.86%** (`98,788 / 165,035`) to **≥70%**, and enforce the threshold in CI.
2. **New / changed code (PR diff) coverage ≥80% (Item 1.6)**: compute diff coverage on pull requests against the merge base and enforce a **≥80%** diff coverage gate on executable changed lines/branches in CI.
3. **L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours (Item 4.1)**: reduce full L5 release pipeline wall-clock duration to **<5 hours**, with per-job budget accounting and over-budget alerts in the pipeline summary.
4. **Cache/prefetch management for all bulk data downloads with zero redundant downloads on cache hit (Item 4.3)**: audit and cache/prefetch all bulk downloads in CI (JiuwenSwarm ~1.5 GB runtime and virtualenvs, pnpm/uv dependencies, benchmark datasets and fixtures, model/sidecar assets, and container/base images), record download duration separately, and eliminate repeat bulk downloads when caches hit.

## Design Ideas

1. **Whole-repo branch coverage ≥70%**:
   - Prioritize packages with the largest uncovered branch mass in `coverage/summary.json` and `coverage/python/summary.json` (such as `services/api` at `54.79%` branches, `packages/workspace` at `55.72%`, `packages/artifact-manager` at `56.63%`, `services/gateway` at `57.22%`, `services/memory-graph` at `56.95%`, and `apps/web` at `70.73%`).
   - Add targeted unit and system tests for error branches, boundary guards, and fallback paths, and wire the `≥70%` branch threshold into `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` / `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`.

2. **PR diff coverage ≥80%**:
   - Extend `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` (or add a dedicated diff-coverage step in the `Coverage` job) to intersect `git diff <base>...<head>` hunk lines with merged LCOV / JSON coverage records from Node.js (`ut` + `st`) and Python (`coverage.py`).
   - Publish a clear per-file diff coverage table in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and fail the `Coverage` / `merge-gate` check when changed executable lines fall below `80%`.

3. **L5 release CI end-to-end duration <5 hours**:
   - Add per-job wall-clock and phase timing (setup/download vs. execution) to the L5 summary and enforce a `<5h` (`18,000s`) end-to-end budget check.
   - Combine shard parallelism tuning, long-tail case timeout/step-budget tightening, and deduplication of overlapping lower-tier work in the release profile so the end-to-end critical path stays under 5 hours.

4. **Bulk data download caching and prefetching**:
   - Inventory every multi-hundred-megabyte download across `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `real-e2e.yml`, and `release.yml` (JiuwenSwarm bundle and Python virtualenvs, Node/pnpm stores, benchmark datasets/fixtures, browser binaries, and Docker layers).
   - Key caches by lockfile/manifest content hashes, warm them once in an upstream setup step or shared cache entry, and log cache-hit status plus download byte/time metrics in each job summary so cache-hit runs perform zero redundant bulk downloads.

## Involved Public APIs

None. All changes are internal to CI workflows, coverage reporting/gating scripts, and test suites; no product HTTP, CLI, or SDK APIs are added or modified.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`: coverage gating, bulk-download cache orchestration, and L5 duration budget reporting.
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`, `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`: whole-repo branch coverage gate (`≥70%`) and PR diff coverage calculation/gate (`≥80%`).
- `packages/*`, `services/*`, `apps/*` test suites: branch coverage additions to lift whole-repo branch coverage from `59.86%` to `≥70%`.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Branch coverage ≥70%**: run `pnpm test:shared` with coverage enabled and `node scripts/coverage-report.mjs`; verify merged whole-repo branch coverage is `≥70.00%` and that lowering the threshold or dropping coverage causes the gate script unit tests to fail.
- **PR diff coverage ≥80%**: add unit tests for the diff-coverage calculator covering added, modified, deleted, and non-executable files, plus a synthetic PR diff below and above `80%` to verify both the step summary table and non-zero exit code on failure.
- **L5 <5h and bulk download caching**: verify on consecutive CI / L5 runs that cache-hit jobs report `cache-hit: true` with near-zero download time for JiuwenSwarm, dependencies, and datasets, that the pipeline summary outputs the job timing breakdown against the 5-hour budget, and that the end-to-end L5 run completes in `<5 hours`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Merged whole-repo branch coverage (`Node.js + Python` across `ut` + `st`) reaches **≥70.00%** (up from `59.86%`), and the CI coverage gate fails if whole-repo branch coverage drops below `70%`.
- [ ] Pull request CI computes diff coverage on changed executable lines against the PR base and fails the gate when PR diff coverage is below **80.00%**, with the per-file diff breakdown rendered in the job summary.
- [ ] All bulk data downloads in CI (JiuwenSwarm install and virtualenvs, pnpm/uv dependencies, benchmark datasets/fixtures, and runtime assets) are managed through content-addressed cache/prefetch steps, download duration is measured separately, and cache-hit runs perform zero redundant bulk downloads.
- [ ] The L5 release CI pipeline finishes end-to-end in **<5 hours** (`<300 minutes`) and publishes a per-job duration vs. budget summary with automatic over-budget alerting.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` and `pnpm test:shared`.

## Additional Information

- Parent tracking issue: #817
- Related merged PRs: #940, #951, #971
- Reference CI runs audited:
  - `main` coverage run: [42968972446](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42968972446) (`679038182e`)
  - L5 runs: [42380603816](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42380603816) (`15h 39m`), [42340397412](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42340397412) (`8h 49m`), [42236770100](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42236770100) (`7h 30m`)
  - Release run: [41196686771](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41196686771) (`25h 01m`)

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**现象**：在会话里让模型「帮我打开 UniProt 这个 MCP 服务器」，模型发起 `connector.enable` 请求（scope = 本次会话，激活模式 same_run）。界面弹出「启用连接器」卡片，但正文只有一句「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」，可用动作只有「关闭」，既没有确认/拒绝，也没有跳转到设置的入口。关闭后该请求被记为拒绝，模型回复「未启用 —— 本次会话中没有打开 UniProt MCP 服务器」，并声明不会再就同一配置需求重新发起请求。

**复现步骤**
1. 新建会话，输入「帮我打开 UniProt 这个 MCP 服务器」
2. 模型调用 configuration 工具的 `connector.enable`（describe → propose）发起启用请求
3. 会话内出现「启用连接器」卡片：正文「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」，只有「关闭」按钮
4. 点击「关闭」后卡片变为「启用连接器 · 暂不配置 · 原任务已完成」，模型回复连接器未启用（`sessionEnabled=false`），整个任务中 UniProt 工具均不可用

**代码定位（main，2026-11-11）**
- 卡片正文来自 packages/configuration-ui/src/messages.ts 的 `compact.unavailable`「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」；当 compact 卡片被归为 `unsupported` 时，ConfigurationRequestCard.tsx 中 `collapsedEditor = compact?.unsupported` 为真，编辑器被收起，只留「关闭」。
- 归类逻辑在 apps/desktop/src/app/configuration-presentation.ts 的 `connector.enable` 分支：仅当 `state === "awaiting_confirmation"` 且有 `previewDigest`（即 ready），且 `enabledConnectorIds` 的 before/after 能解析为「精确新增一个 id」时才返回 `{ connectorAddition: true }`，其余一律 `{ unsupported: true }`。
- 对比：apps/web 有专门的会话内连接器卡片（ConversationalConnectorCard.tsx）可以批准；桌面端没有对应实现，而 `unsupported` 兜底文案里的「原版界面」在桌面安装包里并不存在，用户无处可点。

**期望行为**
- 桌面端支持在会话内批准 `connector.enable`（session scope / same_run），至少提供「启用 / 不启用」两个明确动作，并在启用后让本次运行拿到该连接器工具
- 若确实暂不支持，卡片应给出可操作入口（如「前往 设置 → MCP/连接器」），而不是「请用原版界面」；同时应明确提供「拒绝」，避免模型把「关闭卡片」当成用户拒绝并不再重试
- 该能力在桌面端不可用时，不应让模型发起这类请求；至少提示用户只能在设置页手动开启

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- 应用：ScienceDiscovery 桌面版（Windows x64）
- 系统：Windows 11 专业版 25H2（10.0.26200）
- 界面语言：中文
- 场景：会话内让模型启用 UniProt MCP 连接器（connector.enable，session scope，same_run）

### Additional Information

两张截图：
1. 对话中的「启用连接器」卡片：正文「暂不支持，请用原版界面。」，右下角只有「关闭」
2. 关闭后的回执「启用连接器 · 暂不配置 · 原任务已完成」，以及模型的结论：未启用，已提交的 connector.enable 请求被拒绝，UniProt 连接器保持 sessionEnabled=false

### Version Information

- 版本：0.3.0 日包（daily build）
- 构建时间：2026-11-11T00:15:34Z（安装目录 resources/version.json 的 builtAt，其中 repoCommit 为 unknown）
- 安装方式：Windows x64 安装包

issue:1104.body:
### 1. Summary

On a **native Windows** deployment (host processes, no Docker/WSL), the Runner's managed scientific
environment never becomes usable. The micromamba provisioning run that builds `starter-python` fails
inside the **shared package cache**, and the failure is a path-length failure, not a download or a
disk failure:

* libmamba reports individual files inside extracted cache entries as `... is missing`;
* those files **are not missing** — they exist and are reachable through an extended-length (`\\?\`)
  path, and only unreachable through a normal Windows path;
* libmamba then declares the entry an invalid cache, tries to delete and re-extract it, and
  `remove_all: The directory is not empty.` fires because the delete step hits the same length limit;
* the entry is left with its `info\` directory gone, which is the condition under which conda
  considers a cache entry permanently unusable, and nothing in the Runner resets that shared cache.

Net effect: `scientificEnvs.available = false`, `shell.available = false`, and every `run_shell` call
returns `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE`. The instance cannot heal itself by restarting, and the damaged set grew
from 1 entry to 6 across two provisioning passes over the same cache.

### 2. Environment

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Windows 11, build 22631, x64 |
| Deployment | native Windows local stack (API, Runner, Evolve, Memory Graph as host processes) |
| Long-path policy | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem\LongPathsEnabled` = `0x0` (REG_DWORD, read with PowerShell `Get-ItemProperty`; not modified for this report) |
| Provisioner | micromamba pinned by this repo: `services/runner/src/micromamba-releases.json` -> `"version": "2.8.1-0"`, `win-64` binary, 11 311 104 bytes |
| Provisioner manifest | the binary contains the `longPathAware` manifest declaration (2 string hits), which is inert while the system policy is `0` |
| Runner self-report | `/health` -> `platform=win32`, `status=ok`, `runnerVersion=0f1ff6de` (build id of a downstream fork of `main`) |
| Node.js | v22.23.4, read from the executable the Runner process is actually running |
| Cache layout | `<DATA_DIR>` (58 characters on this machine) -> `<DATA_DIR>\scientific-envs\provisioner\pkgs` (91 characters) -> `<...>\pkgs\https\conda.anaconda.org\conda-forge\win-64` (**135 characters**) |

The command the Runner runs, as echoed back by its own failure payload (only the prefix path is
ours, the argv is the product's):

```
micromamba.exe --no-rc create --yes --strict-channel-priority --override-channels
  --prefix <DATA_DIR>\scientific-envs\revisions\starter-python\rev-<uuid>
  --channel conda-forge python=3.12 numpy=2.0 pandas=2.2 scipy=1.14
  matplotlib-base=3.9 m2-bash m2-coreutils m2-grep m2-sed
```

### 3. Observed Evidence

#### 3.1 Path-length census over the whole cache tree

Method: walk the cache with an extended-length root, then re-`stat` every file through its plain
path. Nothing was deleted, moved or rewritten.

| measure | result |
| --- | --- |
| files in the cache tree | 15 024 |
| files whose plain path length is greater than 260 | 103 |
| files whose plain path `stat()` fails | **125** |
| of the failures, files at exactly 260 characters | 22 |
| files at 259 characters or shorter that fail | **0** |
| longest plain path that still resolves | 259 |
| directories unreachable by plain `stat` | 0 |
| deepest file in the tree | 143-character relative tail (`matplotlib-base` entry), plain absolute path 278 characters |
| budget arithmetic | 135 (channel directory) + 143 (deepest tail) = 278; keeping every entry addressable needs the channel directory at or below **116** characters |

The two counts (103 and 125) differ by exactly the 22 files sitting at 260 characters, so the
effective ceiling is **259**: the documented 260 includes the terminating NUL. 125 is the damaged set;
103 is what a strict "longer than 260" filter reports, and both are quoted where they differ.

#### 3.2 The six files reported as "missing" exist

Each entry below is one file inside a cache entry, checked by extended-length path and by plain path.

| cache entry | file reported missing | plain path length | exists | reachable by plain path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fonttools-4.68.0-py312h05f76fc_0` | `varLib\__pycache__\interpolatableTestContourOrder.cpython-312.pyc` | 262 | yes | no |
| `libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001` | `Library\share\man\man3\hwloc_obj_attr_u_hwloc_numanode_attr_s_hwloc_memory_page_type_s.3` | 262 | yes | no |
| `matplotlib-base-3.9.4-py312h90004f6_0` | `backends\qt_editor\__pycache__\_formlayout.cpython-312.pyc` | 261 | yes | no |
| `numpy-2.0.2-py312h49bc9c5_1` | `_core\tests\__pycache__\test_casting_floatingpoint_errors.cpython-312.pyc` | 261 | yes | no |
| `pandas-2.2.3-py312h72972c8_3` | `core\array_algos\__pycache__\datetimelike_accumulations.cpython-312.pyc` | 261 | yes | no |
| `scipy-1.14.1-py312h337df96_2` | `optimize\_trustregion_constr\__pycache__\canonical_constraint.cpython-312.pyc` | 266 | yes | no |

So the correct statement is: **inaccessible through a normal Windows path, present on disk.** These
are not lost files and the archives themselves are intact (80 `.conda` archives still present,
55 under `win-64` and 25 under `noarch`; no partial-download markers anywhere).

Resulting cache state, 81 extracted entries (56 `win-64` + 25 `noarch`):

* exactly **6** entries now lack `info\` — the same six as the table above, all with the same
  directory mtime (14:41:58 of the same day);
* all 25 `noarch` entries still have `info\index.json`;
* entries that also contain over-long files but survived: `libpython` (5 files), `libwinpthread` (1),
  `m2-filesystem` (1), plus 260-character-only cases in `python` (3) and `m2-msys2-runtime` (1);
* `matplotlib-base` is the one gutted entry that also lost its `.conda` archive, which is why it is
  the entry the final `critical` line names.

#### 3.3 The messages, verbatim

First provisioning pass, one entry flagged (`<CACHE>` stands for the 135-character channel directory):

```
warning  libmamba Invalid package cache, file '<CACHE>\libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001\Library\share\man\man3\hwloc_obj_attr_u_hwloc_numanode_attr_s_hwloc_memory_page_type_s.3' is missing
error    libmamba Cannot find a valid extracted directory cache for 'libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001.conda'
critical libmamba Package cache error.
```

Second provisioning pass, same cache, now six entries flagged, each immediately followed by a failed
delete-and-re-extract:

```
warning  libmamba Invalid package cache, file '<CACHE>\<entry>\<over-long file>' is missing     (x6, alphabetical entry order)
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\matplotlib-base-3.9.4-py312h90004f6_0"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\pandas-2.2.3-py312h72972c8_3"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\numpy-2.0.2-py312h49bc9c5_1"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\scipy-1.14.1-py312h337df96_2"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\libhwloc-2.15.0-default_hae90fe0_1001"
error    libmamba Error when extracting package: remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\fonttools-4.68.0-py312h05f76fc_0"
critical libmamba remove_all: The directory is not empty.: "<CACHE>\matplotlib-base-3.9.4-py312h90004f6_0"
```

Two things follow from this transcript. The flagged set went from 1 entry to 6 over the *same* cache,
so which entry dies depends on scan order rather than on a fixed rule - the remaining deep-path
packages can be added on a later pass. And the earlier `Failed to load shard for package 'libgdal-*'
... will download` warnings are cold-cache noise: they are self-resolving, and extraction succeeded
after them.

#### 3.4 Runner state that results from it

* `/health` (Runner) and `/api/health` (API) both report `scientificEnvs` with `available=false`,
  `enabled=true`, `startersReady=false`, `provisioner=null`, `languages=[]`, and `unavailableReason`
  carrying the full transcript above; `revisions\` ends up holding no environment at all.
* In the captured run history we hold for one session, **11** `run_shell` tool results carry
  `{"code":"RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE","dispatched":false, ... }`.
* Capability probes return `shell.available=false` while the top-level `runner.status` still reads
  `ok` - the gap is only visible in the payload, never in the headline status.
* The bootstrap is fire-and-forget: a failed `setupManagedEnvironments()` logs one `WARN`
  (`server.ts:1300-1301`) and the service continues to report itself healthy.
* The user-visible cost is not an error dialog: each shell request parks for about 10 minutes in
  `wait_for_runner` and then hands the whole micromamba transcript to the agent as its "reason".

#### 3.5 Secondary: the failure is also hard to see in the logs

Not the cause, recorded because it cost us two rounds of diagnosis. `shortErrorMessage()`
(`packages/operational-logging/src/redaction.ts:40-42`) front-slices at 500 characters. The two
`runner.log` bootstrap-failure lines unescape to exactly 500 characters: 448 of them are the echoed
command line, leaving 52 characters of actual child-process stderr, so in `runner.log` the first
failing package name is simply absent. The untruncated copies exist only in `api.log`
(2 936 and 8 698 characters).

### 4. Controlled Experiment

#### 4.1 Reproduction recipe

1. Windows host, `LongPathsEnabled = 0`, native (non-Docker, non-WSL) stack.
2. Put the instance data directory at a realistic depth. The channel directory is the data directory
   plus 77 characters (`\scientific-envs\provisioner\pkgs\https\conda.anaconda.org\conda-forge\win-64`)
   and the deepest tail this package set creates is 143 characters, so a data directory of **40
   characters or more** is already enough to push an entry to 260 and out of reach (40 + 77 + 143 =
   260). Ours is 58.
3. Start the Runner so that it bootstraps `starter-python` with the default package set.
4. Observe: the messages in 3.3, `scientificEnvs.available=false`, and, in the cache tree, entries
   that have no `info\index.json` while still containing files whose plain path is 260 characters or
   longer.

#### 4.2 The comparison arm

Same micromamba binary, same `win-64` package set, same long target prefix (109 characters). The
only variable changed: the **package cache root** was pointed at a 10-character directory through the
mechanism `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` feeds (`CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` plus `--offline`). The long-path
registry policy stayed at `0` in both arms.

| measure | long cache root (production argv) | short cache root (arm B) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| exit code | `Command failed` (non-zero) | `0`, 29.6 s, 195 output lines |
| `Invalid package cache` lines | 6 | 0 |
| lines containing `remove_all: The directory is not empty` | 7 (6 `error` + 1 `critical`) | 0 |
| `warning` / `error` / `critical` lines | 6 / 6 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| network use | downloads required - three packages announced `will download`, and the cache's 56 package directories were written in one contiguous 38-second window | `Total download: 0 B`, `will download` 0 times |
| environment produced | none to measure - `revisions\` holds no directory, because each failed attempt removes its own revision | 16 847 files, all 81 packages of the spec linked, **0** files unreachable by plain `stat`, deepest path 220 characters |
| real computation through it | not possible | `rc=0`, 2 550 ms, empty stderr, python 3.12.16 + matplotlib 3.9.4 (Agg), PNG 6 165 bytes, CSV 272 bytes |

What this establishes: the packages, the solver and the disk are fine, and moving **only** the cache
to a short root makes the identical provisioning succeed. What it does not establish is listed in
section 10.

### 5. Expected Behavior

1. Before provisioning, the Runner should know its path budget. The cache root is derived as
   `<dataDir>\scientific-envs\provisioner\pkgs`; the channel subdirectory is already 135 characters
   on this machine, and the deepest entry path this package set creates is 143 characters, so the
   channel directory has to stay at or under 116 characters for the entries to remain addressable. A
   length pre-flight (root length plus the expected tail) would catch this before micromamba runs.
2. If the budget cannot be met, fail fast with an explicit compatibility diagnostic that prints the
   offending root, its length, the platform's long-path state and the supported remedy - instead of
   letting a package manager report individual files as missing.
3. The cache location should be short and stable by default on Windows (a machine-level short root,
   or `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` honoured by default rather than only when explicitly set),
   rather than inheriting an arbitrarily deep per-instance data directory.
4. Cache validation and cache removal should use the same long-path-aware access that the rest of a
   Windows deployment needs (`\\?\` / `path.toNamespacedPath`, the pattern already used in
   `packages/cas`), so that a file libmamba just wrote cannot become invisible to libmamba one step
   later.
5. A path-length condition must not be reported as "file is missing" or as a generic
   `Package cache error`. As written, the message tells the operator that the package cache is
   corrupt, which invites exactly the wrong remedy (wipe the cache and re-download, which reproduces
   the same state).
6. After an entry is invalidated in the shared cache, the Runner should be able to recover it, or
   stop using it. Today the failure path removes only the per-attempt
   `revisions/<env>` directory (`environment-store.ts:924`) and never the shared entries, and the next
   start repeats the identical `create` against that cache, so every bootstrap re-reads the same
   poisoned entries.

### 6. Actual Behavior

* Provisioning fails, first with `Invalid package cache ... is missing` and
  `Cannot find a valid extracted directory cache`, then with `remove_all: The directory is not empty`
  and `critical libmamba ...`, and the shared cache ends up with 6 unusable entries.
* The state is stable across restarts: the entries keep their gutted form, `revisions\` stays empty,
  and a second pass flags more entries than the first.
* `scientificEnvs.available=false`, `startersReady=false`, `shell.available=false`;
  `run_shell` returns `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` with `dispatched=false`, so no shell or Python step can
  execute for the whole instance.
* `runner.status` still says `ok`, and the only log line about it is one `WARN` whose message is
  truncated to 500 characters, so neither the UI nor `runner.log` states that the scientific
  environment is dead.
* The guidance the failure itself returns points at a remedy that cannot work against this cause:
  `Recreate or update the starter environment on the target Runner to repair managed Bash and its
  required utilities.` Re-creating the environment re-reads the same poisoned shared cache; that is
  exactly what happened here, where a later pass flagged five more entries than the first one did.

### 7. Questions for Maintainers

1. Is native Windows (host processes, no Docker/WSL) a supported runtime mode for the Runner? The
   install and quick-start documentation is what we followed; nothing in it states a path-length
   requirement for the data directory.
2. If it is not supported, should the launcher detect the platform and refuse with a clear message
   at startup, instead of booting and reporting `status=ok` while `shell.available=false`?
3. If it is supported, which fix do you prefer: (a) a short machine-level default cache root, or
   honouring `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` by default on Windows; (b) long-path-aware validation
   and removal of cache entries; (c) a pre-flight length check plus an explicit compatibility
   diagnostic; or a combination?
4. Could CI gain a provisioning regression test whose cache entries sit at **259, 260 and 261+**
   characters, covering create, extract, and the cleanup/`remove_all` path? The 259/260 boundary is
   where our damaged set changes character, and it is the case a "just below MAX_PATH" test misses.
5. `services/runner/src/platform/win32.ts:117-128` already substitutes `matplotlib-base` for
   `matplotlib` precisely because the qt6 tree exceeds MAX_PATH. Our data says that substitution is
   necessary but not sufficient: `matplotlib-base-3.9.4` is itself one of the six gutted entries,
   because its own `Lib\site-packages\...\__pycache__` test artefacts reach 260+ characters. Should
   the starter set be screened by measured depth rather than by known-bad package names?
6. Should an entry invalidated in the shared cache be reset automatically (with an audit record),
   given that the instance cannot recover by restarting?

### 8. Scope

This report is about **Windows native Runner environment provisioning** and its package cache.
Deliberately excluded, each with its own report: agent output truncation, MCP connector bookkeeping,
Memory Graph behaviour, and usage accounting. The 500-character log slicing in 3.5 is mentioned only
because it hides this particular error, not as a logging proposal.

### 9. Source-code references (checked against the current `main`)

* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:389` - `MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX: resolve(config.root,
  "provisioner")`, which is what ties the cache to the per-instance data directory.
* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:390` - `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` is exported only when
  `config.packageCacheDir` is set; `:1104-1105` - `--offline` likewise.
* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:540` - the only pre-flight on the cache directory is an
  existence check (`await access(...)`); there is no length check, and no `MAX_PATH`, `\\?\` or
  `toNamespacedPath` token appears anywhere in this file.
* `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:906` and `:924` - `bootstrapStarter()` create arguments,
  and the failure path that removes only `revisions/<id>`.
* `services/runner/src/server.ts:397-398` - `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` is the sole override.
* `services/runner/src/server.ts:1300-1301` - `void setupManagedEnvironments().catch(...)`, one
  `WARN` on failure.
* `services/runner/src/platform/win32.ts:117-128` and `services/runner/src/platform/types.ts:80-86` -
  the existing MAX_PATH note for this starter package set.
* `services/runner/src/micromamba-releases.json:2` - the pinned provisioner version.
* `packages/operational-logging/src/redaction.ts:16` and `:40-42` - the 500-character front-slice.

### 10. What this report does not establish

* **Mechanism granularity.** That micromamba validates and deletes cache entries through
  non-extended-length paths is inferred from the message text plus the resulting on-disk state (which
  files remain, which disappear, in what order), not from libmamba's source, which is a binary here.
  The observable facts in 3 are independent of that inference.
* **`LongPathsEnabled = 1` was not tested.** Changing the registry was outside the authorised scope,
  so we cannot claim that enabling the policy would fix it; the `longPathAware` declaration in the
  binary is inert while the policy is off, and we did not verify per-call behaviour with the policy
  on.
* **Concurrency is excluded as the cause of the damage in our instance**, but for a narrower reason
  than "locks exist": downloads and extraction all fall inside one runner generation's window
  (monotone, 09:00:07-09:00:45), the previous generation had only fetched repodata,
  `enqueueMutation()` serialises mutations in-process, no second `scientific-envs` tree exists on
  this machine, and `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` was unset so no cache is shared between
  instances. There is **no cross-process lock** around the package cache; two Runners configured with
  the same cache root could race. We report that as a structural risk, not as part of this failure.
* **The comparison arm in 4.2 bypassed the service.** It ran micromamba directly with the equivalent
  argv; configuring `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` in the launcher and restarting was not
  authorised. `Total download: 0 B` also does not prove the offline seed fully served the solve, and
  `--offline` pins the package set to what was seeded, so packages beyond this spec would need the
  seed to cover them too.
* **Sample size.** Two provisioning passes in one instance, one session's run history, and the six
  entries named above. We did not survey other Windows hosts.
* **The earlier Docker observation is a user-provided history, not evidence.** Running the same
  product under Docker worked, as reported by the operator, but we have not run a same-SHA,
  same-configuration controlled comparison, so we explicitly do **not** present "Docker works" as a
  proven cause-or-cure for anything in this report.

### 11. Related items and prior search

Searched the tracker before filing, over open and closed issues, for `MAX_PATH`, `micromamba`,
`LongPathsEnabled`, `Package cache error`, `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS`, `remove_all`, `longPathAware`,
`Windows provisioning` and `scientific environment bootstrap`. No existing item covers this defect;
`LongPathsEnabled`, `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS`, `remove_all` and `longPathAware` each return zero results. The
nearest items, all distinct from this one:

* #643 - Windows runtime: native startup chain, execution routing, micromamba environments (closed) -
  the feature this report is about.
* #916 - Windows managed Shell missing base Unix tools and a diagnosable capability declaration
  (closed) - adjacent, different defect: tools absent in a *successfully created* environment.
* #583 - CAS: Windows durable-directory sync with `toNamespacedPath` (closed) - precedent that the
  long-path namespace treatment is already applied elsewhere in this project.

### 12. References

* Installation (docs site we followed): https://sciencediscovery.github.io/zh/install/index.html
* Quick start: https://sciencediscovery.github.io/zh/docs/getting-started/quick-start.html
* Mamba troubleshooting, which documents the same class of Windows path problem:
  https://mamba.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/troubleshooting.html
* Windows path limits (the 260 value that includes the terminating NUL, and the `\\?\` prefix):
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file

## 1. Actual behaviour

An Agent calls `check_runner` and gets a green light. Nine seconds later it calls `run_shell` and is refused. Both answers describe the same Runner instance, and their embedded Runner capability blocks are **equal in every field except `checkedAt`**.

So there are two distinct problems in the same contract.

**(a) The diagnostic verdict is route-blind.** `checkRunner` narrows its verdict to the managed Shell only when its 4th argument `requiresShell` is passed (`services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts:193-196`), and the tool-facing binding never passes it:

```
:415   runnerReadiness: {
:416     check: (machine, signal) => checkRunner(machine, signal),
```

so the answer an Agent receives from `check_runner` is *always* the Python-channel answer (`requiresShell = false`, `:180`), whatever the Agent intended. The same function is called with `true` from the Shell execution route (`:278`) and re-passes the blocked operation's own `requiresShell` in `wait_for_runner` (`:431`, `:446-447`). `ready` therefore has two meanings selected by a parameter the tool cannot set and the Agent is not told about. The tool's own description says it "Reports the platform, Shell, guaranteed utilities, sandbox diagnostics and repair suggestions" (`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:1642` at B, `:1637` at A) — but the headline field it publishes ignores the Shell probe it also publishes.

**(b) The Runner-level verdict inside the payload is a constant.** The `sandbox === "none"` branch of the probe hard-codes the answer (`services/runner/src/readiness.ts:43-45`): `ready: true, reason: "ready"`, with the failure text parked next to it in `detail`. That is why the refused call's own payload carries `ready: false` at the top and `capability.ready: true, capability.reason: "ready"` inside — one object, two verdicts, and the nested one is the Runner's official answer. Consumers that read `capability` (the `/health`-style surface, the UI) get `"ready"`; consumers that read the top-level get the truth, and which one they get depends on which code path built the object.

**(c) A closed vocabulary cannot express the state.** `RunnerExecutionCapability.reason` is typed `"ready" | "dependency-unavailable" | "incompatible" | "sandbox-unusable"` (`packages/schema/src/environment.ts:520`). There is no value for "the shell route is dead", so `"ready"` is the only permitted answer even when the probe's own sub-capability says no.

Measured across the whole capture: an object with the `RunnerCheckResult` key set occurs **194** times in the 62 stream files of this session (occurrences, not calls — see section 4 for how one call multiplies). In **194 of 194** the embedded verdict is `capability.ready: true` with `capability.reason: "ready"` (the reason text survived field bounding in 177 of them) and `capability.shell.available: false` with `shell.utilities: []`. The headline `ready` splits **76 true / 118 false** over that identical nested verdict. Zero occurrences anywhere in the capture report `shell.available: true`. So this is not an intermittent race: the Shell was unavailable throughout, the Runner probe said `"ready"` throughout, and the only thing that varied was which code path asked.

Two consequences worth separating from the diagnosis:

- A Runner that starts with a provably dead managed Shell logs nothing. `services/runner/src/server.ts:1189-1190` warns `execution_unavailable` only `if (!capability.ready)`, and `capability.ready` is the literal `true` from `readiness.ts:43` on this branch. The operator's startup log was silent for the entire 10-hour capture while the Shell was unprovisionable.
- The Agent that chooses to wait can end with no answer at all. In this capture `wait_for_runner` (`call_29c5a855…`, run `0673152f`) returned `action: "cancel"`, and the cancel branch (`workspace-bindings.ts:444-445`) returns `{action, operationId, dispatched: false, instruction}` with **no** `runner` object — so the next readiness question goes back through `check_runner` and returns `ready: true` again.

## 2. Expected behaviour

The decoupling is deliberate and we are not asking for it to be undone: PR #716's stated design is that "A missing managed shell must not block Python execution" (`services/runner/src/readiness.ts:35-37`), and that is right. What is missing is a route-scoped answer on the *diagnostic* surface, so that "is this Runner able to run my Shell command?" is answerable from the check instead of only from the refusal. Any one of the following closes it; they are alternatives, not a list to implement in full.

1. Give the tool the route it is asked about: accept `requires_shell` (or `route: "python" | "shell" | "any"`) in `check_runner`'s parameter schema and pass it to `checkRunner`. Default behaviour unchanged; the Agent's question finally determines the answer's scope.
2. Or make the verdict structural instead of caller-selected: publish route-scoped fields derived from what is already probed (for example `readyFor: { python: <ready>, shell: <ready && shell?.available !== false > }`) so every consumer reads one object and branches, and the two verdicts cannot disagree.
3. Or, minimal: never emit `reason: "ready"` when a probed sub-capability answered no. `capability.shell.available === false` should set `reason` to a new value (for example `"shell-unavailable"`) while the coarse `ready` keeps whatever meaning the Python channel needs; the union at `packages/schema/src/environment.ts:520` gains that value. This is the precedent the project already set for `sandboxNetwork` (section 6, #461/#463), whose sub-capability reports `available: false` with an `unavailableReason`.
4. Or, if the current payload is judged complete: say so where a caller reads it. `check_runner`'s description and the `RunnerExecutionCapability` doc comment should state that `ready` deliberately ignores `shell.available`, and the second suggestion should stop telling the Agent to "use check_runner" to recheck a blocker the check cannot report (`services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts:206`).

Whichever shape is chosen, `capability.ready`/`capability.reason` should be derived on the `sandbox === "none"` branch the way they are derived on the sandboxed branch (`readiness.ts:78-79` derives `ready` from the probe result rather than fixing it), so that the nested verdict is not a constant, and a positive test should assert that a payload reporting `shell.available: false` does not report `reason: "ready"`.

## 5. Trigger conditions

- A Runner whose sandbox kind resolves to `"none"` **on Windows** — the default for `SCIENCE_AGENT_SANDBOX_PROVIDER=auto` on that platform (`services/runner/src/server.ts:353-359`), which is also the only condition under which the shell probe is wired at all (`:1187`). On Linux/macOS with `bubblewrap`/`seatbelt`, `ready` is derived from `sandboxUsable` (`services/runner/src/readiness.ts:78-79`), so disagreement (a) cannot arise there — though the sandboxed branch is the one that already derives its verdict from a probe, which is what section 2 item 4 asks the `none` branch to do.
- The managed starter environment must be unprovisionable at check time (here `micromamba create` failing on a corrupt package cache), so `shellCapability()` answers `available: false` with a reason (`services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:445-446` / `:463-464`). Any Shell-probe failure should do: the probe is a file/executability check plus the environment store's own creation state, and it runs no user code.
- The Agent must ask. Because `runnerReadiness.check` drops the argument (`workspace-bindings.ts:416`), `check_runner` answers the Python question whatever the Agent meant; the disagreement surfaces as soon as the Agent then takes the Shell route.
- Not required: wall-clock timeouts, model behaviour, sandbox permissions, remote Runners, the specific package-cache error. An older Runner that reports no `shell` field at all shows no contradiction — by design (`:191-192`), which is also why a fix must keep treating an absent field as unknown rather than as unavailable.
- Deterministic reproduction: run the Runner on Windows against a data directory whose starter-env revision cannot be created (or otherwise force `shellCapability()` to answer `available: false`); from one Agent, call `check_runner` and then any Shell tool, and compare `ready`/`reason` in the two results against the `capability` blocks, which will match except for `checkedAt`. A unit-level version needs a test that goes through the workspace tool registry rather than calling `checkRunner` directly, because the binding's default is the thing under test.
