Fixes #777

Owner: Dev2
Written-by: Dev-2
Tip SHA: 0bb3ee16884843a09d30278a63db007ba3f4da5d
Base: a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c (main at push; branch rebased onto it, no overlap)

`web_fetch`/`web_search` handed search-result titles and snippets to the model with named HTML references still encoded. Only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp` decoded, so a page title like `Café — a review` reached the prompt and the report verbatim, and the sources a science search cites most often (encyclopedias, European sites) are exactly the entity-heavy ones. This decodes every named reference a browser resolves, in the same single pass as before.

## What changed

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts`: the five-name map is replaced by the full WHATWG named character reference set — 2125 semicolon-terminated names — expanded into a `Map` once at module load. `nbsp` keeps its existing ordinary-space mapping; numeric references, the single-pass rule (`&lt;` → `<`) and unknown names (`&bogus;` stays literal) are unchanged. The decoding loop is the same one-scan replace it was; only the data changed shape and moved out of this module.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html-entities.ts` (new): the table itself — a `name;code point;…` constant, 246 folded lines — under a 37-line header that states the source (WHATWG named character references via CPython's `html.entities.html5`, 2231 keys of which the 2125 semicolon forms are what this pattern accepts), the retrieval date, the exact `python3` snippet that regenerates the body, and the licence position: the standard's table reproduced as factual data — names and code points any HTML parser needs — not copied from another project's source. `html.ts` keeps the decoder and goes from 79 lines to 90 (+11); 368 is only the shape this branch's previous commit had with the table inline, and this commit moves it out. The data is 246 of the new file's 284 lines.
- `tsconfig.base.json`: one line, `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`. The import in `html.ts` keeps a `.ts` extension so `node --experimental-strip-types` — the command the issue reproduces with — resolves the sibling source instead of failing with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; that option is what lets tsc accept the specifier and still emit `./html-entities.js` (verified: the built `dist/web/native/html.js` line is `import { NAMED_ENTITIES_PACKED } from "./html-entities.js";`). It belongs in the base config rather than the package one: the root tests config used by `pnpm typecheck` extends only `tsconfig.base.json`, and with the option in `packages/data-source/tsconfig.json` alone that check fails with `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts(73,39): error TS5097: An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when 'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled.` From the base config both the package build and that check pass. It changes nothing else in the tree — the only `test/` file that `tsc` type-checks imports `.js` paths; the Playwright specs under `test/` are not in any tsconfig.
- `html-entities.ts` is force-added: `.gitignore`'s `data-*/` rule also matches the `packages/data-source/` directory (`git check-ignore -v` reports `.gitignore:91`). I left that rule alone to keep this PR single-purpose; say the word if you would rather have it anchored as `/data-*/` and I will open a separate issue.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts`: cases for the names in the issue (`eacute`, `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `apos`, `diams`, `rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, Latin-1, symbols), case sensitivity, an unknown name, the single-pass rule after the table widened, and a guard that the exported table still has exactly 2125 entries plus one two-scalar value (`NotEqualTilde`), so a dropped or mis-chunked line cannot pass as a smaller table. The test file is unchanged by the move.

Size, whole PR: 4 files, 344 insertions, 8 deletions (`html-entities.ts` +284, `html.test.ts` +41/−1, `html.ts` +18/−7, `tsconfig.base.json` +1).

## Red first

Decoder tests. Command:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/html.test.ts
```

Before the fix:

```
# Subtest: decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
not ok 3 - decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
  expected: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
  actual: 'café — 5–10 … O'Brien'
# Subtest: decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
not ok 4 - decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
  expected: 'Ää'
  actual: 'Ää'
# pass 5
# fail 2
```

Table guard. The guard lands in its own commit before the export exists, so it is red on the change that adds only the test:

```
# pass 0
# fail 1
SyntaxError: The requested module './html.js' does not provide an export named 'NAMED_ENTITIES'
```

and it fails the way it is meant to when one entry is dropped from the packed constant (mutation check, one `AElig;c6;` field removed, then restored):

```
not ok 8 - keeps every entry of the generated WHATWG table
  expected: 2125
  actual: 2124
# pass 7
# fail 1
```

Green after the implementation, same command as the decoder run: `# pass 8`, `# fail 0`. The package suite goes from 74 to 75 tests with the guard: `# tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0`.

## The issue's reproduction

Command from #777:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

On this tip:

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

The middle line is the single-pass guarantee: the decoded ampersand does not start a second scan.

## Gates

On this tip, in `packages/data-source` unless noted:

```
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json                                        # exit 0 (build)
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit                               # exit 0
$ node --experimental-strip-types -e 'import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(...)'
  café — 5–10 … O'Brien                                          # exit 0
$ npm test                                                        # # tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0
$ cd ../.. && node scripts/check-architecture.mjs                 # 333 source files, boundaries OK
$ cd ../.. && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json        # exit 0
$ cd ../.. && pnpm --recursive typecheck                          # 34 packages Done, exit 0
```

`pnpm architecture:check` is **98 passed / 1 failed** on this host: `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` shells out to `.ci/run-research-python.sh race`, which needs a writable uv Python install and network (`Read-only file system` at `~/.local/share/uv/python`); it does not touch `packages/data-source`. `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` itself is green, as shown above.

## Not run

- Repo-level UT/ST/E2E, CodeCheck (GitCode) and the Docker/binary layers: CI. This PR changes one package's text extractor and its test, plus one compiler option; the package tests, both tsc configurations, the architecture check and the recursive typecheck were run locally.

pr:922.body:
Fixes #665

`web_fetch`'s public-URL guard lets several IPv6 families through even though each one carries an IPv4 address the guard already knows how to judge. A model-supplied URL such as `http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/` or `http://[2002:a9fe:a9fe::]/` reaches loopback or the link-local metadata endpoint, while the equivalent `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is rejected. This closes those holes, pins that public addresses in the same forms keep working, and — after review — refuses the non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix rather than guessing where their IPv4 address sits.

## What was wrong

`ipv6Blocked()` consulted `ipv4Blocked()` only for IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`) forms, where the embedded IPv4 address sits in the last two hextets. Other families carry the same address elsewhere:

| family | prefix | where the IPv4 address sits | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NAT64 well-known | `64:ff9b::/96` | last 32 bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| NAT64 local-use | `64:ff9b:1::/48` | last 32 bits **only for the canonical `/96` sub-layout** | canonical `/96` decoded; every other suffix under the `/48` rejected |
| 6to4 | `2002::/16` | hextets 2–3 | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| IPv4-translated | `::ffff:0:0:0/96` | last 32 bits, after `ffff` and 16 zero bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| Teredo | `2001:0::/32` | last 32 bits, bitwise inverted | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| site-local (deprecated) | `fec0::/10` | no IPv4 — the range itself is non-public | reject |

No branch inspected those positions, so each form fell through to `return false`.

The local-use row is the review fix. `64:ff9b:1::/48` is wider than the `/96` an embedded address needs, and RFC 8215 allows deployments to use other suffix lengths — a deployment that puts the IPv4 address in bits 64–95 is not judged by hextets 6–7. Reading hextets 6–7 of *every* address in the `/48` therefore judged the wrong bits: `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` was interpreted as the public `128.8.8.8`.

## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts`: one helper, `dotted(high, low)`, and `ipv6Blocked()` extracts the embedded address for the rows above and hands it to the existing `ipv4Blocked()`. There is no second copy of the IPv4 block list, no blanket range ban, and no refactor of the existing mapped/compatible branches.

For the local-use prefix the rule is now explicit and fail-closed: decode the canonical `64:ff9b:1:0:0:0::/96` sub-layout, and **return blocked for every non-canonical suffix** under `64:ff9b:1::/48` (`return true`, never `return false` — an unknown suffix must not become the way around the guard). The well-known `64:ff9b::/96` prefix is untouched by that rule.

## Red first

The new test (`providers.test.ts`), run against the unfixed `url-guard.ts`:

```
not ok 11 - web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
  error: |-
    64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808

    false !== true

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  expected: true
  actual: false
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The assertion loop stops at its first failing literal, so every blocked literal was also probed one by one against the unfixed predicate, and every public one against the fixed predicate. Values are `blocked` / `allowed` from `isBlockedAddress`; the flipped rows are the review fix, all in the tightening direction:

| address | before `e9e7358c` review fix | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `64:ff9b::7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b::808:808` | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1::7f00:1` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::a9fe:a9fe` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::808:808` (canonical `/96`) | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:1:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:0:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:dead:beef:cafe:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:a9fe:a9fe` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |

Five flips in this probed set, all `allowed → blocked`; zero `blocked → allowed`.

## Only tighter

The same probe run before and after the review fix differs in exactly one line — the tightened address. Everything a legitimate client may reach still resolves as public:

```
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b::808:808            (NAT64 well-known, public)
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b:1::808:808          (NAT64 local-use canonical /96, public)
ALLOW  literal 2002:808:808::              (6to4 for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal ::ffff:0:808:808            (IPv4-translated for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2001:0:808:808::f7f7:f7f7   (Teredo for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2606:4700:4700::1111        (native IPv6)
ALLOW  resolver 64:ff9b::808:808 for http://example.com/
ALLOW  resolver 2606:4700:4700::1111 for http://example.com/
```

These are asserted in the test too (`assert.equal(isBlockedAddress(...), false)` and `assert.equal(await assertPublicUrl(...), url)`), so the guard cannot be "fixed" by blocking a prefix.

## After the fix

```
# tests 16
# pass 16
# fail 0
```

The test now has 17 blocked addresses and 6 public ones (23 assertions across the literal and resolver paths), including the canonical `/96` cases in both directions and the non-canonical suffixes.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts | 71 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts      | 35 +++++++++++-
 2 files changed, 106 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

This branch is `f4dd1813` + four commits, two files, nothing else:

1. `dd29d921` test: pin NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local fetch targets
2. `eb818998` fix: judge NAT64, 6to4 and IPv4-translated literals by their embedded IPv4
3. `e4bb3e67` test: judge the local-use NAT64 prefix by its canonical /96 only
4. `e9e7358c` fix: decode only the canonical /96 under the local-use NAT64 prefix

It does not contain any commit from #915; the three-file view was the reviewer's worktree.

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` in `packages/data-source` — `# tests 16 # pass 16 # fail 0`; the same command on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 15 # fail 1`).
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Per-address probe of the 17 blocked and 6 public literals before and after the review fix — the before/after table and the only-tighter block above.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` (full layers) were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser/API/CLI journey was added: the change is a predicate inside the `web_fetch` URL guard, and the mocked E2E subset does not exercise NAT64/6to4 literals.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a model-supplied `web_fetch` URL that encodes a private, loopback or link-local IPv4 address in NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated, Teredo or site-local form is rejected with `PublicUrlError` instead of being fetched; public addresses in the same forms keep working, and non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix are rejected rather than guessed at.

Compatibility and migration: none. A deployment that puts the NAT64 IPv4 address in bits 64–95 of `64:ff9b:1::/48` is now rejected instead of silently misjudged; the canonical `/96` layout and `64:ff9b::/96` behave exactly as before.

## Summary

Part of #835.

This is the independent tool-output trust-boundary slice from the staged landing plan. It introduces category-driven fencing for model-visible untrusted content while preserving raw stored evidence and observer behavior. It does not register Knowledge Engine tools or change kbScope, research state, finish-gate, or agent memory.

### Included

- Per-registry nonces and explicit `untrustedCategory` classification, with legacy-name and MCP-remote fallback behavior.
- Fencing for tool-domain, MCP, remote, and error payloads; only genuine framework-control messages bypass the boundary.
- Durable output sidecars preserving trust and neutralization metadata through line, character, and search readbacks. New records carry an explicit trust format version; pre-metadata records fail closed as untrusted legacy content, while authenticated fence metadata prevents planted fence-shaped tool text from changing durable status or evidence.
- Connector-controlled tool-search results are fenced and neutralized. Model-facing tool descriptions and schema `description`/`title`/`$comment` metadata receive the same protection without changing property identifiers, enum values, or the execution-time schema.
- A shared TypeScript/adapter/durable-store nonce, with native web and subagent history fenced at the actual model-request and dynamic-context rehydration boundaries. Existing fences are unwrapped during hydration only at a legacy anchored position or when framework metadata authenticates the category and nonce; missing trust wiring fails closed.
- Tool identity resolution through assistant `tool_call_id` mappings, including OpenAI tool messages without `name`; platform output is not double-fenced.
- Equivalent native-history handling for JiuwenSwarm housekeeping/default compression requests. Housekeeping selects a provider only when platform-call history proves one unique active run through its `_sd_run`; concurrent runs stay isolated, and finished, foreign, or ambiguous history fails closed instead of borrowing another run's model, credentials, or nonce.
- Framework truncation/readback/failure guidance kept outside untrusted fences, including explicit post-fence overflow notices and durable readback references.
- Final model-message fitting that enforces byte/line limits, truncates only the untrusted body, preserves complete markers, and fails closed when the trust envelope cannot fit.
- Authority-tag neutralization for remote-origin and subagent content, including custom categories and durable `runtime_context_data` wrappers; generic corpus content remains byte-exact except forged fence markers.
- Protected fence semantics and concise answer discipline in prompt `m8.5.1`.

closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**This is a behavior-change request, not a regression.** The current behavior is deliberate and pinned by unit tests (listed below). What is asked here is that one unusable model answer should be retried, trimmed or degraded, instead of ending a research run that has already spent tokens of a paid model.

Every model stage in the Idea Tree engine gets exactly **one** correction — `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:280`:

```python
for attempt in range(2):
```

Two failure paths do not even use that one correction, or use it and then give up:

**1. Empty or truncated output — no correction at all.** `research.py:311-312`, raised before the correction branch at `:318-320` is reachable:

```python
if raw is None or isinstance(raw, str) and not raw.strip():
    raise ValueError(f'{role}: empty or truncated model output; stage cannot continue')
```

**2. A proposal deeper than `maxDepth` — one correction, then give up.** `research.py:494-495` (inside `proposal_path()`):

```python
if parent['depth'] + len(path) + 1 > depth:
    raise ValueError('Proposal exceeds maxDepth')
```

That raises from `validate_proposal()` (`:506-510`), which the ideate stage passes as its check hook through `check_proposals` (`:553-559`). The second failure is re-raised at `:318-320`:

```python
if attempt:
    raise ValueError(f'{role}: invalid model result after one correction: {error}') from error
```

`ask()` (`:256-271`) does not retry; it only marks the activity `failed` and re-raises. Both paths therefore land in `run()`'s catch-all (`:627-631`):

```python
except Exception as error:
    if self.stop_action:
        ...
    else:
        s.update(status='interrupted', reason=str(error))
```

No third attempt, no trimming of the offending path, no fallback that keeps the completed stages and the remaining budget.

#### Where `maxDepth` comes from

- Engine default **5**, range 1–20: `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research_service.py:27` — `maxDepth: int = Field(default=5, ge=1, le=20)`.
- Runtime-settings default **5**: `packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts:342` (`DEFAULT_IDEA_TREE_SETTINGS`). The `IdeaTreeSettingsOverride` interface ends at `:336`; a Session that does not set `maxDepth` inherits the global value.
- The `standard` intensity does **not** change it: `templates.py:36-40` lists only `maxRounds`, `candidatesPerRound`, `maxSearchRounds`, `maxActiveDirections`, `explorationSlots`, `candidateConcurrency` for each intensity, and `apply_intensity()` (`:49-52`) merges exactly those keys.

So a Session that only picks a template and `standard` runs with `maxDepth = 5`.

#### Observed occurrences (real runs, not synthesized)

| When | Product tree / test head | Stage | Recorded `research.reason` | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-08T01:47:40Z (last write 01:51:57Z) | desktop session, no test head | ideate | `ideate: invalid model result after one correction: Proposal exceeds maxDepth` | ~4 min, 142,584 tokens, round 1 |
| 2026-11-23T04:13:00Z | main `591e9f47`, L5 test head `602ff6e7` | ideate | `ideate: invalid model result after one correction: Proposal exceeds maxDepth` | 985.3 s for the journey step (16.2 m case) |
| 2026-11-23T02:31:39Z | main at the time, L5 test head `d296180a` | design | `design: empty or truncated model output; stage cannot continue` | 1581.7 s (26.0 m case) |

The first row is the only one whose stored research record survived: `round=1`, 4 nodes, **maximum node depth 1**, `tokens=142584`, `settings` with `maxDepth=5`, `explorationIntensity=standard`, `maxRounds=3`, `candidatesPerRound=3`. The two journey rows had their project deleted by the test cleanup, so their round and node counts cannot be recovered; the reason strings above are quoted from the journey reports verbatim.

#### Why raising `maxDepth` is not the fix

In the one recoverable record the tree was 4 nodes deep at most and still on round 1 — the proposal overflowed the budget because it carried a long `direction` + `refinements` chain inside a single answer, not because the tree had actually grown to depth 5. Raising `maxDepth` only moves the cliff; the run is still lost when the model overshoots it, and an empty answer has nothing to do with depth at all.

#### What is requested

The run should survive a single bad answer. Which of these to take is a product decision — this issue only lists the options and does not prescribe a fix:

1. Retry an empty/truncated stage answer the same way other model failures are retried (bounded, and inside the existing token budget), instead of raising on the first one.
2. Give the depth/validation rejection more than one correction round, so the model can actually shorten the proposal.
3. Trim or clamp the offending `direction` + `refinements` chain to the remaining depth instead of rejecting the whole proposal.
4. If the answer stays unusable, settle the research as a degraded result (keep completed stages and the tree so far, with a clear reason) rather than `interrupted`.

#### Minimal reproduction

`research.py:311-312` is not a theoretical path — row 3 above is it happening in a real run. The smallest deterministic way to pin it in a unit test is the same shape the existing tests already use (`services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py`, a transport that answers with a scripted sequence):

1. Build the engine with `Settings(maxDepth=5, explorationIntensity='standard')`.
2. Make the transport return `''` for the first stage call and a valid answer for the next one.
3. Run the research: it settles `interrupted` with `empty or truncated model output` after a single model call, although a second call would have succeeded.

For the depth path, make the ideate transport return a candidate whose `direction` + `refinements` exceed the remaining depth on both the first and the corrected call.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Affected component: Idea Tree research engine in the Python Evolve sidecar — `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/` (`research.py`, `research_service.py`, `templates.py`). Nothing outside `services/evolve` is involved.
- Repository / product version examined: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` main at `591e9f477d0b74e708fc61a90d3908aedcd593f3` (`fix(permissions): localize the timeline card and keep JiuwenSwarm call detail`); desktop shell `0.4.0-rc1`.
- The two L5 journey runs above were driven by `test/journey-idea-tree-l5.spec.ts` from PR #1297 (`602ff6e7`, `d296180a` — test-only heads; the product tree was a `refs/heads/main` tarball, which carries no `.git`, so the SHA field inside those journey reports shows a stale value).
- OS: Windows 11 host, WSL2 Ubuntu, `linux-amd64`; API at `127.0.0.1:4310`, backend `legacy` (`start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`).
- Model: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`/v1/chat/completions`), one worker, real credentials.
- Settings for the failing L5 case: template `water-treatment-materials/v1`, `explorationIntensity=standard`, `maxDepth` not overridden (so 5), `maxTokens` not set.
- Settings for the 2026-11-08 record: template `scientific-hypothesis-general/v1`, `standard`, `maxDepth=5`, `maxRounds=3`, `candidatesPerRound=3` (that record also still carries the retired `maxTokensPerCall` field, removed since #1281).

### Additional Information

- **Precedent already accepted for the same class of problem:** #1232 / #1236 — a transient HTTP 429 used to `interrupt` the research and was changed to bounded retry with backoff, keeping completed stages alive. The paths in this issue are content-level rather than transport-level, but the principle ("one bad model answer should not destroy the run") is the same.
- **Current behavior is pinned by tests** (change these together with the behavior, not instead of it):
  - `services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py:347-355` `test_invalid_response_corrected_once_without_partial_tree` — an invalid answer is asked exactly twice and then `status == 'interrupted'`.
  - `:357-363` `test_invalid_parent_does_not_save_partial_batch` — an illegal parent ends the research and leaves no half tree.
  - `:365-381` `test_a_parent_outside_the_selection_gets_one_correction` — when the correction works, the research is **not** interrupted.
  - `:383-398` — a `propagate` exception interrupts the research.
- **No test asserts the over-depth path.** Searching `services/evolve/tests` for `Proposal exceeds maxDepth` gives zero hits. The tests that do set `maxDepth=1` (`:236`, `:472`) propose with `parentId: "ROOT"` and no `direction`, so `path` is empty and the depth check is never reached; `:452` does not go through ideation at all. The over-depth rejection is therefore only covered indirectly, through the generic "invalid result" test.
- **Frequency:** two recorded occurrences of the depth path (2026-11-08 and 2026-11-23) plus one of the empty-output path — with a sample this small no rate can be quoted, and both paths are rare but reproducible.
- No duplicate was found: searching the repository for `maxDepth`, `Proposal exceeds maxDepth` and `"empty or truncated model output"` returns only PR #1297 (the test that surfaced it) and unrelated issues.

### Version Information

- Product under test: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` main `591e9f477d0b74e708fc61a90d3908aedcd593f3`; desktop shell `0.4.0-rc1`; `services/evolve` ships in-tree, so it has no version of its own.
- Test-only artifacts: PR #1297 head `602ff6e7` (the failing L5 run) and `d296180a` (the empty-output run). Both are test files only; neither changes product code.
- Lives in: `services/evolve` (Python) — the fix belongs there; nothing in `packages/` is required beyond the existing settings defaults.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Idea Tree ends the whole research as interrupted after a single empty or over-deep model answer

closed_recent.author: qingkwl
closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

#400 defined the desktop delivery design for Windows and macOS. The Windows implementation has landed through #639, #643 and #666. This feature completes the macOS side so that research users can install, configure, run and update ScienceDiscovery without using a terminal-based source workflow.

**Current status (2026-11-17):** PR #1156 has been merged into `main` as `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74`. The 47-commit feature branch was squashed on merge, producing a tree byte-identical to reviewed head `43d54632`. Implementation and code review are complete; this issue remains open for the unchecked release-acceptance criteria below.

Related: #400 (parent delivery design), #666 (Windows shell counterpart), #34 (desktop window origin).

### Feature scope

- Adapt the shared Electron shell to macOS menus, window and quit behavior, data/log locations, system proxy and process-group lifecycle.
- Add a fail-closed, main-process Seatbelt startup probe and a bilingual standalone failure page.
- Provide reproducible macOS payload assembly, DMG/ZIP packaging, Developer ID signing, notarization and staple.
- Support first acquisition through DMG and visible, prompt-only updates through notarized ZIP and `latest-mac.yml`.
- Provide in-app data cleanup plus an offline uninstall/reset companion script.
- Preserve Windows behavior through the `win_desktop/` → `application/` rename and packaging/CI updates.

### Target user journey

1. Download the signed DMG.
2. Drag ScienceDiscovery into Applications.
3. Choose the data directory on first launch.
4. Let the shell run Seatbelt and runtime startup checks in the background; a Seatbelt failure opens the standalone error page.
5. Configure the model and run a local scientific-research task.
6. Install later updates through the visible notarized ZIP/OTA flow.

## Design Ideas

### Architecture

Reuse JiuwenSwarm as the Agent foundation. This feature connects the scientific-research services and productizes them for macOS desktop users; it does not create a second Agent stack.

```text
Electron shell
Windows, menus, first-run wizard and process management
        ↓
Scientific-research services
API, task execution and runtime adaptation
        ↓
JiuwenSwarm
Existing Skills, Tools and Agent capabilities
```

Seatbelt is checked before execution and blocks entry to the main UI on failure. Data and logs are written outside the signed `.app` so the bundle remains read-only.

### Runtime and packaging entries

`application/` is one shared shell, not two applications. `main.ts` is the common Electron runtime entry; `platform/index.ts` reads `process.platform` and dispatches platform decisions.

```text
application/src/main.ts
        ↓
platform/index.ts
        ├── win32.ts    Windows paths, venv, tray and window behavior
        └── darwin.ts   macOS paths, venv, Dock and menu behavior
```

Runtime entry and packaging entry are separate concerns:

| Platform | Runtime entry | Packaging entry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | `application/src/main.ts` → `platform/index.ts` → `platform/win32.ts` | `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh`; payload assembly defaults to `win32-x64` |
| macOS | `application/src/main.ts` → `platform/index.ts` → `platform/darwin.ts` | `application/scripts/build-mac.sh`; clean machines start with `build-mac-from-scratch.sh`; payload uses `darwin-arm64` |

### Key decisions and constraints

| Decision | Implementation | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Platform facade | Shared types, `win32`, `darwin` and dispatch under `application/src/platform/` | One application with isolated, testable platform decisions |
| Sandbox | Seatbelt only, fail-closed, no bypass tier | Never degrade into unsandboxed execution |
| Bundle integrity | Redirect writes out of `.app`; copy-mode bootstrap; propagate `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`, including to MCP sidecars | A signed/notarized bundle must remain read-only |
| venv relocation | Convert build-host absolute symlinks to relative links into the bundled Python tree | Matches POSIX venv structure and makes the payload relocatable |
| Desktop runtime | v1 uses the build machine's uv-installed Python, as the Windows chain does. Darwin entries in `scripts/binary-release/runtimes.json` are for auditing and a possible future single-file edition; desktop assembly does not consume them in v1 | Aligns the delivery record with the actual DMG/ZIP payload |
| Signing modes | Ad-hoc smoke builds by default; Developer ID + notarization + staple require `SD_MAC_SIGN=1` | Prevents smoke builds from silently using release credentials |
| Updates | Notarized ZIP + `latest-mac.yml`, prompt-only, backend drain before restart | ZIP is the electron-updater carrier; DMG is acquisition-only |
| Architecture | arm64 only for v1 | Intel/x64 timing is deferred until there is concrete demand |
| CI boundary | Windows desktop distribution is covered by CI; macOS packaging and real-Mac acceptance currently rely on local evidence | Makes the current verification boundary explicit |

### Platform behavior

| Area | Windows | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Installation | NSIS / `setup.exe` | DMG drag-install; notarized ZIP for updates |
| Runtime layout | `Scripts/`, `python.exe`, DLL | `bin/`, `python`, symlinks |
| Execution safety | Existing Provider path | Seatbelt + fail-closed |
| System proxy | Registry | `scutil --proxy` |
| Uninstall | Uninstaller + optional deep cleanup | Trash + in-app cleanup + offline uninstall/reset script |

Both platforms share the Electron shell, Node services, Python runtime and JiuwenSwarm.

### Uninstall and reset behavior

The Help menu provides in-app uninstall/data cleanup. `application/scripts/uninstall-mac.command` adds four offline modes: full uninstall, app-only uninstall, data reset and read-only path inspection. It backs up selected critical data, moves deleted items to Trash and checks for leftover backend processes. The script is a separate Release asset and is not embedded in the DMG/ZIP.

### UI and failure states

The packaged desktop flow does not display the SPA `SetupWizard` self-check step. The main process checks Seatbelt in the background: success continues to the remaining initialization steps, while failure replaces the window with a standalone bilingual error page containing structured diagnostics and no path into the main UI.

The SPA self-check component remains covered by component tests, but its pending, success and in-component failure renders are not part of the packaged desktop user journey and are therefore not presented as product screenshots here.

**Standalone Seatbelt error page**

![Standalone Seatbelt error page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/pr-1156-wizard-shots/docs/pr-assets/seatbelt-error-zh.png)

### Non-goals for this delivery

- No Keychain/safeStorage migration; retain AES-256-GCM + `0600` file-based secrets.
- No simultaneous Intel/x64 release.
- No `.pkg` installer.
- No second Agent framework or duplicate JiuwenSwarm capability stack.
- The website `/install` Mac card and telemetry changes are outside this repository.

## Involved Public APIs

No backend public API changes. The shell exposes `sdShell.platform` through preload so the renderer reads the main-process platform value rather than relying on UA sniffing. The platform facade is internal to the shell, and the backend start-stack contract remains unchanged.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Relevance and required verification |
| --- | --- |
| `application/scripts/assemble-backend.mjs`, `application/scripts/lib/assemble-platform.mjs` | Add platform-aware payload assembly; Windows remains the default dialect. Verify payload layout and required files for both platforms. |
| `scripts/binary-release/runtimes.json` | Contains darwin audit entries that desktop assembly does not consume in v1; do not treat them as evidence of a separately pinned desktop Python runtime. |
| `application/scripts/after-pack-trim-locales.cjs` | Supports Windows dash-pak and macOS `.lproj` layouts; verify both packaging paths. |
| `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh` | Supports `application/` with compatibility fallback; Windows install, upgrade and uninstall require regression coverage. |
| `application/src/main.ts`, `stack.ts`, `proxy.ts`, `sandbox-probe.ts`, `updater.ts`, `uninstall-data.ts` | Own shell lifecycle, networking, safety, updates and cleanup; verify platform dispatch and failure paths. |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/SetupWizard.tsx` and text contracts | The packaged shell opens this wizard at model configuration and skips its self-check step; verify that handoff and retain component-test coverage for the non-packaged flow. |
| `services/api` MCP sidecar launch | Propagates `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` into the SDK's minimal child-process environment; verify child-process behavior remains unchanged on other platforms. |

## Test Design and Test Plan

### Test environment

Existing local development-machine evidence was collected on:

**macOS (arm64)**

| Item | Environment |
| --- | --- |
| Model | MacBook Pro, MacBookPro17,1 |
| Chip | Apple M1, 4 performance cores + 4 efficiency cores |
| Memory | 8 GB |
| Architecture | arm64, Apple Silicon |
| OS | macOS 14.8.9, build 23J631 |
| Node.js | v24.22.1 in the local terminal |

**Windows (x64)**

| Item | Environment |
| --- | --- |
| Model | Lenovo laptop |
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 5800H, 8 cores / 16 threads, 3.2 GHz, 16 MB L3 |
| Memory | 32 GB (2×16 GB DDR4-3200, dual channel) |
| GPU | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (8 GB GDDR6) + integrated Radeon |
| Disk | SK hynix 1TB NVMe SSD |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro 64-bit, Build 26300 |

These environments document existing local evidence; they do not replace release acceptance on a clean macOS machine.

### Measured timing data (v0.4.0)

Wall-clock measurements captured on the machines above. First initialization excludes network downloads (the runtime ships inside the package); first-conversation latency includes the round trip to the connected model API.

| Platform | Installer size | Install time | First initialization | Warm start | First conversation | Uninstall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (arm64, DMG) | 578 MB | 43s | 12.3s | 7.2s | 9.8s | 6s |
| Windows (x64, setup.exe) | 587 MB | 1min30s | 11.4s | 10.5s | 10.6s | 25.4s |

> *Reference measurements of WorkSwarm on the same machines:*
>
> **macOS (arm64, MacBook Pro M1, 8 GB)**
>
> | Version | Installer size | Install time | First initialization | Warm start | First conversation | Uninstall |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | WorkSwarm v0.2.6 | 497 MB | 10s | 7s | 6s | 9.7s | — |
> | WorkSwarm v0.2.9 | 834 MB | 12s | 6.7s | 6.9s | 7s | — |
>
> **Windows (x64, Ryzen 7 5800H, 32 GB)**
>
> | Version | Installer size | Install time | First initialization | Warm start | First conversation | Uninstall |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | WorkSwarm v0.2.6 | 352 MB | 43s | 14.1s | 11.3s | 10.8s | 4.6s |
> | WorkSwarm v0.2.9 | 594 MB | 2min4s (second install 1min20s) | 10s | 8.7s | 7.2s | 6s |

Per-stage screenshots:

| Stage | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Install | ![macOS install 43s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/01-mac-install-43s.jpg) | ![Windows install 1min30s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/06-win-install-1min30s.jpg) |
| First initialization | ![macOS first init 12.3s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/02-mac-first-init-12.3s.jpg) | ![Windows first init 11.4s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/07-win-first-init-11.4s.jpg) |
| First conversation | ![macOS first conversation 9.8s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/03-mac-first-conversation-9.8s.jpg) | ![Windows first conversation 10.6s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/08-win-first-conversation-10.6s.jpg) |
| Warm start | ![macOS warm start 7.2s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/04-mac-warm-start-7.2s.jpg) | ![Windows warm start 10.5s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/09-win-warm-start-10.5s.jpg) |
| Uninstall | ![macOS uninstall 6s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/05-mac-uninstall-6s.jpg) | ![Windows uninstall 25.4s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/10-win-uninstall-25.4s.jpg) |

Full-journey recordings (install → first initialization → first conversation → warm start → uninstall):

- macOS: [MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/11-mac-full-recording.mp4) · [GIF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/11-mac-full-recording.gif)
- Windows: [MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/12-win-full-recording.mp4) · [GIF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/issue-1165-evidence/docs/issue-assets/12-win-full-recording.gif)

> **Version-over-version improvement (v0.3.0 → v0.4.0, Windows)** — same Lenovo Windows machine as above. All six metrics improved:
>
> | Metric | v0.3.0 | v0.4.0 | Improvement |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | Installer size | 791 MB | 587 MB | **smaller by 204 MB (25.8%)** |
> | Install | 2min | 1min30s | faster by 30s (25.0%) |
> | First initialization | 14.5s | 11.4s | faster by 3.1s (21.4%) |
> | Warm start | 14s | 10.5s | faster by 3.5s (25.0%) |
> | First conversation | 22.2s | 10.6s | **faster by 11.6s (52.3%)** |
> | Uninstall | 30s | 25.4s | faster by 4.6s (15.3%) |

### Test matrix

| Dimension | What must be protected | Verification method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shell functionality | Start, stop, update, uninstall and Windows/macOS branch behavior | `pnpm --dir application test` |
| Compile and build integrity | Type, syntax and shell build failures | `pnpm --dir application typecheck` and `pnpm --dir application build` |
| Platform isolation | Shared dispatch without cross-platform regressions | `application/src/platform/index.ts`, `win32.ts`/`darwin.ts` branch tests and `shell-platform.ts` compatibility tests |
| Sandbox security | Seatbelt existence, execution, spawn failure, signals, exit codes, timeout and fail-closed behavior | `sandbox-probe.ts` real probe plus `sandbox-probe.test.ts` decision and exception tests |
| UI and diagnostics | Model-configuration handoff, zh/en copy and standalone Seatbelt failure diagnostics; the packaged flow must not show the SPA self-check step | `apps/desktop/tests/app-model-setup-render.test.ts` (the packaged-handoff guard: four scenarios × zh/en, injecting `sdShell: { wizardIntroDone: true }`), `setup-wizard.test.tsx` (non-packaged component states), `seatbelt-error.html` and component-render review |
| Packaged runtime completeness | Python, dependencies, symlinks, patches and bytecode | `build-mac.sh` and `pyc-budget.test.ts`: A1 import smoke, A1b runtime probe, A2 required files, A6 bytecode, path, symlink and patch-chain gates |
| Build reproducibility | A fresh Mac/clone can assemble and package without undocumented machine state | `build-mac-from-scratch.sh` followed by `build-mac.sh` local gates |
| Apple distribution checks | App and DMG signatures, notarization, staple and Gatekeeper assessment | `codesign`, `notarytool`, `stapler` and `spctl` on both artifacts |
| Startup timing guard | A healthy launch never silently turns into a hang: every component reaches its ready/healthy event within its hang ceiling | `perf-gate.mjs` two-layer gate in CI (`macos-desktop` job, `--hang-only`): real packaged `.app` launch via `perf-smoke-mac.sh`, first-run `shell.log` judged against `perf-budget.json` hang ceilings (H1-H9); measured log uploaded as `perf-smoke-shell-log-<sha>` artifact — landed via #1374 |

Unit tests with fake process spawns verify decision logic; component renders verify UI states; local packaging verifies the build chain. None of these alone substitutes for the remaining real-machine release acceptance.

The timing guard was added after the matrix above: it is the machine-checked layer for the "silent hang" class, judging the same logs the real-machine acceptance reads.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Engineering checks

- [x] `pnpm --dir application test` passes for the merged implementation.
- [x] `pnpm --dir application typecheck` passes for the merged implementation.
- [x] Local macOS packaging gates and the signing/notarization chain have been exercised.
- [x] The from-scratch packaging flow has passed clean-room reproduction checks.

### Release acceptance

- [ ] **Clean-machine macOS acceptance:** download DMG → drag install → wizard → complete a small task, with no unexpected Gatekeeper prompt; `spctl` accepts both the `.app` and DMG.
- [ ] **Sandbox red line on the release package:** when Seatbelt fails, the app never reaches the main UI; zh/en error surfaces show actionable diagnostics and no forward button.
- [ ] **Signed bundle remains read-only:** first and second runs write nothing into `.app`; re-verify with `codesign --verify --deep --strict`.
- [ ] **Quit semantics:** Cmd+Q drains and stops the complete stack, including detached JiuwenSwarm processes; no orphan processes or occupied ports remain.
- [x] **Windows regression:** install, upgrade and uninstall still work after the `application/` rename and payload-gate changes. (Evidence: the Windows measurement table above — setup.exe 587 MB, install 1min30s, first initialization 11.4s, warm start 10.5s, first conversation 10.6s, uninstall 25.4s — with per-stage screenshots and the full-journey recording.)
- [x] **Minimum macOS version:** pinned to macOS 14.0 — `minimumSystemVersion: 14.0.0` in `application/electron-builder.yml` (#1217). Basis: Electron 37 supports the last three macOS majors (15/14/13); the only acceptance machine runs 14.8.9; macOS 13 has fallen outside that window with no test coverage and no Gatekeeper data.
- [ ] **Release CI policy:** record whether manual real-Mac evidence is sufficient for v1 or whether a macOS CI job is required. *Update: a macOS CI timing gate has landed via #1374 (`macos-desktop` job smoke-launches the packaged `.app` and judges the first-run `shell.log` in `--hang-only` mode, uploading the measured log) — the manual real-Mac evidence stays the baseline source, and the gate covers the silent-hang class on every PR/push. Awaiting owner sign-off on this record.*

Commands that must pass for the applicable engineering/package checks:

```bash
pnpm --dir application test
pnpm --dir application typecheck
pnpm --dir application build
bash application/scripts/build-mac.sh
spctl -a -vv -t open --context context:primary-signature <dmg>
```

## Additional Information

- Merge commit `5058334` records application tests **345/345** (the full `pnpm --dir application test` run on macOS). The export tests inherited from upstream sit in three files: `export-history.test.ts` (7 cases), `export-state.test.ts` (4) and `export-tokens.test.ts` (5). The `apps/desktop` figure **30 passing** is the full suite under `pnpm --dir apps/desktop test` (`tests/*.test.ts(x)`). Typecheck clean; Windows distribution-gate CI contract green.
- The v0.4.0 smoke DMG is **578 MB**. Three progressive clean-room checks reproduced the from-scratch flow.
- The signing/notarization chain has been exercised successfully. Credential holder and release operator for v1 (F1): the Developer ID Application certificate is issued to **Haowen Zhong** (Apple Developer team **UGV44NUA6W**); the same person holds the App Store Connect notarization key and the `sd-notary` keychain profile, and operates the formal macOS release.

- **Startup timing guard (merged, #1374 → `9c74af8b`).** The shell/start-stack/jiuwenswarm ms instrumentation in `shell.log` is now judged by a two-layer gate: an absolute **hang layer** (hard hang ceilings H1-H9 in `application/scripts/perf-budget.json`; a missing event pair IS the hang signal; the agent-ready ceiling equals `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` so gate and runtime blow together) plus a machine-local **regression layer** (baseline × 1.4, warn-first, two-strike hard fail — judged only on machines with baselines, so CI runs hang-only). The `macos-desktop` CI job launches the packaged `.app` for real (`perf-smoke-mac.sh`: seeded wizard state backed up/restored, rotation-safe log-delta locking, signal traps), judges the first-run log in `--hang-only` mode, and uploads the measured log (`perf-smoke-shell-log-<sha>`, 14 days) as evidence. End-to-end verified on a real macOS runner before merge (fork Package@macos run 45541198600: ok 10 / hang 0 / exit 0, agent-ready 20.9s, far below its 180s ceiling). Parser/verdict/gate/smoke are pure additions; no runtime behavior changed. P2 (wizard/reuse-path instrumentation) and P3-2 (baseline collection from release-run logs) remain follow-ups.

> **The startup timing guard: per-component hang ceilings** (`application/scripts/perf-budget.json`, first-session table; the warm table keeps the same ceilings with shorter baselines and no unpack).
>
> What the three numbers mean, to avoid misreading:
> - **Hang ceiling (hard red line):** a component still short of its ready/healthy event past this value — or a missing event pair — is judged a hang: the gate exits 1, CI goes red. It is a loose tripwire, **NOT an expected duration**.
> - **Measured baseline (expected reference):** what the signed build actually takes on a healthy launch.
> - **Regression line (soft):** baseline × 1.4 — warn first, hard-fail on the second consecutive strike. Gradual drift trips here long before the ceiling.
>
> | Component (event pair) | Hang ceiling | Measured baseline (expected reference) | How the ceiling was derived |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | shell-boot (module-load → stack-spawned) | 30s | 6.2s | Loosened from measurement: unpack is ~1GB I/O-bound, 20s+ on slow disks; re-reviewed 20s → 30s |
> | unpack (first sessions only) | 30s | 2.0s | ~1GB I/O-bound extract, 20s+ on slow disks; same 30s floor as shell-boot |
> | runner-ready | 30s | 0.2–0.4s | Sub-second op; the 30s is a stall floor (GC/disk contention), not a multiplier |
> | memory-graph-ready | 45s | 0.6–2.9s | Healthy range already spans ~5× (cold imports); 45s covers the worst healthy case |
> | evolve-ready | 45s | 0.8–2.9s | Same: healthy range spans ~4×; 45s covers the worst healthy case |
> | api-ready (api-spawn → HEALTH-200, full-stack marker) | 60s | 3.2–3.6s | Cold-runner dependency imports can take tens of seconds; 60s covers the worst healthy case |
> | jw-ready (spawn-jw-app → IS-UP) | 120s | 4.8s (warm) / 7.9s (first) | Loosened: a from-scratch reinstall can take minutes |
> | agent-ready | 180s | 8.2–18.8s | **Pinned to the runtime constant `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`** (= jw 120s + 60s watch/adapter margin; the gate and the runtime blow together, a unit test reads the source to keep them from drifting) |
> | shell-ui (AGENT-READY → loadUi-loadURL) | 15s | 0.1–0.2s | Sub-second UI load; 15s is the minimum floor against GC/Spotlight stalls (event pair corrected in review) |
> | warmup-done (AGENT-READY → [warmup] 200) | 60s | 0.4–1.3s | **Pinned to `FIRST_CHAT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_MS`**; cold full-catalog measured ~48s, 60s just covers it (only 25% headroom — raise together if the catalog grows) |
>
> Derivation (why so wide): the ceiling only waits for events that never arrive — width changes how soon a hang is reported, not whether it is, and gradual drift trips the regression line (baseline × 1.4) first. The big multipliers come from the reference frames differing: the baseline column is a healthy dev machine's median, while the ceiling is sized for the **worst healthy case** (slow disk / loaded runner / cold caches / fresh install — warmup-done's 60s covers the measured 48s cold-catalog path, not the 1.3s warm path; jw-ready's 120s covers a from-scratch reinstall; agent-ready's 180s mirrors the runtime constant `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`; sub-second components get a ~15s floor against transient stalls). Worst-case serial chain 320s < the 600s cold-start backstop.

## 🚀 背景说明

#400 确定了 Windows 和 macOS 双平台桌面交付设计，Windows 侧已经通过 #639、#643 和 #666 落地。本需求补齐 macOS 侧能力，让科研用户无需通过终端运行源码，也能完成 ScienceDiscovery 的安装、配置、任务执行和更新。

**当前状态（2026-11-17）：** PR #1156 已合入 `main`，合并提交为 `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74`。原功能分支的 47 个提交在合并时压缩为一个提交，合并后的代码树与评审头 `43d54632` 逐字节一致。实现和代码评审已经完成；本 Issue 继续跟踪下方尚未完成的发布验收项。

关联：#400（交付总设计）、#666（Windows 桌面壳）、#34（桌面窗口起点）。

### 需求范围

- 让共用 Electron 壳适配 macOS 菜单、窗口与退出行为、数据和日志目录、系统代理及进程组生命周期。
- 由主进程在启动时检查 Seatbelt，失败即阻断，并提供中英文独立错误页。
- 提供可复现的 macOS 载荷组装、DMG/ZIP 出包、Developer ID 签名、公证和 staple。
- 首次安装使用 DMG，后续更新使用公证 ZIP 和 `latest-mac.yml`，更新过程可见且只提示、不静默。
- 提供应用内数据清理，以及独立的离线卸载／重置脚本。
- 在 `win_desktop/` 更名为 `application/` 后，保持 Windows 行为、打包链和 CI 兼容。

### 目标使用流程

1. 下载签名 DMG。
2. 将 ScienceDiscovery 拖入 Applications。
3. 首次启动时选择数据目录。
4. 由桌面壳在后台执行 Seatbelt 和运行时启动检查；Seatbelt 失败时显示独立错误页。
5. 配置模型并运行本地科研任务。
6. 后续通过可见的公证 ZIP／OTA 流程完成更新。

## 设计思路

### 技术架构

继续复用 JiuwenSwarm 的 Agent 底座。本需求负责接入科研服务并完成 macOS 桌面产品化，不再另建一套 Agent 能力。

```text
Electron 桌面壳
窗口、菜单、首启向导与进程管理
        ↓
科研服务
API、任务执行与运行时适配
        ↓
JiuwenSwarm
复用既有 Skills、Tools 与 Agent 能力
```

Seatbelt 在执行前先自检，失败则阻断主界面；数据和日志写入签名 `.app` 之外，保证应用包保持只读。

### 运行时入口与出包入口

`application/` 是双平台共用的一套桌面壳，不是两套应用。`main.ts` 是公共 Electron 运行时入口，`platform/index.ts` 根据 `process.platform` 分发平台决策。

```text
application/src/main.ts
        ↓
platform/index.ts
        ├── win32.ts    Windows 路径、venv、托盘与窗口行为
        └── darwin.ts   macOS 路径、venv、Dock 与菜单行为
```

运行时入口和出包入口不是一回事：

| 平台 | 运行时入口 | 出包入口 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | `application/src/main.ts` → `platform/index.ts` → `platform/win32.ts` | `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh`，载荷默认按 `win32-x64` 组装 |
| macOS | `application/src/main.ts` → `platform/index.ts` → `platform/darwin.ts` | `application/scripts/build-mac.sh`；干净机器先执行 `build-mac-from-scratch.sh`，载荷按 `darwin-arm64` 组装 |

### 关键决策与约束

| 决策点 | 当前实现 | 原因 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 平台门面 | `application/src/platform/` 放置公共类型、win32、darwin 和统一分发入口 | 保持一套应用，隔离平台差异并便于单测 |
| 沙箱 | 仅 Seatbelt，失败即阻断，不留绕行档位 | 沙箱不可用时不能降级成无隔离执行 |
| 签名包完整性 | 写入改道到 `.app` 外；bootstrap 使用拷贝模式；`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` 传递到 MCP sidecar | 签名、公证后的应用包必须保持只读 |
| venv 搬迁 | 把构建机绝对路径符号链接改为指向包内 Python 的相对链接 | 符合 POSIX venv 结构，保证载荷可以迁移 |
| 桌面运行时 | v1 使用构建机上由 uv 安装的 Python，与 Windows 链一致；`scripts/binary-release/runtimes.json` 的 darwin 条目用于版本审计和未来可能的单文件版本，桌面组装暂不消费 | 让交付说明与 DMG/ZIP 的实际载荷一致 |
| 签名模式 | 默认 ad-hoc 冒烟；显式设置 `SD_MAC_SIGN=1` 才使用 Developer ID、公证和 staple | 避免冒烟构建误用正式凭证 |
| 更新 | 公证 ZIP＋`latest-mac.yml`，只提示，重启前停稳后端 | electron-updater 使用 ZIP，DMG 只负责首次安装 |
| 架构 | v1 仅支持 arm64 | Intel/x64 等有明确需求后再安排 |
| CI 边界 | Windows 桌面包分发由 CI 看护；macOS 出包和真机验收目前依靠本地证据 | 明确当前验证边界 |

### 平台行为差异

| 方面 | Windows | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 安装 | NSIS / `setup.exe` | DMG 拖拽安装，公证 ZIP 用于更新 |
| 运行时结构 | `Scripts/`、`python.exe`、DLL | `bin/`、`python`、符号链接 |
| 执行安全 | 既有 Provider 路径 | Seatbelt＋失败即阻断 |
| 系统代理 | 注册表 | `scutil --proxy` |
| 卸载 | 卸载器＋可选深度清理 | 废纸篓＋应用内清理＋离线卸载／重置脚本 |

双平台共用 Electron 壳、Node 服务、Python 运行时和 JiuwenSwarm。

### 卸载与重置行为

帮助菜单提供应用内卸载和数据清理。`application/scripts/uninstall-mac.command` 提供四种离线模式：完全卸载、只卸载应用、数据重置和仅查看路径。脚本会备份指定的关键数据，将删除内容移入废纸篓，并检查后端残留进程。该脚本作为 Release 独立资产分发，不放进 DMG/ZIP。

### 界面与失败状态

打包后的桌面流程不展示 SPA `SetupWizard` 中的自检步骤。主进程在后台检查 Seatbelt：成功后继续后续初始化步骤；失败后将窗口切换为中英文独立错误页，展示结构化诊断信息，且不能进入主界面。

SPA 自检组件仍由组件测试看护，但其自检中、自检通过和组件内失败状态不属于打包桌面版的真实使用流程，因此不再作为产品截图展示。

**Seatbelt 独立错误页**

![Seatbelt 独立错误页](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/assets/pr-1156-wizard-shots/docs/pr-assets/seatbelt-error-zh.png)

### 本期非目标

- 不迁移 Keychain/safeStorage，继续使用 AES-256-GCM＋`0600` 文件密钥方案。
- 不同时发布 Intel/x64 版本。
- 不增加 `.pkg` 安装器。
- 不另建 Agent 框架，也不重复实现 JiuwenSwarm 已有能力。
- 官网 `/install` 的 Mac 卡片和遥测改动不在本仓范围内。

## 涉及的公开接口

后端公开 API 没有变化。壳层通过 preload 增加 `sdShell.platform`，让前端读取主进程的真实平台值，而不是通过 UA 猜测。平台门面属于壳内部实现，后端起栈契约保持不变。

## 对其他模块的影响

| 模块 | 影响及需要补充的验证 |
| --- | --- |
| `application/scripts/assemble-backend.mjs`、`application/scripts/lib/assemble-platform.mjs` | 增加按平台组装载荷的能力，默认仍走 Windows 方言；需要验证双平台载荷布局和必需文件。 |
| `scripts/binary-release/runtimes.json` | 包含桌面组装暂不消费的 darwin 审计条目，不能据此宣称桌面版已经单独固定 Python 运行时。 |
| `application/scripts/after-pack-trim-locales.cjs` | 同时支持 Windows dash-pak 和 macOS `.lproj` 布局；需要验证两条出包路径。 |
| `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh` | 支持 `application/` 并保留兼容回退；需要回归 Windows 安装、升级和卸载。 |
| `application/src/main.ts`、`stack.ts`、`proxy.ts`、`sandbox-probe.ts`、`updater.ts`、`uninstall-data.ts` | 负责壳生命周期、网络、安全、更新和清理；需要验证平台分发及失败路径。 |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/SetupWizard.tsx` 及文案契约 | 打包壳加载该向导时直接进入模型配置并跳过自检步骤；需要验证这一衔接，同时保留非打包流程的组件测试。 |
| `services/api` 的 MCP sidecar 启动 | 将 `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` 传入 SDK 的最小子进程环境；需要确认其他平台的子进程行为不变。 |

| 平台隔离 | 公共分发正常，修改一端不影响另一端 | `application/src/platform/index.ts`、`win32.ts`／`darwin.ts` 分支测试和 `shell-platform.ts` 兼容测试 |

| 界面与诊断 | 模型配置衔接、中英文文案和 Seatbelt 独立错误页诊断正确；打包流程不得展示 SPA 自检步骤 | `apps/desktop/tests/app-model-setup-render.test.ts`（打包衔接守卫：四场景 × zh/en，注入 `sdShell: { wizardIntroDone: true }`）、`setup-wizard.test.tsx`（非打包组件状态）、`seatbelt-error.html` 和组件渲染检查 |
| 安装包运行时完整性 | Python、依赖、符号链接、补丁和字节码完整 | `build-mac.sh`、`pyc-budget.test.ts`：A1 导入冒烟、A1b 运行时探针、A2 必需文件、A6 字节码，以及路径、符号链接和补丁链门禁 |
| 出包可复现性 | 全新 Mac／克隆不依赖未记录的本机状态也能出包 | 执行 `build-mac-from-scratch.sh`，再执行 `build-mac.sh` 本机门禁 |
| Apple 分发检查 | 应用和 DMG 的签名、公证、staple 与 Gatekeeper 评估通过 | 对两类产物执行 `codesign`、`notarytool`、`stapler` 和 `spctl` |
| 启动性能看护 | 健康启动不悄悄退化成挂死：每个组件都在报错上限内到达 ready/healthy 事件 | `perf-gate.mjs` 两层看护接入 CI（`macos-desktop` job，`--hang-only`）：经 `perf-smoke-mac.sh` 真实启动打包后的 `.app`，用 `perf-budget.json` 报错上限（H1-H9）判定首启 `shell.log`；实测日志以 `perf-smoke-shell-log-<sha>` artifact 上传——经 #1374 落地 |

使用模拟进程启动的单测负责验证决策逻辑，组件渲染负责验证界面状态，本机出包负责验证构建链；任何一项都不能单独替代剩余的真机发布验收。

启动性能看护在上述矩阵之后加入：它是针对「静默挂死」类的机器检查层，判定的正是真机发布验收所读的同一份日志。

## 验收标准

### 工程检查

- [x] 合并实现的 `pnpm --dir application test` 已通过。
- [x] 合并实现的 `pnpm --dir application typecheck` 已通过。
- [x] 本地 macOS 出包门禁和签名、公证链已实际执行。
- [x] 从零出包流程已通过 clean-room 复验。

### 发布验收

- [ ] **干净 macOS 环境验收**：下载 DMG → 拖入 Applications → 完成向导 → 跑通一个小任务；没有意外的 Gatekeeper 拦截，`spctl` 对 `.app` 和 DMG 均放行。
- [ ] **发布包沙箱红线**：Seatbelt 失败时不能进入主界面；中英文错误页提供可操作的诊断信息，且没有前进按钮。
- [ ] **签名包保持只读**：首启和二启都不写入 `.app`，并用 `codesign --verify --deep --strict` 复验封条。
- [ ] **退出语义**：Cmd+Q 排空并停止完整后端栈，包括独立进程组中的 JiuwenSwarm；不留孤儿进程，端口全部释放。
- [x] **Windows 回归**：`application/` 改名和载荷门禁调整后，安装、升级、卸载仍然正常。（证据：上方 Windows 实测数据表——setup.exe 587 MB、安装 1min30s、首次初始化 11.4s、热启动 10.5s、首对话 10.6s、卸载 25.4s——含各阶段截图与全流程录屏。）
- [x] **最低 macOS 版本**：已定为 macOS 14.0——`application/electron-builder.yml` 写入 `minimumSystemVersion: 14.0.0`（#1217）。依据：Electron 37 官方支持最近三个 macOS 大版本（15/14/13）；唯一验收机为 14.8.9；macOS 13 已出支持窗，无任何测试与 Gatekeeper 数据。
- [ ] **发布 CI 策略**：明确 v1 是否接受人工真机证据作为发布门禁，还是必须增加 macOS CI 任务。*更新：macOS CI 耗时看护已经 #1374 落地（`macos-desktop` job 冒烟启动打包 `.app` 并以 `--hang-only` 判定首启 `shell.log`，上传实测日志）——人工真机证据仍为基线来源，门禁在每个 PR/push 上覆盖静默挂死类风险。等 owner 对此记录签字确认。*

适用的工程检查和出包检查必须通过以下命令：

```bash
pnpm --dir application test
pnpm --dir application typecheck
pnpm --dir application build
bash application/scripts/build-mac.sh
spctl -a -vv -t open --context context:primary-signature <dmg>
```

## 补充信息

- 合并提交 `5058334` 记录 application 测试 **345/345**（macOS 上完整执行 `pnpm --dir application test`）。上游合入的导出相关测试分布在三个文件：`export-history.test.ts`（7 项）、`export-state.test.ts`（4 项）与 `export-tokens.test.ts`（5 项）。`apps/desktop` **30 项通过**为 `pnpm --dir apps/desktop test` 的全量结果（`tests/*.test.ts(x)`）。类型检查通过；Windows 分发门禁的 CI 契约检查通过。
- v0.4.0 冒烟 DMG 为 **578 MB**；从零出包流程已完成三次递进的 clean-room 复验。
- 签名、公证链已经实测通过。v1 凭证持有人与发布执行人（F1）：Developer ID Application 证书属 **Haowen Zhong**（Apple Developer 团队 **UGV44NUA6W**）；公证所用 App Store Connect 密钥与 `sd-notary` 钥匙串档案同由其保管，正式 macOS 发布亦由其执行。
- 官网 `/install` 和遥测工作需要在本仓之外单独跟踪。
- Intel/x64 分发继续后置。
- **启动性能看护（已合并，#1374 → `9c74af8b`）。** shell/start-stack/jiuwenswarm 打进 `shell.log` 的毫秒级打点现在由两层门禁判定：绝对 **hang 层**（报错上限 H1-H9 落在 `application/scripts/perf-budget.json`；缺失事件对即挂死信号；agent-ready 上限与运行时常量 `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` 对齐，门禁与运行时同时引爆）+ 机器本地 **regression 层**（基线 × 1.4，warn-first、二振出局——只在有基线的机器上判定，因此 CI 以 `--hang-only` 运行）。`macos-desktop` CI job 真实启动打包后的 `.app`（`perf-smoke-mac.sh`：向导状态备份/恢复、轮转安全的日志增量锁定、信号陷阱），以 `--hang-only` 判定首启日志并上传实测日志（`perf-smoke-shell-log-<sha>`，14 天）作证据。合并前已在真实 macOS runner 端到端实证（fork Package@macos run 45541198600：ok 10 / hang 0 / exit 0，agent-ready 实测 20.9s，远低于 180s 上限）。解析器/判定层/门禁/冒烟均为纯新增，不改任何运行时行为。P2（向导/reuse 路径打点）与 P3-2（发布跑基线采集）留作后续。

> **启动性能看护：组件报错上限表**（`application/scripts/perf-budget.json` 首启档；热启档上限同值、基线更短、无 unpack）。
>
> 三层数值语义，防误读：
> - **报错上限（硬红线）**：组件超过该值仍未到达 ready/healthy 事件、或事件对缺失 → 判「挂死」→ 门禁 exit 1 → CI 红。它是宽松探测线，**不是预期值**。
> - **实测基线（预期参考）**：签名包健康启动的实际耗时——预期量级。
> - **回归警戒线（软线）**：基线 × 1.4；超先警告，连续第二次硬失败。渐进退化在此提前报警，不用等到碰上限。
>
> | 组件（事件对） | 报错上限 | 实测基线（预期参考） | 上限如何而来 |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | shell-boot（module-load → stack-spawned） | 30s | 6.2s | 实测放宽：unpack 为 ~1GB I/O 主导，慢盘机器可 20s+，复审从 20s 放宽到 30s |
> | unpack（仅首启档） | 30s | 2.0s | ~1GB 解压 I/O 主导，慢盘可 20s+，与 shell-boot 同 30s 地板 |
> | runner-ready | 30s | 0.2~0.4s | 亚秒操作；上限是防瞬时卡顿（GC/磁盘争用）的地板值，非按倍数定 |
> | memory-graph-ready | 45s | 0.6~2.9s | 健康范围近 5 倍（冷依赖导入）；45s 罩最坏健康场景，防卡顿地板 |
> | evolve-ready | 45s | 0.8~2.9s | 同上：健康范围已达 4 倍，45s 罩最坏健康场景 |
> | api-ready（api-spawn → HEALTH-200，全栈标志） | 60s | 3.2~3.6s | 冷 runner 依赖导入可达几十秒，60s 罩最坏健康场景 |
> | jw-ready（spawn-jw-app → IS-UP） | 120s | 4.8s（热）/ 7.9s（首） | 实测放宽：从零重装可到分钟级 |
> | agent-ready | 180s | 8.2~18.8s | **对齐运行时常量 `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`**（= jw 120s + watch 轮询/adapter 启动 60s 余量；门禁与运行时同时引爆，单测读源码钉死防漂移） |
> | shell-ui（AGENT-READY → loadUi-loadURL） | 15s | 0.1~0.2s | 亚秒 UI 加载；15s 是防 GC/Spotlight 瞬时卡顿的最低地板（事件对曾误配，复审已修正） |
> | warmup-done（AGENT-READY → [warmup] 200） | 60s | 0.4~1.3s | **对齐 `FIRST_CHAT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_MS`**；冷态全量 catalog 实测 ~48s，60s 恰好罩住（余量仅 25%，catalog 膨胀需同步上调） |
>
> 推导口径（为何这么宽）：上限只等「永不到来」的事件——宽窄只影响报警早晚、不影响是否报警，渐进变慢由回归警戒线（基线 × 1.4）先抓。倍数看着大是因为参照系不同：基线列是开发机健康启动的中位数，上限对着的是**最坏健康场景**（慢磁盘/高负载 runner/冷缓存/从零安装——warmup-done 60s 罩的是冷态 catalog 实测 48s 而非热态 1.3s，jw-ready 120s 罩从零重装，agent-ready 180s = 运行时常量 `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` 的镜像，亚秒组件另有 ~15s 起的防瞬时卡顿误报地板）。串行最坏 320s < 冷启兜底 600s。
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: macOS desktop adaptation: shell, packaging chain, Seatbelt sandbox & distribution

closed_recent.author: nanzhaogang
closed_recent.body:
## 背景

积分规则已确定：首次登录赠送 500 积分，每个自然日首次登录自动发放 100 积分，累计签到每满 7 天再发放 50 积分，且不设发放上限。

当前产品尚未提供任何账户相关页面与管理入口：用户无法确认今日奖励是否到账、看不到积分花在哪里，也没有自助管理登录设备的入口；运营与客服在核对流水、发放补偿、处理账号风险时只能直连数据库，既不安全也不可审计。

本 issue 包含两份需求文档：面向用户的账户中心（在本仓验收）、面向运营的用户管理后台（不在本仓验收）。

---

## 一、ScienceDiscovery 用户账户中心（用户信息详情页）需求文档

| 项目 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 文档版本 | v1.2 |
| 状态 | 待评审 |
| 更新日期 | 2026-11-21 |

在应用内提供可自助查看的账户页：用户能确认积分余额与 token 折算、今日奖励到账与满 7 天进度、积分消耗去向，并管理登录设备与昵称。

### 01 需求详情

#### 背景与问题

积分规则已经确定：首次登录赠送 500 积分，每个自然日首次登录自动发放 100 积分，累计签到每满 7 天再发放 50 积分，且不设发放上限。当前产品尚未提供账户相关页面，用户无法确认今日奖励是否到账、看不到积分花在哪里，也没有自助管理登录设备的入口。为此新增用户信息详情页：点击用户按钮后打开账户面板，让用户在一屏内看清余额、今日奖励与消耗去向，并能管理登录设备与昵称。

### 02 需求设计方案

#### 页面形态与信息架构

新增用户详情入口，点击后在工作区上方打开账户面板（左侧导航栏保留，点击「会话」返回工作台），自上而下分为五层：

1. **账户概览**：头像首字母与昵称 → 可用积分 → token 折算 → 累计获得 / 累计消耗。
2. **今日奖励**：今日到账状态与 +100 积分 → 7 天进度（第 1–7 天）→ 距离满 7 天还差几天。
3. **积分流水与消耗明细**：全部 / 获得 / 消耗筛选、分页与消耗明细展开。
4. **登录设备管理**：当前设备与其他设备的退出操作。
5. **页脚**：退出登录（退出后保留工作台，自定义模型仍可使用）。

页面只展示积分与 token，不出现任何金额；每日奖励为登录自动到账，不设签到按钮。

### 03 需求规格

#### 功能需求清单

| 编号 | 功能 | 规则与结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | 账户概览 | 展示头像首字母、昵称、可用积分；token 折算 = 积分 × 4 万，按“万”取整；展示累计获得、累计消耗。**不展示任何金额。** |
| FR-02 | 今日奖励与 7 天进度 | 当日已发放时显示“今日登录奖励已到账 +100 积分”，未发放时显示“登录后自动到账”；7 个格子按顺序展示到账积分（第 1 天 600、第 2–6 天各 100、第 7 天 +50），当天高亮；提示“再连续 N 天可获满 7 天奖励 +50 积分”。 |
| FR-03 | 积分流水与消耗明细 | 按时间倒序展示流水，含类型、时间、变动积分、变动后余额；支持“全部 / 获得 / 消耗”筛选；点击模型调用记录可展开模型、输入 / 缓存 / 输出 token、耗时与 token 合计；支持分页（每页 10 / 30 / 50 / 100 条，可跳页，显示当前页与总页数）。 |
| FR-04 | 登录设备管理 | 展示平台与登录时间；当前设备带“当前”标记且不可退出；其他设备可“退出”，点击后该会话立即失效并从列表移除，提示“已退出该设备”。不展示 IP、内部设备 ID 与完整 openid。 |
| FR-05 | 昵称与退出登录 | 昵称可编辑（1–24 字符），保存后面板头部与用户按钮同步更新；页脚“退出登录”清除本机账号会话并保留工作台，自定义模型仍可继续使用。 |

### 04 需求验收标准

| 编号 | 对应功能 | 验收条件 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | 账户概览 | 可用积分与账户实际余额一致；token 折算 = 积分 × 4 万，误差不超过 1 万；累计获得、累计消耗满足“获得 − 消耗 = 余额”；全页不出现 ¥、元、价格、成本等金额表述。 |
| AC-02 | 今日奖励与 7 天进度 | 当日已发放时显示“已到账 +100 积分”，未发放时显示“登录后自动到账”；页面不存在签到按钮；第 1 天显示 600、第 2–6 天显示 100、第 7 天显示 +50；当天高亮，“再连续 N 天”与实际剩余天数一致。 |
| AC-03 | 积分流水与消耗明细 | 记录按时间倒序，相邻记录满足“上一条余额 + 本条变动 = 本条余额”；“获得 / 消耗”筛选结果正确；消耗行展开后展示模型、输入/缓存/输出 token、耗时与 token 合计，获得行不可展开；分页切换后条数与页码一致。 |
| AC-04 | 登录设备管理 | 当前设备带“当前”标记且无退出按钮；点击其他设备“退出”后立即从列表移除并提示；被退出设备下一次请求被拒绝并要求重新登录。 |
| AC-05 | 昵称与退出登录 | 昵称保存后面板头部与用户按钮同步更新，刷新后保持；空值无法保存，输入上限 24 字符；退出登录后清除本机账号会话并保留工作台，自定义模型仍可使用。 |

---

## 二、ScienceDiscovery 用户管理后台需求文档（本需求不在 ScienceDiscovery 代码仓验收）

| 项目 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 文档版本 | v1.0 |
| 状态 | 待评审 |
| 更新日期 | 2026-11-18 |

为运营与客服提供后台：能检索任意用户、查看其积分与用量全貌，并在必要时调整积分、限制账号或强制下线，所有操作留痕可追溯。

### 01 需求详情

#### 背景与问题

前台账户中心解决了用户“看得到”的问题，但运营与客服还需要“查得到、管得住”：用户反馈积分异常时，需要核对其流水与用量；出现滥用或账号风险时，需要限制账号或强制下线；活动补偿需要人工发放积分。当前缺少统一的管理入口，上述动作只能依赖数据库直连，既不可审计也存在误操作风险。为此新增用户管理后台：以用户列表为入口，进入单个用户后可查看账户、流水、用量与会话，并执行受权限约束、必须填写原因的管理操作。

### 02 需求设计方案

#### 页面形态与信息架构

后台为独立站点，与前台账户体系分离，通过账号密码完成登录，仅授权账号可进入。页面由列表页与详情页两级构成：

1. **概览与用户列表**：顶部展示总用户数、今日新增、今日活跃、今日消耗积分、在线会话、冻结用户；列表支持按昵称或标识搜索，按状态、在线状态筛选，按余额、消耗、最近活跃排序，并分页展示。
2. **用户详情**：上半部分为身份与积分概览，下半部分为流水、用量、会话、操作审计四个区块。
3. **管理操作**：积分调整、账号状态修改、强制下线，均在详情页内发起，需二次确认并填写原因。
4. **操作留痕**：每次写操作记录操作人、对象、动作、原因、时间与来源地址，可在用户审计与全局审计中查询。

管理操作与只读查看在权限上分离，只读账号不可执行任何写操作。

### 03 需求规格

#### 功能需求清单

| 编号 | 功能 | 规则与结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | 登录与权限 | 账号密码校验通过后建立后台会话；连续输错达到阈值临时锁定；禁用账号拒绝登录；会话超时自动失效；写操作仅对具备操作权限的账号开放。 |
| FR-02 | 概览与用户列表 | 概览展示总用户、今日新增、今日活跃、今日消耗积分、在线会话、冻结用户；列表展示昵称、用户标识、状态、余额、累计消耗、最近活跃与是否在线；支持关键词搜索、状态与在线筛选、三种排序与分页。 |
| FR-03 | 用户详情概览 | 展示昵称、用户标识与脱敏外部账号、注册时间、账号状态、邮箱、最近登录、积分更新时间；并以卡片展示可用余额、累计消耗、累计获得、在线会话数，冻结积分单独标注。 |
| FR-04 | 流水、用量与审计 | 流水按时间倒序分页展示类型、变动积分、变动后余额、备注与时间；用量按日展示请求数、消耗积分与 token 量，默认近 30 天；审计展示该用户的全部管理操作记录。 |
| FR-05 | 积分调整 | 支持按正负积分调整余额，单次额度不超过系统上限，原因必填且长度受限；调整后余额不得为负；成功后立即生成一条管理员类型的流水并写入审计，返回最新余额。 |
| FR-06 | 状态与强制下线 | 账号状态可在正常、受限、冻结等状态间切换，变更写入审计；会话列表展示设备、平台、状态与最近活跃，可对指定会话执行强制下线，被下线会话立即失效并记录审计与登录事件。 |

### 04 需求验收标准

| 编号 | 对应功能 | 验收条件 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | 登录与权限 | 密码错误无法登录，连续输错达阈值后账号被临时锁定；禁用账号无法登录；只读账号看不到写操作入口，直接调用写接口返回无权限。 |
| AC-02 | 概览与用户列表 | 概览六项指标与数据库统计一致；关键词搜索可命中昵称与用户标识；状态、在线筛选结果正确；三种排序生效；翻页后总数与页码一致，空结果有明确提示。 |
| AC-03 | 用户详情概览 | 详情展示的身份信息与列表、数据库一致；余额与流水最后一条的余额一致；累计消耗与累计获得满足“获得 − 消耗 = 余额”；外部账号仅显示脱敏结果。 |
| AC-04 | 流水、用量与审计 | 流水按时间倒序且可继续加载下一页；用量日期连续、无重复，合计与区间内消耗一致；审计列表按时间倒序，仅包含该用户的记录。 |
| AC-05 | 积分调整 | 未填原因或原因超长时无法提交；超出单次上限被拒绝；调整为负导致余额为负时被拒绝；成功后余额、流水与审计三处数据一致，流水备注与填写原因相同。 |
| AC-06 | 状态与强制下线 | 状态变更后列表与详情同步生效，受限账号后续请求按规则被拒绝；强制下线后目标会话立即失效并需重新登录；两类操作均在审计中记录操作人、对象、时间与来源地址。 |

### 1. User Account Center (User Profile Details Page) Requirements Document

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Version | v1.2 |
| Status | Pending review |
| Last updated | 2026-11-21 |

Provide a self-service account page inside the product: users can confirm their credit balance and its token equivalent, verify today's reward and 7-day progress, see where credits were spent, and manage signed-in devices and their nickname.

#### 01 Requirement Details

**Background and Problem.** The credit rules are already fixed: 500 credits on first sign-in, 100 credits granted automatically on the first sign-in of each calendar day, an extra 50 credits for every cumulative 7 days of check-ins, with no cap on issuance. The product currently provides no account-related page, so users cannot confirm whether today's reward has arrived, cannot see where their credits went, and have no self-service entry point for managing signed-in devices. This requirement therefore adds a user profile details page: clicking the user button opens an account panel where users can see their balance, today's reward and spending in one screen, and manage signed-in devices and their nickname.

#### 02 Solution Design

**Page Form and Information Architecture.** Add a user details entry point; clicking it opens an account panel over the workspace (the left rail stays, and 会话 returns to the workbench), organized top to bottom into five layers:

1. **Account overview**: avatar initial and nickname → available credits → token equivalent → total earned / total spent.
2. **Today's reward**: today's crediting status and +100 credits → 7-day progress (days 1–7) → days remaining until the 7-day reward.
3. **Credit ledger**: All / Earned / Spent filters, pagination and expandable spend details.
4. **Signed-in devices**: the current device and the sign-out action for the others.
5. **Footer**: Sign out (the workspace stays, and a custom model keeps working).

The page shows credits and tokens only, never any monetary amount. Daily rewards are granted automatically on sign-in; there is no check-in button.

#### 03 Requirement Specification

| ID | Feature | Rules and Results |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | Account overview | Show the avatar initial, nickname and available credits; token equivalent = credits × 40,000, rounded to the nearest ten thousand; show total earned and total spent. **No monetary amounts are displayed.** |
| FR-02 | Today's reward and 7-day progress | When granted today, show "Today's sign-in reward received: +100 credits"; otherwise show "Granted automatically after sign-in". The seven cells show the credits granted in order (day 1: 600, days 2–6: 100 each, day 7: +50), with today highlighted; show "N more consecutive days for the 7-day reward: +50 credits". |
| FR-03 | Credit ledger and usage details | Show entries in reverse chronological order with type, time, credit change and balance after the change; support All / Earned / Spent filters; clicking a model-call entry expands the model, input / cached / output tokens, duration and total tokens; support pagination (10 / 30 / 50 / 100 per page, page jump, current and total pages). |
| FR-04 | Signed-in device management | Show platform and sign-in time; the current device is marked "Current" and cannot be signed out; other devices can be signed out, which immediately revokes the session, removes it from the list and shows "Device signed out". Do not show IP, internal device ID or the full openid. |
| FR-05 | Nickname and sign-out | The nickname is editable (1–24 characters) and syncs to the panel header and the user button after saving; the footer "Sign out" clears the local account session and keeps the workspace, where a custom model keeps working. |

#### 04 Acceptance Criteria

| ID | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | Account overview | Available credits match the actual balance; the token equivalent equals credits × 40,000 with an error under 10,000; total earned and total spent satisfy "earned − spent = balance"; no ¥, yuan, price or cost wording appears anywhere on the page. |
| AC-02 | Today's reward and 7-day progress | When granted today, show "received +100 credits"; otherwise show "granted automatically after sign-in"; no check-in button exists; day 1 shows 600, days 2–6 show 100 and day 7 shows +50; today is highlighted and "N more consecutive days" matches the actual remaining days. |
| AC-03 | Credit ledger and usage details | Entries are in reverse chronological order and adjacent entries satisfy "previous balance + this change = this balance"; the Earned / Spent filters return correct results; expanding a spent entry shows the model, input/cached/output tokens, duration and total tokens, while earned entries cannot be expanded; the row count matches the page number after paging. |
| AC-04 | Signed-in device management | The current device is marked "Current" and has no sign-out button; signing out another device removes it from the list immediately with a notification; the next request from that device is rejected and requires signing in again. |
| AC-05 | Nickname and sign-out | After saving, the nickname syncs to the panel header and the user button and persists after refresh; an empty value cannot be saved and the input is capped at 24 characters; after signing out the local account session is cleared and the workspace stays, with a custom model still usable. |

### 2. User Management Console Requirements Document (Acceptance is out of scope for the ScienceDiscovery code repository)

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Version | v1.0 |
| Status | Pending review |
| Last updated | 2026-11-18 |

Provide operations and support teams with a console: search any user, review their credits and usage in full, and when necessary adjust credits, restrict accounts or force sign-out, with every action traceable.

#### 01 Requirement Details

**Background and Problem.** The user-facing account center solves "can users see it", but operations and support also need "can we find it and control it": when a user reports a credit anomaly, their ledger and usage must be checked; when abuse or account risk appears, the account must be restricted or sessions terminated; campaign compensation requires manual credit grants. There is currently no unified management entry point, so these actions can only be performed through direct database access, which is neither auditable nor safe from mistakes. This requirement therefore adds a user management console: starting from a user list, staff can open an individual user to review the account, ledger, usage and sessions, and perform permission-controlled management actions that require a reason.

#### 02 Solution Design

**Page Form and Information Architecture.** The console is a standalone site, separate from the user-facing account system, signed in with a username and password and accessible only to authorized accounts. It consists of two levels, a list page and a details page:

1. **Overview and user list**: the top shows total users, new users today, active users today, credits spent today, online sessions and frozen users; the list supports search by nickname or identifier, filtering by status and online state, sorting by balance, spending or last active, and pagination.
2. **User details**: the upper part shows identity and credit overview; the lower part contains four blocks — ledger, usage, sessions and operation audit.
3. **Management actions**: credit adjustments, account status changes and forced sign-out, all initiated from the details page with confirmation and a required reason.
4. **Traceability**: every write action records the operator, target, action, reason, time and source address, and can be queried in the user audit and the global audit.

Management actions and read-only viewing are separated by permission; read-only accounts cannot perform any write action.

#### 03 Requirement Specification

| ID | Feature | Rules and Results |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | Sign-in and permissions | A backend session is created after the username and password are verified; repeated failures beyond a threshold lock the account temporarily; disabled accounts are refused; sessions expire automatically; write actions are available only to accounts with operation permission. |
| FR-02 | Overview and user list | The overview shows total users, new users today, active users today, credits spent today, online sessions and frozen users; the list shows nickname, user identifier, status, balance, total spent, last active and online state; it supports keyword search, status and online filters, three sort orders and pagination. |
| FR-03 | User details overview | Show nickname, user identifier and masked external account, registration time, account status, email, last sign-in and credit update time; cards show available balance, total spent, total earned and online sessions, with frozen credits called out separately. |
| FR-04 | Ledger, usage and audit | The ledger shows type, credit change, balance after the change, remark and time in reverse chronological order with pagination; usage shows requests, credits spent and tokens per day for the last 30 days by default; the audit shows all management actions on that user. |
| FR-05 | Credit adjustment | Credits can be adjusted up or down, within a per-action system limit, with a required reason of limited length; the resulting balance may not be negative; on success an admin-type ledger entry is created immediately and an audit record is written, and the latest balance is returned. |
| FR-06 | Status and forced sign-out | Account status can be switched among normal, restricted, frozen and similar states, with the change written to the audit; the session list shows device, platform, state and last active, and a selected session can be forced offline, taking effect immediately and recording both an audit entry and a sign-in event. |

#### 04 Acceptance Criteria

| ID | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | Sign-in and permissions | A wrong password cannot sign in, and repeated failures beyond the threshold lock the account temporarily; disabled accounts cannot sign in; read-only accounts see no write entry points, and calling write APIs directly returns a permission error. |
| AC-02 | Overview and user list | The six overview metrics match database statistics; keyword search matches nickname and user identifier; status and online filters return correct results; all three sort orders work; after paging, the total and page number are consistent, and an empty result shows a clear message. |
| AC-03 | User details overview | Identity information on the details page matches the list and the database; the balance matches the balance of the latest ledger entry; total spent and total earned satisfy "earned − spent = balance"; the external account is shown only in masked form. |
| AC-04 | Ledger, usage and audit | The ledger is in reverse chronological order and further pages can be loaded; usage dates are continuous with no duplicates and the totals match spending in the period; the audit list is in reverse chronological order and contains only that user's records. |
| AC-05 | Credit adjustment | Submission is blocked when the reason is missing or too long; exceeding the per-action limit is rejected; an adjustment that would make the balance negative is rejected; after success the balance, ledger and audit are consistent, and the ledger remark equals the entered reason. |
| AC-06 | Status and forced sign-out | Status changes take effect immediately in both the list and the details page, and subsequent requests from a restricted account are rejected per the rules; after a forced sign-out the target session is invalidated immediately and the user must sign in again; both actions record the operator, target, time and source address in the audit. |
