closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] I understand that a report without environment details and a minimal reproduction is difficult to act on.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

In the desktop conversation view, while a run is active and the model is still planning ("Planning the next step"), the transcript visibly flickers. The flicker comes from an extra line appearing and disappearing just below the run line: the "Connecting to the local service…" strip.

Reproduction:

1. Open the desktop app on a session that has no pending configuration requests.
2. Send a prompt and wait until the assistant line reads "Planning the next step" (the model is thinking, before any answer or tool card).
3. Watch the transcript for several seconds.

Observed: every couple of seconds the "Connecting to the local service…" strip is inserted under the run line and then removed. The strip has padding and a bottom border, so each insertion changes the transcript height; the transcript's resize observer re-pins the scroll to the bottom, which reads as the whole conversation flashing.

Expected: the connecting strip belongs to the first read of a session's configuration data. Background re-reads during a live run must not draw it, so the transcript stays still while the model is planning.

Root cause (confirmed on the desktop source): `useConfigurationRequests` raised its `loading` state at the start of every `refresh()`. While a run is active the hook re-reads the configuration request list every two seconds (its poll) and again on every run-status or tool-status change (through the refresh key). With no configuration cards on the session, `Conversation` draws the "Connecting to the local service…" strip whenever `loading` is true and both request lists are empty, so each read blinked the strip in and out.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop (Windows x64 build).
- Observed on: Windows; the affected code path is platform-independent and reproduces in the desktop web view on other platforms as well.
- Requires an active run and a session with no pending configuration requests; no special model or provider is needed.

### Additional Information

A fix is proposed in pull request #1244: the first read of a session scope keeps the `loading` state that draws the strip, background reads are tracked separately for poll throttling, and a refresh that reads the same list paints nothing.

### Version Information

ScienceDiscovery desktop 0.3.0, Windows x64.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Desktop transcript flashes under "Planning the next step" while a run is active

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The streamed research-package pipeline landed in #1200 (`Closes #1152` stage 2). Its own review left six findings that are real and were deliberately **not** pushed onto the approved head, because a push there would dismiss both approvals. This issue tracks them as one focused follow-up, as #1152's design asks.

**F1 — the restore still holds a whole session's workspace objects.**
`services/api/src/http/index.ts:1619` charges memory as `max(largest object, records) + 256 MiB`, on the assumption that the restore reads one object at a time. The snapshot loops do (`research-snapshots.ts:943`, `:1016`), but the workspace restore does not: `const workspaceFiles = (source?.workspace ?? []).flatMap(...)` (`research-snapshots.ts:1074-1081`) calls `imported.objects.get(objectPath)` for **every** workspace file before the first write, and those buffers stay referenced through the loop at `:1091`. Peak memory is the sum of that session's workspace objects.
Reproduction: a package whose session carries several workspace objects totalling more than the heap (e.g. a 5 GiB workspace in a few files) on a host that passes the per-object check. The API OOMs mid-restore and the snapshot is left half written.
Fix: move the `get` into the write loop (or give `PackageObjectDirectory` a callback/streaming accessor), then the existing memory requirement is correct.

**F2 — the 5 GiB default reaches paths that still materialise the whole archive.**
`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:34` raises the default to 5 GiB, but the synchronous GET export route still calls `createResearchPackageAsync(input, sizeCap)` (`http/index.ts:1521`) and then copies the archive again for `response.end(Buffer.from(result.bytes))` (`:1530`), with no capacity check — the new export preflight guards only the `/exports` task route. The Web dialog uses that route and re-buffers the response (`apps/web/src/api/plugins.ts:69-87`, `ResearchPackageActions.tsx:221`), and the desktop save path does the same (`apps/desktop/src/api/research-package.ts:57`).
Measured: `createResearchPackageAsync` on a 256 MiB incompressible object peaks at 1375 MiB maxRSS in 7.1 s before the response copy. A 5 GiB payload needs an order of magnitude more than the 3072 MiB heap, so an export the cap allows OOMs the API instead of producing a file.
Fix: serve the GET route with `writeResearchPackage(input, response)` (or move the Web dialog to the `/exports` task plus a streamed download), charge that route with the export requirement, and only then keep the raised default.

**F3 — a write error during a streamed import kills the API process.**
`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:699` creates the object file with `createWriteStream(..., { flags: "wx" })` and attaches no `'error'` listener; the only handlers are `once(file, "drain")` inside a failed `write()` and the `file.end(cb)` callback. An open error, or a flush error after the last write, is emitted as an unhandled `'error'` event and terminates the process.
Reproduced: an object path that already exists prints `Unhandled 'error' event … EEXIST` and exits 1 before the import resolves; a write failing with EFBIG rejects the import **and** then exits 1 in the same run.
Fix: race the write loop against `new Promise((_, reject) => file.on("error", reject))` (or use `pipeline`), and destroy the stream in the catch.

**F5 — the restore's disk requirement misses the workspace and version writes.**
`services/api/src/research-package-preflight.ts:99` charges `unpacked * 2 + records` (snapshot objects and CAS blobs). The restore also writes every workspace file (`research-snapshots.ts:1091`) and one `VersionStore` blob per version object (`:1025`); for a package whose objects are workspace files — the normal shape — it writes up to `3 × unpacked`.
Their example: 12 GiB free, a 3.8 GiB package of workspace objects; the budget admits the parse, the post-parse check passes at `2 × 3.8` against 8.2 GiB, then the workspace writes need another 3.8 GiB and the volume fills mid-restore.
Fix: charge the workspace and version bytes (`3 × unpacked + records`), or lower `researchPackageUnpackBudget` to `free / 4`; add a workspace object to the budget/check pair case.

**F6 — trailing bytes after the tar terminator hang the import.**
`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:686` breaks on the first zero block, but the gzip pipeline keeps offering into `ChunkQueue`; once more than the 8 MiB high-water mark is queued the sink parks in `offer` with no consumer left to call `released()`, and `await conveying` (`:717`) waits forever.
Reproduced: a valid package plus 20 MiB of trailing zeros never resolves — still running after 6 s, no error.
Fix: after the zero block keep draining the decompressor to completion without parsing (or destroy and await the pipeline), and reject non-zero trailing bytes.

**F7 — a missing CAS blob fails the whole streaming export instead of being omitted.**
`services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:412` stores a lazy `open: () => provenanceRecorder.cas.stream(hash)` and never checks that the blob exists. The resident branch reads inside a `try` and turns a missing object into an `omissions` entry (`:595-596`, `:767-768`); with `streamObjects` the failure surfaces later inside the writer's hash pass and the export task ends failed, where it used to complete with an omission note.
Fix: verify the source when it is added (existence/stat) and push an omission, dropping it from the inventory, as the read path does.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` after #1200 merged; the findings were reported against head `c11690c0`.
- Node v22.23.4, pnpm workspace; `services/api` runs with `--max-old-space-size=3072` by default (`services/api/src/heap-budget.ts:23`).
- Reproductions above were run by the review bot against that head: the write-error exit, the 20 MiB trailing-data hang, the 256 MiB export peak (1375 MiB / 7.1 s) and the workspace-object memory sum.
- The 5 GiB-class round trip *is* bounded on the paths #1200 changed: 5100 MiB payload exported at 155 MiB peak and imported at 459 MiB peak in the PR's measurements. The gaps above are on routes and paths it did not convert.

### Additional Information

Deliberately not folded into #1200: those threads were left unresolved on an approved head, and any push there would dismiss both approvals. F1/F2/F3 are high severity; F5/F6/F7 are medium. F2 in particular means the raised default is only proven on the `/exports` task path, not on the synchronous GET route or the two clients — that limitation should stay visible until this is fixed.

### Version Information

`main` as of 2026-11-17, i.e. any build that contains #1200.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Streaming research-package import/export leaves memory and robustness gaps that the 5 GiB default exposes

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Idea Tree can prepare and run a research through the existing backend and is observable in the Web client, but the desktop app does not yet provide a complete way to inspect and control that research. We need the desktop experience first so a researcher can exercise the real backend, observe how the tree grows, inspect node assessments and pruning, and identify defects before deciding how the research algorithm should evolve.

The immediate goal is a complete, testable desktop journey: configure and start a research, observe its progress and tree, inspect the actual node contents, and control or reopen the research. The UI must display the backend's current behavior faithfully; it must not invent missing data or present model assessments as experimental results. Backend behavior remains subject to later verification and fixes discovered through this journey.

## Design Ideas

### 1. One cohesive desktop experience

Keep the desktop-facing work together in one substantive PR, including its necessary client integration and user-journey tests. Do not split cards, tree, node details, settings, and their wiring into separate small PRs.

Use the existing desktop **Evolve** experience as the primary visual and interaction reference: a recognizable conversation card opens a task-oriented side panel; the panel provides a readable interactive tree, selected-node detail, progress and controls. Reuse established visual language, layout, interaction patterns and genuinely shared components where appropriate. Idea Tree and Evolve have different data and semantics: do not force Idea Tree into Evolve's candidate/score model or fabricate an Evolve-style metric when the backend does not return it. Keep the existing Evolve experience intact, including sessions that contain both types of research.

The first desktop delivery should include:

- **Start and settings:** support the existing `/idea-tree <task>` / `/idea-tree-team <task>` agent-driven path, verify that it actually creates a research, and expose the supported Idea Tree settings needed to run a representative case. Surface prerequisites and actionable errors, including an unavailable Evolve service or missing model credentials. Do not add a separate research-creation form unless the existing path proves insufficient.
- **Conversation and panel:** show the session's research card(s), open the corresponding research in the task-oriented panel, and support multiple researches without mixing sessions or runs. Display backend-provided status, phase, round/batch progress, activities and token usage; explicitly show unavailable or unknown values.
- **Tree and node detail:** make parent/child relationships and direction versus candidate nodes visible. Allow users to select a node and inspect the available hypothesis, design, assessments, score, insight, status, priority, pruning reason and other returned details. Display absent scores or missing details as unavailable, never as zero or a successful result. Only show artifact/subagent actions when real references are returned.
- **Live control and recovery:** receive progress via the existing event stream, recover sensibly after a dropped connection, and support pause, continue and end with the backend's actual semantics. Reopening a session or restarting the app must show persisted state without automatically restarting research. Clearly report unavailable, interrupted and failed states.
- **Localization and usability:** provide Chinese and English text, accessible labels and responsive behavior. Include screenshots or recordings of the actual desktop UI in the implementation PR so the interaction can be reviewed.

The UI should make the existing search, leaf evaluation, insight propagation and pruning observable. It must not silently redefine these algorithms, assume that every direction has a score, or treat model estimates as measured scientific evidence.

### 2. Verify behavior and fix findings in a focused follow-up

Use the completed desktop journey to assess real capabilities and boundaries: command-to-research handoff, tree growth, node content, search selection and pruning, leaf evaluation, insight propagation, budgets, error handling and restart recovery. Record concrete expected/actual behavior and evidence, distinguish product defects from environment or model limitations, and align misleading documentation with verified behavior.

Group related backend, contract and regression fixes discovered by that validation into a focused follow-up PR when needed. Do not create a separate PR for every node action or UI component. If a small backend change is essential to make the first desktop journey usable, include it with that delivery and explain it. Changes to the research algorithm, such as a different definition of final leaves or scoring, require an explicit verified contract and are not assumed to be part of the initial UI adaptation.

## Involved Public APIs

Prefer existing APIs, verifying their current response and error contracts before relying on them:

- `GET` / `PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` for currently supported settings.
- `GET` / `POST /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` for the research list, details and lifecycle operations.
- `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research/:researchId/events` for live progress.
- `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph` for legacy read-only trees where applicable.
- `GET /api/evolve/status` for the current service prerequisite.
- Agent tools `create_idea_research` and `get_idea_research` for the existing handoff; these are distinct from the HTTP API.

Do not promise new or editable settings that the current public contract does not actually support. If a change is necessary, describe API compatibility, ownership and historical-data behavior in the implementing PR.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Desktop conversation, session workspace/task panel, Evolve UI patterns, settings, and Chinese/English text.
- Idea Tree research client, session-scoped APIs, SSE and persisted Python research state.
- Existing Agent/skill handoff, model configuration and Evolve service availability.
- Web Idea Tree as a behavior reference; desktop Evolve as the primary visual/interaction reference. Preserve both existing experiences.
- Documentation and tests: resolve the existing discrepancy between the chat-command documentation and the queued skill-based implementation using verified behavior.

## Test Design and Test Plan

This is a **proposed test plan, not a claim that these cases have passed**. Fix the target commit and verify the actual API contract before execution. Tree growth, pruning and other existing algorithm behavior are subjects of verification, not assumed changes in the initial desktop UI PR.

### Core desktop journey

Against an isolated real product stack, configure a model and service, start a research from the desktop, observe its card and task panel, open the tree and inspect direction/candidate nodes, then exercise pause, continue, end and reopening after an application restart. Assert user-visible outcomes and agreement with backend state, not just that clicks or requests occurred. Use a controllably slow model response to pause an in-flight call; use a separate unfinished research for the end scenario rather than treating an ended research as resumable.

### Test matrix

| ID | Scenario | Expected result and focus | Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| IT-01 | Save supported settings and start with each of `/idea-tree` and `/idea-tree-team` | A research belongs to the current session; settings survive reopening and the new research reflects the effective configuration; startup failures are visible. | Component, API, desktop E2E |
| IT-02 | Service unavailable, missing model credentials, or startup failure | Show an actionable cause and next step; do not show false running/success; retry works once the prerequisite is restored. | API, component, desktop E2E |
| IT-03 | Open a running research card and task panel | The correct research, phase, progress and available usage are visible and update with backend state; the card opens the matching panel. | Component, desktop E2E |
| IT-04 | Expand the tree and select root, direction and candidate nodes | Parent/child relationships and types are correct; show returned hypothesis, design, assessments, score, insight, priority and pruning reason. Missing values are unknown/unavailable, never zero or success. | Component, desktop E2E |
| IT-05 | Use controlled model outputs to grow a tree and trigger predictable pruning | Compare added nodes, parentage, search status and pruning reasons with backend state. Pruned nodes remain inspectable. Do not make nondeterministic model choices a fixed expectation. | Engine/API, mocked desktop journey |
| IT-06 | Observe candidate assessment and insight propagation to ancestors | Check returned stages, scores and ancestor summaries against the backend; never portray model scores as measured results. Verify the current contract where a candidate is a leaf when evaluated but may later grow children. | Engine/API, component |
| IT-07 | Pause while a model call is in flight, then continue | Show pausing before paused; continue from saved state after the call returns without presenting the retry as a separate research. | Engine/API, desktop E2E |
| IT-08 | End a separate unfinished research with confirmation; restart or reopen | Ended results remain visible and cannot continue. A previously running research is shown as interrupted when reported by the backend and is not automatically resumed or restarted. | Engine/API, desktop E2E |
| IT-09 | Disconnect and reconnect the event stream; also make the backend unavailable | Controlled reconnect or refresh recovers state; errors or stale state are visible; no duplicate research or loss of persisted results. | Client, component, desktop E2E |
| IT-10 | Multiple researches in one session, separate sessions, and Evolve in the same session | Cards, node data and controls remain scoped to the correct research/session; Evolve card, panel and operations continue to work. | API, component, desktop E2E |
| IT-11 | Empty tree; absent score, stages or pruning reason; unknown usage; partial or legacy data | No crash or fabricated values; show appropriate empty/unknown state; only offer artifact/subagent actions for real references; handle legacy trees according to the existing read-only contract. | Component, API |
| IT-12 | Window sizes, keyboard operation, and Chinese/English locales | Card, tree, details and controls remain visible, identifiable and operable; accessible names are correct and neither locale has missing text. | Component, desktop E2E, visual review |

### Mocked regression and real-model validation

- **Mocked regression:** use deterministic model responses and controlled events for success, pausing, failure, growth and pruning. Deliver the core journey with the initial UI PR and include the applicable cases in the project's gates.
- **Real model:** when a suitable model and stack are available, run at least one representative research and manually assess whether objective, constraints, materials, node contents, assessments and root summary are traceable and internally coherent. Record contradictions, omissions and unsupported conclusions. Do not require an exact node count, wording or score; scientific validity requires independent judgment.
- If a real model or desktop environment is unavailable, mark the journey **BLOCKED**. Mocked results, collection and skipped cases are not real-run passes.

### Evidence and reporting

Record target commit, environment, startup/test commands, model or fixture, numbered user steps, expected/actual outcomes, key screenshots or logs, failure attribution, and discovered/executed/passed/failed/skipped or blocked counts. The UI PR includes desktop evidence. Run applicable desktop typecheck/test/build, `pnpm ci:l1`, and required UT/ST/E2E gates; group related backend fixes and regression tests in a focused follow-up rather than making one PR per case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A user can configure the settings the API actually accepts (`templateId`, `explorationIntensity`, `maxTokens`, `maxTokensPerCall`, `maxDepth`, `maxNodes`, `scoreDirection`, the three prompt overrides and `roleThinkingEfforts`) and start a real backend Idea Tree research from the desktop conversation; missing prerequisites or startup failures are actionable. Settings the API no longer accepts - the rounds / candidates / assessor-weight fields #49 retired - are neither rendered nor written.
- [ ] A session research card opens a desktop task-oriented view consistent with the existing Evolve experience, while preserving Evolve functionality when both are present.
- [ ] The tree, node relationships, backend-provided contents, assessments, search/pruning state and reasons can be inspected interactively. Missing or unknown data is represented honestly.
- [ ] Progress updates, pause, continue, end and restart/reopen behavior reflect the backend; reopening does not automatically restart a research.
- [ ] Multiple researches and sessions remain correctly associated; historical or legacy data is handled according to the existing contract.
- [ ] Chinese/English UI and relevant automated checks pass; the PR includes desktop UI evidence and an end-to-end journey result or an explicitly described blocker.
- [ ] A recorded validation identifies capability boundaries, observed defects and unresolved contract questions; related fixes are grouped into a focused follow-up when needed.

## Additional Information

Implementation baseline: main `955902e499672f7835a274404dca88f50e378bbb` when this plan was written. The current autonomous engine runs in the Evolve Python service and independently advances research after the Agent handoff. Existing Web and backend tests are useful starting points, not proof that the new desktop journey or real-model behavior has already been validated.

closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

### Summary

Creating, deleting, or testing a custom MCP server can block until ScienceDiscovery refreshes the full custom MCP catalog. Since catalog refresh connects to every enabled custom server and waits for the slowest connector, one unrelated unhealthy streamable HTTP MCP server can make `/api/mcp/servers` exceed the caller timeout.

This can leave ScienceDiscovery in an inconsistent state:

1. A client sends `POST /api/mcp/servers`.
2. ScienceDiscovery persists the new server.
3. ScienceDiscovery starts a synchronous full catalog refresh.
4. An unrelated old connector waits until the MCP connection timeout.
5. The client times out before ScienceDiscovery returns the created server.
6. The new server was already persisted, so a later retry can create another orphan connector.

Repeated retries can therefore accumulate invalid custom MCP servers and make later saves slower or more likely to fail.

### Environment

- ScienceDiscovery version: `0.3.0` packaged binary, Linux x86_64
- Also reproducible in the source tree around commit `5058334f`
- Deployment mode: `ScienceDiscovery serve`
- Custom MCP transport: streamable HTTP
- Multiple enabled custom MCP servers were configured
- The API caller used a 10-second request timeout

### Observed behavior

In one production-like case:

- There were 7 enabled custom MCP connectors.
- 6 connectors were stale or invalid.
- Most invalid connectors returned an authentication/authorization error quickly.
- One connector waited until the MCP connection timeout.
- The full catalog refresh took about 10 seconds.
- The caller timed out first.
- The new connector had already been persisted on the ScienceDiscovery side.

Relevant sanitized log pattern:

```text
INFO  event=mcp_connection_started
      reason=initial
      serverId=custom-xxxxxxxxxxxx
      transport=http
      endpointHost=<redacted>
      endpointProtocol=https

ERROR event=mcp_connection_failed
      reason=initial
      serverId=custom-xxxxxxxxxxxx
      transport=http
      durationMs=10003
      errorMessage="MCP connection timeout"

WARN  event=mcp_catalog_server_failed
      errorMessage="MCP connection timeout"
      serverId=custom-xxxxxxxxxxxx

INFO  event=mcp_catalog_loaded
      durationMs=10003
      failedServerCount=6
      serverCount=7
      toolCount=14
```

The external caller then received a transport timeout, but a subsequent `GET /api/mcp/servers` showed that the newly created server had already been stored.

### Reproduction

A deterministic reproduction can be built with two custom streamable HTTP servers:

1. Configure `slow-server` as an enabled custom HTTP MCP server whose initialize request does not complete within the configured client timeout.
2. Configure or create another server, for example `new-server`, through the API:

   ```http
   POST /api/mcp/servers
   Content-Type: application/json
   Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
   ```

   Example body shape:

   ```json
   {
     "name": "new-server",
     "description": "temporary test server",
     "transport": "http",
     "url": "http://<redacted>/mcp",
     "enabled": true,
     "authMode": "headers",
     "headers": {
       "X-Example-Header": "<redacted>"
     },
     "timeoutSeconds": 60
   }
   ```

3. Observe that the `POST` does not return after persisting the new server. Instead, it waits for the full catalog refresh, including `slow-server`.

4. Abort the client after its own timeout.

5. Query the server list again:

   ```http
   GET /api/mcp/servers
   ```

   The newly created server may still be present even though the client never received a successful creation response.

The same coupling also affects testing one selected server:

```http
POST /api/mcp/servers/<id>/test
```

A selected-server test can end up waiting for unrelated servers through the full catalog refresh path.

### Expected behavior

- `POST /api/mcp/servers` should persist and register the new server, then return promptly.
- `PUT /api/mcp/servers/<id>` should persist the update, then return promptly.
- `DELETE /api/mcp/servers/<id>` should persist deletion, remove in-memory state, and return promptly.
- Full catalog refresh should run in the background.
- One unhealthy MCP server should not block configuration changes for unrelated servers.
- `POST /api/mcp/servers/<id>/test` should probe only the selected server.
- A background refresh failure should mark that server unhealthy without delaying unrelated mutations.
- The effective proxy policy for the selected connector should be used by the selected-server test.
- Logs should identify the failing server and refresh duration without exposing credentials or authenticated URLs.

### Current implementation notes

In `services/api/src/mcp/custom-servers.ts`:

- `save()` persists the server and then awaits a full refresh.
- `remove()` persists deletion and then awaits a full refresh.
- `test()` probes the selected server and can then await another full refresh for enabled servers.

In `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts`, the custom MCP refresh callback uses `mcpCatalog.refresh()` rather than reload semantics that also recompute per-server proxy mappings.

Consequences:

- Mutation latency is coupled to the slowest enabled connector.
- Selected-connector tests can wait on unrelated connectors.
- Newly registered connectors may not receive the same effective proxy policy as the global catalog reload path.
- Client timeouts after persistence can leave orphan connectors.

### Suggested direction

A possible fix is to separate mutation persistence from catalog discovery:

1. `save()`:
   - validate;
   - persist atomically;
   - update the in-memory registry;
   - return promptly;
   - do not synchronously probe or refresh the full catalog.

2. `remove()`:
   - persist deletion;
   - remove registry/check state;
   - schedule a background reload.

3. `test()`:
   - probe only the selected server;
   - use that server's effective proxy policy;
   - update only that server's health/tool cache;
   - schedule a background reload after returning.

4. Background refresh:
   - use reload semantics so per-server proxy mappings are recomputed;
   - log per-server failures;
   - never block mutation requests.

With this separation, a previously timing-out selected connector test completed in about 0.25 seconds and discovered 14 tools once the unrelated full-refresh dependency was removed.

### Suggested regression tests

- Saving a custom MCP server does not await the full catalog refresh.
- Deleting a custom MCP server does not await the full catalog refresh.
- Testing one selected server does not connect to unrelated custom servers.
- A slow or unavailable unrelated server does not delay creation/update/deletion of another server.
- A selected-server test uses the effective proxy policy for that server.
- Background refresh failure marks only the failing server unhealthy.
- A client disconnect after persistence does not cause duplicate servers on retry without an explicit recovery mechanism.

### Workarounds

Temporary workarounds only:

- Manually remove stale custom MCP servers.
- Restart ScienceDiscovery after cleanup.
- Increase the caller timeout.

These do not address the root cause because the next unhealthy connector can again block unrelated configuration operations.

### Additional context

This was observed while integrating an external agent platform with a local ScienceDiscovery instance. The external platform had its own timeout/error-handling issue, but the ScienceDiscovery-side root cause is that custom MCP mutation requests synchronously wait for a full catalog refresh.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

### Detailed environment information

#### Product and build

- Product: ScienceDiscovery
- Reproduced with: packaged standalone binary
- Version: `ScienceDiscovery 0.3.0 (linux-x86_64)`
- Bundled Node.js: `v22.19.0`
- Bundled Python: `3.12.13`
- Bundled micromamba: `2.8.1-0`
- Payload cache ID: `bd9c1e9a20e491d23a05356e1ba73907`
- Source inspection revision: `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74`
  - The relevant synchronous custom-MCP refresh behavior was present at this revision.

#### Host operating system

- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS Jammy Jellyfish
- Kernel: `6.8.0-111-generic #111~22.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC x86_64`
- Architecture: `x86_64`
- Locale/encoding: UTF-8
- Deployment type: bare metal, not a VM or container
- Virtualization extensions are available on the CPU, but no VM was used for this reproduction.

#### Hardware

- CPU: Intel Core i7-14700K
- CPU threads: 28
- RAM: 125 GiB total, about 80 GiB available during the test
- Swap: 2 GiB
- Storage: local NVMe SSD
- Root filesystem: ext4
- Free space during reproduction: about 1.3 TiB
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti
- NVIDIA driver: `580.142`
- GPU acceleration was not involved in this code path.
- Network adapter: Intel Ethernet Connection I219-LM
- Network kernel driver/module: `e1000e`

#### ScienceDiscovery runtime and dependencies

- Startup mode: `ScienceDiscovery serve`
- Public API port used in the reproduction: local port `4310`
- Data directory: a local directory on the same ext4 filesystem
- Data directory path is omitted for privacy.
- Local sandbox provider: bubblewrap
- `bwrap` version: `0.6.1`
- `bwrap` reports that this version does not support the newer `--disable-userns` option. This warning was present, but it is unrelated to the custom HTTP MCP catalog refresh issue.
- `uv` version used in the source-mode environment: `0.11.15`
- Source-mode Node.js: `v22.22.1`
- Source-mode pnpm: `10.28.2`
- Source-mode npm: `10.9.4`
- JiuwenSwarm execution backend was enabled.
- The issue is in the custom streamable HTTP MCP configuration/catalog path, not in a stdio MCP subprocess.

#### Custom MCP configuration

- Transport: custom streamable HTTP MCP servers
- Number of enabled custom MCP connectors during the problematic observation: 7
- Roughly 6 connectors were stale or had invalid/expired credentials.
- One connector remained healthy.
- One unrelated stale connector waited until the approximately 10-second MCP connection timeout.
- Custom connector `timeoutSeconds` was configured as `60`.
- The external API caller used a 10-second HTTP timeout.
- Authentication details, endpoint URLs, header names, and credential values are intentionally omitted.

#### Relevant service state

- ScienceDiscovery API health before the operation: healthy
- Local runner health: healthy
- Memory graph was disabled in this deployment.
- The custom MCP catalog refresh was triggered by a create/update/delete operation on an unrelated custom MCP server.
- The slow connector was already configured before the new connector was submitted.
- No GPU, driver, storage-full, or insufficient-memory condition contributed to the timeout.
- The machine and ScienceDiscovery process remained responsive while the HTTP mutation request was blocked.

#### Reproduction consistency

- The behavior was reproducible while at least one enabled custom HTTP MCP connector failed slowly or reached the MCP connection timeout.
- The behavior disappeared after stale connectors were removed.
- The behavior also disappeared after full catalog refresh was moved off the mutation request path in a local diagnostic patch.
- This indicates that the timeout is caused by synchronous full-catalog refresh, not by the host running out of resources.

### Additional Information

_No response_

### Version Information

ScienceDiscovery 0.3.0 (linux-x86_64)
Bundled Node.js: v22.19.0
Bundled Python: 3.12.13
Bundled micromamba: 2.8.1-0
Payload cache ID: bd9c1e9a20e491d23a05356e1ba73907
Source revision inspected: 5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version (confirmed by inspecting current upstream main).
- [x] I have included the available environment information and a minimal reproduction scenario below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A model rate-limit error interrupted an Idea Tree research task during use on November 18, 2026. A temporary provider limit should allow the current model request to resume after a delay, without requiring the user to manually continue the research.

**Actual behavior:** HTTP 429 is not retried by the Idea Tree research transport. It raises an exception immediately, and the research engine records the task as `interrupted`.

**Expected behavior:** Retry transient HTTP 429 responses with bounded backoff, honoring the provider's retry delay when available. Keep completed research stages and the current task alive while waiting. The wait must respect pause/cancel and execution budgets. If the retry budget is exhausted or the error represents a permanent quota/configuration problem, report a clear interruption reason.

**Minimal reproduction scenario (deterministic fault injection):**

1. Start an Idea Tree research task with a configured model.
2. Make the model endpoint return HTTP 429 for one stage request, then return a valid successful completion on the next request. For example, use this first response:

   ```http
   HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
   Content-Type: application/json
   Retry-After: 1

   {"error":{"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Too many requests; retry shortly"}}
   ```

3. Observe that the research becomes `interrupted` on the first response, rather than waiting and issuing the next request.

This response is a proposed reproduction fixture, not a captured production response. The original provider error body and full traceback are unavailable; the user reported a model rate-limit failure. The deterministic scenario was established by code inspection and has not been executed in this report.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Affected component: Idea Tree research service in the Python Evolve sidecar, using the API's internal Evolve LLM proxy.
- Call path: `createIdeaResearchClient` → `/internal/evolve-llm/:researchId/v1/chat/completions` → `handleEvolveCompletion` → `completeChatRequest(..., streamUpstream=true)`; retry ownership remains with the Python research transport.
- The original deployment version, model/provider, client, OS, and runtime versions were not captured. The control flow described here is present in the upstream source revision below.

### Additional Information

The retry gap is specific to this call path:

- [Idea Tree transport](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e/services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py#L179-L201) makes at most two attempts, but only retries `error.code >= 500`, immediately. A 429 goes directly to `RuntimeError`.
- [Research engine exception handling](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e/services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py#L569-L578) changes the research status to `interrupted` for an unhandled failure.
- [The shared completion adapter](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e/packages/model/src/completion.ts#L79-L88) explicitly sets `maxRetries: 0` for this path because the sidecar owns retry and budget decisions. Increasing `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES` therefore does not fix Idea Tree research.
- The ordinary Agent model client already retries HTTP 429 and 5xx by default, which makes the research service's behavior inconsistent.

Suggested regression coverage: a transient 429 followed by success continues the same research stage; repeated 429s terminate after a bounded budget; completed stages are preserved; pause/cancel interrupts a backoff wait. Retry delay metadata must reach whichever layer owns the retry.

### Version Information

- Latest upstream main inspected: `eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e` (fetched on November 18, 2026).
- The affected transport and completion code also match the local revision where this behavior was investigated.

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

On a Chinese Windows host, an Idea Tree research can be created and read back one at a time, but **listing** the session's researches fails with a GBK decode error, so the desktop Idea Tree card never renders. The asymmetry is a decoding bug, not a missing record.

Observed in a real journey (measured by PR-bot-2号 while validating #1169 on this machine): `/idea-tree` handed off successfully and created `research-5e8c3f04…`; a `get` for that research returned a healthy state — `status: running`, `phase: aggregate`, `round: 1`, `268290` tokens, 13 nodes and 12 edges. The very next list call returned an error instead:

```
GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research
{"error":"'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position …"}
```

`get` works, `list` fails, for the same research.

**Why the two disagree — verified in the code on main `eb5f66e8`:**

| Path | Code | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Write | `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:106` opens the checkpoint with `encoding='utf-8'`, and `:109` dumps with `ensure_ascii=False` | state files legitimately contain raw non-ASCII bytes |
| Single read | `research.py:129` — `json.loads(self.path(...).read_text())` — **no `encoding=`** | `Path.read_text()` falls back to the locale default (cp936/GBK on a Chinese Windows host) |
| List read | `research.py:133` — `json.loads(p.read_text())` for every `*.json` in the directory — **no `encoding=`** | same locale-default decode |
| `get` dispatch | `research_service.py:88-95` `state_for()`: a research that is `_running` returns the **in-memory** state; only a non-running one falls back to `store().read()` | a running research's `get` never decodes the file, so it succeeds |
| `list` dispatch | `research_service.py:148-149` always calls `store().list(...)` | always decodes every file on disk |

So the failure is exactly where the report put it: the Python side decodes a UTF-8 checkpoint with the platform default encoding. `0x80` is a UTF-8 continuation byte, which GBK cannot decode — the error names the codec the interpreter chose, not anything the file did wrong.

**This also predicts a second failure the report did not reach:** once a research is no longer in memory (paused, completed, or after the service restarts), `get` takes the `store().read()` branch and will fail the same way — i.e. every non-ASCII research becomes unreadable after a restart, not just unlistable.

Minimal reproduction (Chinese Windows, non-UTF-8 default encoding):

1. Start the stack on a host whose `locale.getpreferredencoding()` is `cp936` (a default Chinese Windows install; no `PYTHONUTF8=1`).
2. Create a research through `/idea-tree <objective>` where the objective or a node hypothesis contains non-ASCII text (Chinese is enough), and let it reach `running`.
3. `GET /api/sessions/{projectId}/idea-tree/research/{researchId}` (via `POST {"operation":"get","researchId":…}`) → returns the state.
4. `GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/idea-tree/research` → `{"error":"'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position …"}`.

Impact: the desktop Idea Tree card renders nothing at all (the list is what it reads), while the research keeps running and spending tokens; the same decode path breaks `get` for any research that is not currently in memory. This is a blocker for #1169 (desktop Idea Tree adaptation).

## Detailed Environment Information Description

| | |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Chinese Windows 11 (system locale cp936 / GBK; `PYTHONUTF8` not set) |
| Python | 3.12 (the evolve service's own venv) — `Path.read_text()` defaults to the locale encoding here |
| Engine | Idea Tree Python research loop inside the evolve service (`services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/`) |
| State location | `$SCIENCE_AGENT_DATA_DIR/idea-research/<projectId>/<sessionId>/<researchId>.json` (UTF-8, `ensure_ascii=False`) |
| Client | Desktop 0.4.0 (Idea Tree card), API route `services/api/src/http/index.ts` (`/idea-tree/research`) |
| Observed research | `research-5e8c3f04…`, status `running`, phase `aggregate`, round 1, 268 290 tokens, 13 nodes / 12 edges |
| Failing call | `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` |

## Additional Information

Suggested fix (small, local to the engine):

- Pass `encoding='utf-8'` explicitly in `research.py:129` and `research.py:133`, and sweep the rest of `vendor/idea_tree` for `read_text()` / `open()` without an encoding (`idea_tree_service.py:33` writes through a file object and `:49` reads with `read_text()` — same class of defect for the legacy tree store).
- A regression test that does not depend on the host locale: write a checkpoint containing non-ASCII text through the UTF-8 writer, then force the default encoding (for example `monkeypatch.setattr(locale, "getpreferredencoding", lambda **_kw: "cp936")`, or run the helper with `PYTHONUTF8=0` and a `cp936` locale) and assert that both `read()` and `list()` return the non-ASCII content intact.
- Optional hardening: fail loudly in one place (a single `load_state(path)` helper used by both readers) instead of two ad-hoc `read_text()` calls.

The measurement above (research id, counters, error text) comes from PR-bot-2号's real run on this host; the code pointers and the `get`/`list` dispatch explanation were verified against `main` `eb5f66e8` before filing.

## Version Information

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Commit | `eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e` ("fix(mac-release): only the updater-contract blockmap name passes 5f") |
| Desktop shell | `sd-shell` 0.4.0 (`application/package.json`) |
| Engine files | `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:106,129,133`; `research_service.py:88-95,148-149` |
| Python | 3.12 (evolve service venv) |

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Users need a research session exported to a `.sdresearch` package and imported again to retain its Evolve history. In a Windows desktop test, after exporting a session with a completed Evolve search, importing it and choosing to continue the research, the conversation no longer showed the interactive Evolve card or the task panel containing the optimization results.

This request covers the complete user-facing preservation and acceptance of Evolve history across export, import and creation of a writable research continuation. Related: #1019 addressed the earlier absence of Evolve run records in research packages; #1060 and #1136 added run/event and candidate-source packaging. Draft PR #1176 addresses run-ID collisions during import and continuation; its desktop journey and full validation remain outstanding.

## Design Ideas

- Carry each selected session's Evolve runs, configuration, budget, status, events, candidate tree, scores, best result and available candidate source content in the package, for both supported export levels.
- Restore each run under the correct imported session. Repeated imports, importing on the source machine, and creating a writable continuation must produce independent, correctly associated records without overwriting another session's runs or mixing candidates.
- In both the read-only imported snapshot and the writable continuation, show the Evolve card and allow it to open the desktop task panel. Preserve the optimization tree, budget and results, node selection, candidate details and available source/diff views.
- Preserve multiple runs and their ownership. Report missing or omitted run data, events or candidate sources explicitly, while keeping the rest of the session usable. Older packages cannot recover data they never contained.
- Do not automatically restart a search when importing or viewing it. An in-flight search cannot continue on the target merely from a historical snapshot: present a truthful historical/terminal state and retain available partial results. Access to a still-running source session remains a separate live status, not an imported live execution.
- Re-running a search or achieving identical scientific results in another environment is outside this request.

## Involved Public APIs

Prefer the existing session export/import and research-continuation APIs and the Evolve run-list, event and candidate-source read APIs. Verify their behavior with remapped run IDs and session ownership; document any necessary additive contract or compatibility changes. Import must not execute package contents.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

Research package serialization, validation, import and continuation; Evolve run/event storage and candidate source storage; session ownership and ID mapping; desktop conversation cards, task panel, tree and node inspector. Preserve compatibility with old packages and sessions without Evolve.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- Add regression coverage for completed, stopped, failed and in-flight searches, multiple runs, missing candidate sources, malformed package data and sessions without Evolve.
- Export and import on the source machine and a fresh data directory; repeat the import and create a writable continuation. Check independent ownership, run identifiers, event order, budgets, scores, candidate content, and absence of automatic execution.
- Exercise the actual Windows desktop user journey: complete a search → export → import → open the card and task panel → inspect tree nodes and source/diff → continue research → repeat the inspection. Also verify the imported snapshot remains read-only and the new session supports chat.
- Run the applicable unit, system and mocked E2E gates (`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e`) and report counts; distinguish blocked environment checks from passing results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After export and import, each Evolve run is associated with the right session and its interactive card opens the task panel, including optimization results, tree, budgets, scores and available node details and source/diff.
- [ ] Creating a writable research continuation preserves the same available Evolve history and allows subsequent chat; the imported snapshot stays read-only.
- [ ] Same-machine import, repeated import and multiple Evolve runs retain independent, correctly associated records without overwriting the original or mixing sources.
- [ ] Stopped, failed and previously running searches display truthful status and available partial data; viewing or importing never starts a new search.
- [ ] Missing or omitted data and limitations of older packages are reported explicitly, and the rest of the session remains usable.
- [ ] Relevant automated regression and Windows desktop user-journey checks pass, with command results and any remaining limitations recorded.

## Additional Information

The requested behavior is preservation and inspection of recorded Evolve results, not deterministic reproduction or automatic resumption. PR #1176 is a draft and must not be treated as full desktop validation.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Preserve interactive Evolve history when exporting and continuing a session

### 🚀 Background Description

Starting a new conversation should not require selecting the same model again. Related: #462 requests remembered model selection, including persistence across restarts; this request tracks the same behavior alongside #1204.

### Design Ideas

Initialize each newly created conversation with the last model explicitly selected by the user, including after an application restart. A later selection becomes the default for subsequent new conversations. Existing conversations that already have messages keep their own model selection; reopening one must not change it or count as a new selection. Persist the last selection across application restarts.

### Involved Public APIs

Determine whether API changes are needed; preserve existing model selection and execution behavior for existing conversations.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

Conversation model picker, new-session initialization, model configuration and session settings. Coordinate the inheritance behavior with permission-mode request #1204.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Select model B, create a conversation and verify B is selected; restart the application and verify another new conversation still uses B. Select C and verify the next new conversation uses C. Reopen an existing conversation with messages and verify its own model remains unchanged. Verify behavior when the remembered model is no longer available and that the displayed model matches the effective selection.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new conversation defaults to the last explicitly selected model including after an application restart.
- [ ] A later model selection is used by subsequently created conversations.
- [ ] Conversations that already have messages retain their own model; reopening one does not change the remembered selection.
- [ ] An unavailable remembered model does not leave a dangling selection; use a valid default or provide actionable feedback.
- [ ] Relevant automated tests and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.

### Additional Information

Related issue: #462. Coordinate implementation and validation with the broader acceptance criteria in that issue.

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A packaging run discovers that the JiuwenSwarm virtualenv no longer matches the swarm patch set **only at the very end of `assemble`**, after the payload has already been copied and precompiled. The failure itself is correct and actionable, but it arrives ~13 minutes in, so every attempt at a packaging run that touches a dependency-carrying patch pays that cost again.

Observed on `main` at `b2075e4972a5af90804fdd579ee314bfa502be46` (2026-11-18), running the Windows installer chain:

```
[08:09:41] assemble payload
[08:22:20] assemble exit=1 elapsed=759s
[assemble] verifying payload imports (self-check)
[assemble] payload import OK: jiuwenswarm venv
[assemble] payload import OK: sd-services venv
[assemble] FAIL: payload greenlet check FAILED: 3.5.0 is below 3.5.5. Windows wheels 3.3.1..3.5.4
           dynamically link MSVC P140.dll (VC++ x64 redistributable) and fail on clean machines.
           Re-run scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup (or bash scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup) with the
           greenlet>=3.5.5 patch, then rebuild.
```

The gate is at `application/scripts/assemble-backend.mjs:1051-1077` (`greenletVersionAtLeast`, then `greenletRuntimeProblem`), which runs inside the "verifying payload imports" stage — after the backend tree, the venv templates, micromamba and the bytecode precompile have all been written. The preceding work in that same run was `[assemble] copying micromamba`, `precompiled bytecode for …` and so on, i.e. several minutes of payload writing that a check made at the start would have refused in seconds.

Why the venv was stale: patch `0021-greenlet-static-runtime.patch` (added with the macOS adaptation work) rewrites `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` to require `greenlet>=3.5.5`, but applying swarm patches only touches the source tree. Nothing in the packaging entry point re-syncs the venv, so a machine that had a working venv from before that patch keeps `greenlet 3.5.0` until someone runs `node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup` by hand. After doing exactly that (`greenlet 3.5.5`, native `_greenlet` import verified), the same commit assembled in 835 s and the installer built.

Minimal reproduction, no hand-editing of the repository:

```powershell
# 1. a checkout whose jw venv predates the greenlet>=3.5.5 patch
node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup            # once, from an older main
git switch main && git pull                   # brings 0021-greenlet-static-runtime.patch
# (applying patches / building is enough; the venv is NOT re-synced by the packaging chain)

# 2. package, and watch where the greenlet refusal arrives
pnpm --dir application dist
# -> payload greenlet check FAILED: 3.5.0 is below 3.5.5, after the payload has been written
```

Impact: anyone packaging the Windows desktop app against a main whose swarm patch set changed its dependencies loses a full payload assembly per attempt, and the same waste applies to the CI Windows job. The message is good; the timing is not.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

| | |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Microsoft Windows 11 家庭版 10.0.26200 (build 26200) |
| Node / pnpm | v22.23.4 / 11.1.2 |
| Desktop shell | `application/` (sd-shell 0.4.0), electron-builder 26 |
| JiuwenSwarm venv | `%REPO%\.sciencediscovery-data\jiuwenswarm\src\.venv` (CPython 3.12.16) |
| Stale package | greenlet 3.5.0 (required by patch `0021-greenlet-static-runtime.patch`: `>=3.5.5,<4`) |
| Command | the Windows installer chain through `pnpm --dir application assemble --expect-runner-sea` |

## Additional Information

Suggested change (small, no behaviour change for a correct tree): make the venv/patch consistency check a **preflight** of `assemble`, run before the payload is copied. Two ways:

1. Move the greenlet gate (and any other "venv must match the patch set" assertion) to the start of `assemble-backend.mjs`, keeping the existing end-of-run gate as a second line of defence.
2. Or have `assemble` compare the patch set's `uv.lock` requirement for `greenlet` (and the pinned versions it cares about) against the venv's installed version, and `fail()` with the same message before any copy when they disagree.

Either way the observable contract is: **a stale venv costs seconds, not a payload assembly**, and the failure names `node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup` as the fix (it already does).

Related: the same class of skew exists for any future dependency-carrying patch (`0018-desktop-slim-deps`, `0019-align-workspace-versions`, `0021-greenlet-static-runtime` all rewrite `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`), so a check driven by "does the venv satisfy the patched lockfile" is preferable to a greenlet-specific one.

A local workaround exists on the packaging side (re-apply patches, then run `jiuwenswarm.mjs setup` whenever a dependency-carrying patch changed), but the repository's own `assemble` remains the place where a packager should learn about it quickly.

## Version Information

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Commit | `b2075e4972a5af90804fdd579ee314bfa502be46` ("fix(ci): stabilize nightly research and Windows package gate") |
| Patch that introduced the requirement | `0021-greenlet-static-runtime.patch` |
| Desktop shell | `sd-shell` 0.4.0 |
| Node | v22.23.4 |
| JiuwenSwarm venv | greenlet 3.5.0 before the fix, 3.5.5 after `node scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs setup` |
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: assemble discovers a stale JiuwenSwarm venv only after the whole payload is written, so a dependency-carrying patch costs ~13 minutes per attempt

### 🚀 Background Description

The permission mode is currently tucked inside the conversation composer settings, making it inconvenient to see and change. Make the active mode visible and accessible directly in the composer.

### Design Ideas

Place a compact permission selector after the + and settings buttons. When closed, show an icon and a short label:
- Request approval / 请求批准: a shield with a check mark.
- Full access / 完全访问: a shield with an exclamation mark and red text.

Clicking the selector opens a popover for choosing the mode, with a short explanation of each permission scope in smaller text; the existing scope descriptions can be retained. Provide both Chinese and English UI text.

A newly created conversation should default to the last permission mode selected by the user, including after an application restart. This inheritance applies only to new conversations: do not change the saved permission mode of conversations that already have messages. Keep each existing conversation's own setting when reopened. Persist the last selection across application restarts.

### Involved Public APIs

Determine whether an API change is needed; preserve existing permission enforcement and mode meanings.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

Conversation composer, new-session initialization, session settings, localization, and permission enforcement.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Verify the selector and popover in Chinese and English, including icons, red full-access text, labels and scope descriptions. Select each mode and create a new conversation and verify it inherits the last choice, both before and after an application restart. Reopen conversations with existing messages and verify their prior modes remain unchanged after selections elsewhere. Verify existing permission enforcement.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The closed composer selector appears after the + and settings buttons and shows the active mode using the specified shield icon and concise label; full-access text is red.
- [ ] Clicking it opens a choice popover with the existing permission-scope explanations in smaller text.
- [ ] Chinese and English interfaces present the selector and explanations correctly.
- [ ] New conversations inherit the last selected mode including after an application restart.
- [ ] Conversations that already have messages retain their own permission mode when other conversations change the selection.
- [ ] Existing permission enforcement remains unchanged; relevant automated tests and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.

### Additional Information

Inheritance must not retroactively modify existing conversations with messages.

closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Session research packages (`.sdresearch`) can contain datasets, artifacts, logs and trajectories. The current main-branch implementation limits the uncompressed archive to 512 MiB and the compressed import upload to 256 MiB. Consequently, an export containing incompressible data can succeed but produce a package that the same application cannot import.

PR #1173 is the baseline for this issue: **assume its changes are merged when implementing the remaining work**. At the time of this update it is still open, so its behavior should not be represented as already present on main. It unifies the configured warning threshold, raises the compressed upload bound to cover the hard archive ceiling, adds preview information and confirmation, and keeps a 1 GiB uncompressed hard ceiling. It does not establish that multi-GiB packages work safely end to end.

This issue tracks the remaining user outcomes: make the threshold and hard ceiling honest and understandable, verify that allowed exports can be imported, and then support larger packages without loading entire packages into memory. Deliver these in stages; do not wait for multi-GiB support to correct an earlier round-trip or user-facing defect.

## Design Ideas

### Stage 1: Complete the reliable round trip and limit experience

- Treat the configured export threshold as a **warning threshold**. Above it, explain the time and memory costs and allow the user to choose a smaller scope or explicitly continue, only while the selection remains within the actual hard ceiling.
- Treat the uncompressed archive hard ceiling separately. Show the ceiling and a clear message when it is exceeded; do not offer a confirmation that cannot succeed. Suggest necessary export or deselecting files.
- Make the distinction consistent in desktop and Web, including localized import/inspect errors. Expose the actual warning and hard limits through the preview or another backward-compatible API rather than assuming client constants.
- Verify the compressed upload, decompressed total, per-file and entry-count constraints independently. Prove that every package the same build allows itself to export can be imported under its own applicable limits; in particular, test a valid incompressible archive larger than the former 256 MiB upload limit. Do not infer this solely from a formula or a scaled-down test.
- Reject an oversized selection before reading and packaging its payload where possible. Keep server-side enforcement and handle changes between preview and export.

### Stage 2: Larger packages with bounded memory

- Stream export from object sources through the archive/compression pipeline and to the destination, without holding all payloads or the complete archive in memory. Ensure frontend and desktop save paths do not re-buffer the complete archive.
- Stream upload and import through bounded storage, validate archive entries and checksums before making imported records available, and preserve path, size, file-count and decompression protections. Clean up partial files on cancellation, failure and interruption.
- Check available disk space where practical and handle disk-full and memory-pressure failures clearly. Memory preflight is advisory because free memory can change during an operation.
- Use 5 GiB uncompressed as a **target for evaluation**, not an unconditional default. Set the eventual default and any configurable ceiling only after full export/import measurements on representative machines demonstrate an acceptable memory, disk and time cost. Document the resulting limits and compatibility.
- If a future per-object limit reaches the tar format's size-field boundary, use a supported encoding or impose a correct per-object limit.

## Involved Public APIs

Keep existing export, preview, inspect and import routes compatible. Add preview fields for warning and hard limits if needed, and document which limit measures compressed versus uncompressed data. Any changes to upload limits, streaming responses or error codes must be compatible with desktop and Web consumers.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

Research-package archive creation and validation; API preview, background export, inspect and import; desktop native save and Web download/upload; temporary files, checksums and storage; localized dialog text and export-scope selection. Coordinate UI changes with #1024. PR #1173 is the assumed baseline; #1177 explored part of the streaming export approach and is not a complete import/export solution.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- Test warning threshold and hard ceiling at and around their boundaries, including changing export scope after acknowledgement; verify both desktop and Web do not offer an impossible override.
- Run a real export → inspect → import round trip using an incompressible archive larger than 256 MiB, and compare restored content hashes. Cover synchronous/background and desktop flows as applicable, plus server-side refusal above the hard ceiling.
- Test malformed archives, decompression limits, missing data, cancellation, interrupted transfers and disk-full cleanup. Ensure the application does not execute imported content.
- For the larger-package stage, measure peak RSS, disk consumption and elapsed time for representative sizes, including a 5 GiB-class round trip on a 16 GiB machine before choosing the default. Measure the complete client-to-storage path, not only the compression function.
- Run `pnpm ci:l1` and the applicable unit, system and E2E gates; record counts and any blocked checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Warning threshold and hard ceiling are distinguished in the API and both export dialogs; a selection beyond the hard ceiling cannot be confirmed into an inevitably failing export.
- [ ] Users receive actionable localized guidance and can reduce the export scope; server-side checks refuse oversized exports before payload packaging where possible.
- [ ] A package allowed by the exporter can be inspected and imported by the same build; a real incompressible package larger than 256 MiB round-trips with matching content hashes.
- [ ] Import and export limits remain enforced independently for compressed upload, uncompressed data, individual files and entry count, including malformed or truncated archives.
- [ ] The larger-package implementation bounds memory across the whole export/import path, cleans up partial files, and records representative performance evidence before changing the default.
- [ ] The eventual default and ceiling are based on measured end-to-end behavior; 5 GiB is a target to evaluate, not a claimed capability before verification.
- [ ] Required tests and user journeys pass, with results and remaining limitations recorded.

## Additional Information

Earlier Windows measurements in the original report for incompressible payloads showed approximately 1,071 MiB peak RSS for 256 MiB, 1,248 MiB for 300 MiB, and 2,056 MiB for 500 MiB, measured across one export and import using the then-current in-memory implementation. These are historical measurements, not evidence for current main or a streaming implementation.

The reported user need is to export real research sessions larger than 512 MiB, while receiving an early and useful explanation when the chosen scope is too large. Large-package support must preserve a safe, verifiable export/import round trip.

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Four tests in `application/test` assume POSIX capabilities that a stock Windows 11 host does not have, so `pnpm --dir application test` (and therefore the Windows installer build) is red on such a machine even though the product code is fine. They pass on the CI `windows-latest` runner (see Additional Information), which is why this only shows up for people packaging the Windows app locally.

Running `pnpm --dir application test` on a stock Windows 11 host (Node 22.23.4) gives `# tests 343 / # pass 339 / # fail 4`:

```
not ok 27 - dirWritable answers true for a writable dir and false for a read-only one
  location: 'application/test/bootstrap.test.ts:417:1'
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly equal:
    true !== false

not ok 28 - bootstrapPackaged degrades in-place to copy mode on a read-only payload (W16 DMG run)
  location: 'application/test/bootstrap.test.ts:434:1'
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly equal:
    true !== false

not ok 248 - uninstall-mac.command: syntax-clean under macOS bash 3.2 (bash -n)
  location: 'application/test/uninstall-data.test.ts:80:1'
  error: 'spawnSync /bin/bash ENOENT'

not ok 288 - replaceVenvSymlinks rewrites burned-in absolute targets to the relative bundled target
  location: 'application/test/venv-launchers.test.ts:102:1'
  error: "EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink 'C:\\Users\\builder\\.workbuddy\\...\\bin\\python3'
          -> 'C:\\Users\\...\\Temp\\sd-sym-...\\v\\bin\\python'"
```

Cause, one by one:

1. **`bootstrap.test.ts:417` / `:434`** — the fixture runs `chmod(dir, 0o555)` and expects `dirWritable()` to answer `false`. On NTFS `chmod` only toggles the read-only attribute and does not make a directory unwritable for its owner, so `dirWritable()` correctly answers `true`; the second test is the same assertion through `bootstrapPackaged`. Both describe a macOS DMG-mounted payload (`W16`), which cannot be simulated this way on Windows.
2. **`uninstall-data.test.ts:80`** — `execFileSync("/bin/bash", ["-n", SCRIPT])` needs a real `/bin/bash`, which a Windows host does not have (Git for Windows ships `bash.exe` elsewhere, WSL is not guaranteed, and the test should not depend on either).
3. **`venv-launchers.test.ts:102`** — `makePosixVenv()` creates symlinks; creating symlinks on Windows needs Developer Mode or elevation, so it raises `EPERM` on a default install.

Minimal reproduction (no test code needed):

```powershell
pnpm --dir application install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --dir application test          # 339 pass, 4 fail on a stock Windows 11 host
```

Impact: `pnpm --dir application dist` is the command that produces the user-facing NSIS installer, and CI runs the same test step before it. Anyone who builds the installer on a normal Windows machine has to either ignore a red gate or hand-skip it; our Windows packaging job is currently blocked at exactly this gate.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

| | |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Microsoft Windows 11 家庭版 10.0.26200 (build 26200) |
| Node | v22.23.4 (x64) |
| pnpm | 11.1.2 |
| Shell used for the build | Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9818 (non-interactive) |
| Electron workspace | `application/` (renamed from `win_desktop/` by the macOS adaptation) |
| Developer Mode | off; the process is not elevated |
| `bash` on PATH | none (`/bin/bash` absent; no Git Bash/MSYS exposure in this shell) |
| Test command | `pnpm --dir application test` (`node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --test test/*.test.ts`) |

## Additional Information

**CI does pass this step, which localises the problem to host capabilities rather than product code.** For commit `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74`, Nightly run `43984975918`, job `Gate / Windows desktop installer` (`133716724096`, `windows-latest`): step 16 "Test and typecheck the desktop shell" = **success**; the job fails later, at step 17 "Build the Windows installer". The same job is skipped on `push` (`43886126438`) and `merge_group` (`43880862208`) because it is gated on `needs.policy.outputs.windows_desktop == 'true'` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:896`), so only the Nightly/release runs exercise it.

Suggested change — gate on the capability the test needs, not on a platform guess:

- `uninstall-data.test.ts:80`: skip when `/bin/bash` is not executable (`existsSync("/bin/bash")` or a `spawnSync` capability probe), and say in a comment that the macOS 3.2 syntax check only runs where that shell exists.
- `venv-launchers.test.ts:102`: skip when a symlink probe in the temp dir throws `EPERM`/`EACCES`, so a machine without Developer Mode still exercises the rest of the file.
- `bootstrap.test.ts:417` / `:434`: these two describe the macOS DMG payload; either skip them on `win32` (the payload is never read-only there) or replace the `chmod` fixture with a Windows-valid read-only simulation (an ACL that denies write) so the assertion means something on both hosts.

The four failures are test-only; `pnpm --dir application build`, `assemble` and `electron-builder --win` are unaffected once the gate is passed.

## Version Information

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Commit | `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74` ("feat(mac): macOS desktop adaptation — shell, packaging chain, sandbox & distribution") |
| Desktop shell package | `sd-shell` 0.4.0 (`application/package.json`) |
| Electron | `^37.0.0` (declared in `application/package.json`) |
| Node | v22.23.4 |
| CI evidence | Nightly run `43984975918`, job `133716724096` |
