### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the issue can be reproduced without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

When the selected model has no saved API key, the run fails with the generic `semantic-error` card. In a Chinese UI the main screen only says "运行中遇到了意外问题，任务未能完成。建议重试", and the actual cause — an English sentence — appears only after expanding "技术详情":

```
semantic-error
The selected model does not have a saved API token
```

This is a user-fixable configuration problem presented as an unexplained crash: the message is not readable in the UI language, and it is one click away from the place where the user would act.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open the desktop client (front end on 5174, API on 4410), locale `zh-CN`.
2. Settings › Models › add a custom model whose credential is left empty (any base URL, `tokenOptional` not effective for runs).
3. Select that model in the composer and send any message.
   - Observed: a failure card titled "运行异常"; expanding "技术详情" reveals `semantic-error` plus the English sentence above.
   - Expected: a readable failure that names the cause and the next step, for example "模型还没有配置 API Key / 到 设置 › 模型 补上后再试".

Reproduced 3 out of 3 times.

**Why it happens**

- The API raises a plain 400 at `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:842`:
  `throw new ApiStatusError(400, "The selected model does not have a saved API token");`
- `services/api/src/run-failure.ts:28` `classifyRunFailure()` matches only tool-call, timeout, auth-status, rate-limit, 5xx and transport wording. This 400 matches nothing and falls through to the catch-all `semantic-error`.
- `packages/schema/src/session.ts:578` `RunFailureCode` therefore has no code that describes this case.
- The desktop already has localized copy per code (`apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1633`, `en.ts:1582`), but with no code to look up it can only render the catch-all text. `apps/desktop/src/views/RunFailureCard.tsx:35-36` then prints the raw code and raw message inside the details block.

**Proposed fix (agreed approach)**

Give this failure its own code and its own copy, using the mechanism that already exists:

1. `packages/schema/src/session.ts` — add `model-credential-missing` to `RunFailureCode`.
2. `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:842` — raise a typed error that carries the code (do not depend on prose matching), and make `classifyRunFailure()` return it so the `run.failed` event carries `errorCode: "model-credential-missing"`.
3. `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts` and `en.ts` — add entries to `runFailure.titles` and the per-code body:
   - zh title: 模型还没有配置 API Key
   - zh body: 这个模型在设置里没有保存 API Key，运行无法开始。到 设置 › 模型 补上后重试。
   - en title: Model has no API key
   - en body: This model has no saved API key, so the run cannot start. Add one in Settings › Models and try again.
4. `apps/desktop/src/views/RunFailureCard.tsx` — for this code, render one localized sentence above the `<pre>` in "技术详情", keeping the provider text verbatim below it for diagnostics.
5. Tests: extend `services/api/src/run-failure.test.ts` (classification) and `apps/desktop/tests/run-failure.test.ts` (title/body lookup).

**Acceptance criteria**

- With a model that has no saved key, the failure card title and body are localized and name the missing key plus the settings path.
- The raw provider message still appears in "技术详情" (diagnostics are not lost).
- A regression test covers the new code on both the API classifier and the desktop copy lookup.
- Unknown future codes keep falling back to the existing generic title and body.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop client (`apps/desktop`), web dev surface: front end `http://127.0.0.1:5174`, API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Browser: Playwright's Chromium build 1228 (headless), viewport 1500x950, locale `zh-CN`.
- Model used for the failing run: a custom profile with an empty credential; the endpoint is never reached.

### Additional Information

- Screenshots attached: the failure card as the user sees it, and the expanded technical details.
- Found while walking a feature map over `apps/desktop` (failure-state item). A neighbouring case — a model whose base URL is unreachable — already classifies correctly as `transport-error` with actionable copy, which is why this one stands out.
- The English sentence is the provider-independent API text, so it reads the same for every model.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `222e7b06a418f3ee1c362c0dc201c7b67530605b` (2026-11-20)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

![What the user sees: generic 运行异常, cause hidden behind a click](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec092310-e0df-4ff0-b5a3-3ad23f71dcb0)

![Expanded technical details: semantic-error plus the English API sentence](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e311b25-093d-4f94-b118-057a45c9a9c4)

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the issue can be reproduced without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

In the desktop client the workspace panel's maximum width is computed as if the left task sidebar were still on screen, but opening the panel removes that sidebar (`App.tsx:1377`). The reserved width is subtracted from a window that no longer contains it, so the panel opens narrower than its own default and, at ordinary laptop widths, the splitter cannot move it at all.

**Steps to reproduce** (viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`)

1. Open the desktop client and open any session that has artifacts (one generated `sales.csv` is enough).
2. Click the workspace panel control (`aria-label="工作区面板"`).
   - Observed: `.app-shell` becomes `sidebar-hidden panel-open` — the task sidebar is not rendered — and the panel opens at 628 px.
3. Drag the splitter to the left, or focus it and press `Shift+ArrowLeft` five times.
   - Expected: the panel widens, as it does on a wide window.
   - Observed: the panel stays at 628 px; not one pixel moves.
4. Widen the window to 1800 px and repeat step 3.
   - Observed: the panel goes 720 → 928 px and stops at 928, so the behaviour is a ceiling, not a broken splitter.

**Measured**

| viewport | panel on open | after 5x Shift+ArrowLeft | ceiling the code gives | ceiling if the hidden sidebar is not reserved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1800x950 | 720 | 928 | 928 | 1100 (capped) |
| 1500x950 | 628 | 628 | 628 | 924 |
| 1440x950 | 568 | 568 | 568 | 864 |
| 1280x950 | 480 | 480 | 480 | 704 |

1500 px is an ordinary laptop width, and there the ceiling (628) is *below* `PANEL_DEFAULT_WIDTH` (720): `PANEL_DEFAULT_WIDTH` only applies from 1592 px up (`720 + 872`). The same happens at 1440 px (568) and 1280 px (480, the floor), which is why the splitter feels decorative rather than merely limited.

**Root cause pointer**

- `apps/desktop/src/app/panel-width.ts:81` — `clampPanelWidth` builds `ceiling = Math.min(PANEL_MAX_WIDTH, viewportWidth - PANEL_SIDEBAR_WIDTH - PANEL_MIN_CHAT_WIDTH)`, with `PANEL_SIDEBAR_WIDTH = 360` (line 44) and `PANEL_MIN_CHAT_WIDTH = 512` (line 47).
- `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx:1377` — `const taskSidebar = sidebarOpen && !panelOpen;`: while the panel is open the task sidebar is not rendered at all, so there is no sidebar column to reserve. The comment directly above it (`App.tsx:1371-1375`) states the same thing: the panel takes the sidebar's place rather than sharing the window with it.
- The constant does not match the layout either. The task column is 296 px (`apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css:184`, `--d-sidebar: 296px` in `styles/tokens.css:70`) and the rail is 64 px (`design.css:60-66`, `--d-rail`); the comment above `PANEL_SIDEBAR_WIDTH` still quotes an older grid, `256px minmax(0, 1fr) var(--panel-width)` from `styles/shell.css:26`, which `design.css` overrides because `styles/index.css` imports it last.
- `apps/desktop/tests/panel-width.test.ts:44-70` asserts the current arithmetic, so its expectations move with the fix.

**Suggested fix**

Reserve only the columns that are actually laid out. While the panel is open, that is the 64 px rail plus the 512 px conversation floor:

```ts
const ceiling = Math.min(
  PANEL_MAX_WIDTH,
  viewportWidth - PANEL_RAIL_WIDTH - (panelOpen ? 0 : PANEL_SIDEBAR_WIDTH) - PANEL_MIN_CHAT_WIDTH,
);
```

with `PANEL_SIDEBAR_WIDTH` corrected to 296. With that, 1500 px allows 924 px and 1800 px reaches the 1100 px cap.

If `clampPanelWidth` should stay a pure function of two numbers, the alternative is to pass the conversation column's real available width from `use-panel-width.ts:69` instead of `window.innerWidth`, reading `.app-shell`'s two fixed columns once per render.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop client (`apps/desktop`), run as the web dev surface: front end `http://127.0.0.1:5174`, API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner on `127.0.0.1:4411`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Browser: Playwright's Chromium build 1228 (headless), viewports 1800x950 / 1500x950 / 1440x950 / 1280x950, locale `zh-CN`.
- Reproduced by hand in the same build at all four widths, and by script on repeated runs.

### Additional Information

- Screenshots attached: the same session at 1800 and at 1500, before and after five `Shift+ArrowLeft` presses. The coloured box is the panel's measured edge, checked against the rendered border in the raw captures (x = 872 at 1500, x = 1080/872 at 1800 before/after).
- The width itself is remembered in `localStorage` (`PANEL_WIDTH_STORAGE_KEY`) and the clamp is applied to what is rendered only (`use-panel-width.ts:69`), so the stored width is not damaged — it is just never shown at these viewport widths.
- No console error is involved; this is a wrong input to one calculation.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

![Q9-panel-width-en](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/146eeb08-ee9f-4aa4-9e03-0e654f8e2c2b)

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the issue can be reproduced without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

When a model connectivity test fails, the desktop client shows the API's English sentence verbatim — in a Chinese UI, with no status marker and no hint about what to fix. The localized explanations for exactly these failures already exist in `text/zh.ts`, but they are unreachable: the API always fills `message`, and the client prefers `message` over `category`.

**Steps to reproduce** (1500x950 viewport, `zh-CN`)

1. Open 设置 › 模型 and click 添加模型.
2. Keep 服务商类型 `DeepSeek`, and fill: 基础URL `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1`, API key `sk-anything`, 模型名称 `probe-model`.
3. Click 测试连接.
   - Expected: a Chinese sentence such as 「连不上这个地址，请检查网络或自定义地址是否可达。」
   - Observed: `Could not connect to model provider; support is unknown` — English, no `✕` prefix, and nothing says the base URL is the likely culprit.

The same shape appears for the other failure categories (`Compatibility check timed out; support is unknown`, `Base URL or model ID was not found`, …): every one of them is an English sentence rendered as-is.

**Why this matters**

This is the one screen where the user is expected to *fix* the problem — the address they typed. The English sentence names neither the field nor an action, and reads like an internal diagnostic, so the user is left to guess. The success path is equally unhelpful in the other direction: it renders a full technical paragraph (`✓ 基础检查通过（1132 ms） · 仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。`) inside a one-line verdict.

**Root cause pointer**

- The API builds the sentence: `services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts:58` — `message: "Could not connect to model provider; support is unknown"`; same at line 55 (`timeout`), line 61 (`invalid_response`), and in `providerFailure()` at lines 46-52 (`API key is invalid or is not authorized`, `Base URL or model ID was not found`, …).
- The client prefers that sentence over the category it already has: `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx:473-476`
  ```ts
  function failureMessage(test: ModelConnectivityTestResult): string {
    if (test.message.trim() !== "") return test.message;
    return TEXT.wizard.testCategories[test.category] ?? TEXT.errors.generic;
  }
  ```
- The localized text for every category is already written and translated: `text/zh.ts:746-756` and `text/en.ts:721-733` (`network` → 「连不上这个地址，请检查网络或自定义地址是否可达。」). Because the API always sends a non-empty `message`, `TEXT.wizard.testCategories` is dead code in practice.
- The verdict itself has no marker: `ModelForm.tsx:889` renders `{verdict.message}` after a bare `kind === "fail"` style, so no `✕` ever appears.

**Suggested fix**

Let the category decide the sentence, and keep the English text as the detail a developer can still reach:

```ts
function failureMessage(test: ModelConnectivityTestResult): string {
  const localized = TEXT.wizard.testCategories[test.category];
  return localized ?? (test.message.trim() !== "" ? test.message : TEXT.errors.generic);
}
```

and put `test.message` in the verdict's `title` (tooltip) — the raw sentence stays available for diagnosis without becoming the interface. Optionally add the `✕` marker so success and failure differ at a glance.

The alternative — stop sending display text from the API — was rejected: `message` is part of `ModelConnectivityTestResult` in `packages/schema`, and other consumers (the first-run wizard, review tooling) read it for logs.

If a category is genuinely new and untranslated, the fallback path keeps today's behaviour, so no failure becomes less informative than it is now.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop client (`apps/desktop`), run as the web dev surface: front end `http://127.0.0.1:5174`, API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner on `127.0.0.1:4411`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Browser: Playwright's Chromium build 1228 (headless), viewport 1500x950, locale `zh-CN`.
- Reproduced 2 times in the same build (probe run + manual check in the same dialog).

### Additional Information

- Screenshot attached: 添加模型 dialog after a failed 测试连接, with the English sentence under the model-name field.
- Found while walking the 设置 feature area (D8-04 测试模型连接); the map expected `✓ 可用（N ms）` / `✕ <reason>`, neither of which exists.
- Related but separate: #1292 covers run-time failures (`semantic-error` fallback). This one is the *configuration-time* path, with its own category enum, so it can be localized without touching run classification.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

items.body:
- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The environment and the exact run are named below, so this is reproducible from the job log alone.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The `UT` job reports **success** while executing **no Python test at all**. A failing Python case therefore cannot turn the gate red — the suites exist, are tagged, and are silently never run.

### What was observed

On PR #1231 (head `49354a23ca6a262bc79a6022c38dc675798143ba`), job **`UT`** = `134700142074` in run `44274693462` finished `success`. Its executed plan contains 681 entries:

| extension | count |
| --- | --- |
| `.ts` | 474 |
| `.tsx` | 159 |
| `.mjs` | 43 |
| none | 5 |
| **`.py`** | **0** |

Two independent greps over the same job log:

```
services/evolve/tests   -> 0 occurrences
.py::                   -> 0 occurrences
```

The environment for Python *was* prepared in that same job, so this is not a skipped setup:

```
2026-11-18T09:20:34.3171967Z Prepare: uv sync --project services/evolve --locked --extra test --extra candidates
2026-11-18T09:20:35.6487682Z Prepare: uv pip install --python .../services/evolve/.venv/bin/python coverage>=7.6,<8
```

### What the runner is supposed to collect

`test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs:112-113`:

```js
export const pythonProjects = Object.freeze(['paper', 'gateway', 'memory-graph', 'evolve', 'adapter']);
export const pythonSources = project => `services/${project}/tests/test_*.py`;
```

`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:257-261`:

```js
if(needUT)for(const project of pythonProjects){
  const dir=join(outputDir,`collect-${project}`);mkdirSync(dir,{recursive:true});
  const sources=[...globSync(pythonSources(project),{cwd:root})].sort();
  catalog.push(...collect({root,files:sources,outputDir:dir,python:python(project),pytestPlugins:pythonPlugins[project]??[],env:projectEnv(env,project)}));
}
```

So for `evolve` the scope is `services/evolve/tests/test_*.py` — 20+ files exist there — and that loop runs under the same `needUT` that produced the `uv sync` above.

### Why it matters

Every Python suite under `services/*/tests` is currently unguarded on PRs. This is not theoretical: PR #1231 adds two regression cases for a UTF-8 decode bug, both tagged `category:ut`, and neither is executed by the job that is supposed to gate them. Any existing Python test could regress without any PR check noticing.

Note that the same plan shows no `.py` for **any** of the five `pythonProjects`, not only `evolve`.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository state: `main` at `eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e`; the run above is on PR #1231 head `49354a23ca6a262bc79a6022c38dc675798143ba`.
- CI: GitHub Actions, the `UT` job of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, run `44274693462`, job `134700062...`/`134700142074`, `ubuntu` runner, 2026-11-18T09:18Z.
- Toolchain: `pnpm@11.1.2`, Node 22, Python 3.12 through `uv` (the job's own `Prepare:` lines above).
- Local contrast: running the same files directly works — `python3 -m pytest services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py` collects and runs them under a normal interpreter, so the files themselves collect; the discrepancy is in the tagged runner's catalog.

## Additional Information

Reproduce without any code change: open any recent `UT` job log and count `Run N/M:` lines by extension — the Python ones are absent while `Prepare: uv sync --project services/<name>` lines are present for all five Python projects.

Possibly related: `collect()` shells out to `python -m pytest ... --collect-only` (`test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs:98`). If that collection returns zero entries or fails quietly, the run still reports success because nothing was planned. Worth checking whether the pytest invocation in the runner resolves the project interpreter and the `science_tags` plugin, and whether an empty catalog for a `pythonProjects` entry should be an error rather than silence.

I found this while fixing #1229 in #1231; that PR deliberately does **not** touch the collection code — it is the encoding fix only.

## Version Information

- `main`: `eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e` (2026-11-18)
- Affected job: `UT`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Runner files: `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs`

items.body:
Actions failure classification: **code**.

Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405 (attempt 2)

Upstream failing job: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135282620250

Head SHA: `59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608`

## Current behavior

`Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-6)` failed the desktop SRBench PUCT smoke at the smoke's own bar of three expansions:

```
Error: The search must record at least 3 expansions
expect(received).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(expected)
Expected: >= 3
Received:    1
```

Its own summary step agrees that the planned case is the only failure: the shared plan reads `- e2e-real: passed 0 of 1 planned`, and the problem list names `FAIL: playwright:test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts::…desktop%20%2Fevolve-design%20reaches%20three%20PUCT%20expansions…`.

The job's evidence artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-6` (artifact id 14490394792; the upload step recorded the zip digest `8e5c0c81…`) belongs to this run and this commit (`E2E_COMMIT_SHA=59d05aa7…`). In it, `real-standard/e2e-real/test-results/desktop-evolve-srbench-rea-ba575-s-on-an-LLM-SRBench-problem-real/` holds:

- `desktop-evolve-metrics.json` — `"search_status": "succeeded"`, `"expansions": 1`; the single search record is `"status": "succeeded"`, `"bestNodeIndex": 1`, `"finishedAt": "2026-11-19T02:10:53.023Z"`, and its confirmed scorecard carries `"solvedThreshold": 0.999` on a `custom_script` criterion.
- `evolve-events.json` (13 events) — the seed (node 0) scored `baselineScore: 0.194226`; the one expansion (node 1) was `"valid": true`, `"score": 1`; then a log event `"planned 24 expansions, made 1; it stopped because target_reward."` and `{"type": "search_finished", "status": "succeeded", "stopReason": "target_reward", "bestTestScore": 1, "expansionsPlanned": 24, "candidates": 2}`.

The search did not stall, lose workers or hit a token ceiling: its first candidate reached the scorecard's solved threshold (test score 1.0 vs 0.999), and the engine stopped there. This run had `E2E_LLM_THINKING_MODE=enabled`, `E2E_LLM_THINKING_EFFORT=low`, so the per-call token ceiling that #1157 described was not involved; provider faults were 0.

That stop is documented product behavior, not a defect in the search. Since #1073 (closing #948) the PUCT engine passes the scorecard threshold as the framework's target stop:

```python
# services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/puct_engine.py:399
            "target_reward": float(spec.scorecard.get("solvedThreshold") or 0.999),
```

and `services/evolve/tests/test_puct_engine.py::test_reaching_the_scorecard_s_solved_threshold_ends_the_run` asserts exactly the event shape this run produced (`stopReason == "target_reward"`, `status == "succeeded"`, fewer expansions than planned).

The smoke, however, hard-codes the count and stops polling on any terminal status, including `succeeded`:

```ts
// test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:441
          || ["budget_exhausted", "failed", "stopped", "succeeded"].includes(status);
// test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:449
      expect(expanded.length, `The search must record at least ${target} expansions`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(target);
```

So the pass condition is only satisfiable when the model's first candidates do not already reach the scorecard threshold — which is model-luck, not a property of the product.

## Same test bytes passed the night before

The spec and workflows are byte-identical between the previous Nightly head and this one: `git diff b2075e4972a5af90804fdd579ee314bfa502be46 59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608 -- test/ .github/` is empty, and `b2075e49` is the last commit touching the spec. Nightly run 44199315530 (head `b2075e49`, final attempt 3) was green, including `Real E2E (research-6)` and `Account for real cases`. This is not a source regression on this head; the difference is whether the design's first candidate already solves the SRBench problem.

## Not the same cause as the open reports

#1157/#1158/#1159 (run 43760882196) describe a different mechanism: two expansions because 22 candidate calls were cut off at the recorded 16000-token per-call ceiling while still thinking, ending on the expansion cap. #1185 (closed, unknown) recorded 0 expansions. Here the search ended `succeeded` on `target_reward` after one expansion, with a valid candidate that scored 1.0. Those reports remain accurate for their runs; this failure needs its own fix.

## Downstream jobs

One cause explains all four failing jobs:

- `Account for real cases` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286552958) fails "Reconcile every planned identity" with `Planned 21; executed 21; passed 20; provider faults 0.` / `- research-6: SHARD_FAILED` — the only failed case is this one.
- `merge-gate` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286707014) refuses because the scheduled real layer is red: `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`.
- `Report the outcome` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286834408) runs `[[ "${RESULT}" == "success" ]]` with `RESULT: failure`, so it exits 1. It reports the gate; it does not decide it.

No rerun is requested. A rerun could pass by luck if the model's first candidate falls short of 0.999, but the assertion still contradicts the documented stop, so the same red is expected whenever the design solves the problem on its first candidate.

## Expected behavior

A search that reaches the scorecard's `solvedThreshold` on its first expansion must end `succeeded` with `stopReason: "target_reward"`, and the smoke should accept that ending as a pass while still failing a search that produced fewer than three expansions for any other reason (token ceiling, worker loss, `max_iters`/`max_calls`). Today the smoke cannot tell those apart.

## Requested code change

In `test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts`, step "Watch the search reach three expansions" (the block around lines 419-449): after `await save("evolve-events.json", events)`, read the `search_finished` event out of the collected events and branch before the `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(target)` assertion:

- `expanded.length >= target` — unchanged: read each candidate back by hash as the code does today.
- otherwise, if the final event is `search_finished` with `status === "succeeded"`, `stopReason === "target_reward"` and `bestTestScore >= scorecard.solvedThreshold` — record the ending (for example `metrics.stop_reason`, `metrics.expansions_planned`) and read back the candidate(s) that were actually recorded by hash, then pass.
- otherwise — keep today's failure, with a message that names `status` and `stopReason`, so a short search that ended at the budget or on an error still fails exactly as it does now (that is the #1157 case).

Please also add a regression test for the branch itself — a small unit test over the extracted predicate is enough, since the journey needs a real model — so a later edit cannot silently drop the distinction between "goal met early" and "stopped short".

## References

- Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405
- research-6: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135282620250
- Account for real cases: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286552958
- merge-gate: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286707014
- Report the outcome: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286834408
- Earlier green Nightly with the identical spec: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44199315530

## Uncertainty and limits

I read the artifact's `desktop-evolve-metrics.json` and `evolve-events.json` (and the scorecard embedded in the former) plus the four failed-step logs; I did not open the Playwright trace or the journey report HTML, and I did not run the journey locally. The artifact metadata ties it to run 44415877405 and commit 59d05aa7 (its digest is the one job 135282620250 recorded), but I cannot separately prove which attempt every file inside it came from, nor which model endpoint state produced the 1.0 score. I make no claim about future Nightly runs beyond the assertion defect described.

This report does not approve development. Existing review gates and a development label applied by a person are still required.

items.body:
Actions failure classification: **unknown**.

Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291 (attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`)

Head SHA: `d57fc2693e0972b5c1040d47a4b74370eb011c3f`

Upstream failing job: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135002663249 (Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-11))

## Current behavior

`research-11` planned exactly one case, J5, and executed none. The shard reported `{"status":"FAIL","planned":1,"executed":0,"passed":0,"failed":0,"skipped":1}`, `1 skipped`, and the problem line `- e2e-real: 1 skipped — a skip is not a pass`. The journey report captured in the `real-e2e-evidence-research-11` artifact (id `14460243200`) records the precondition:

```
BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: Conda environment setup failed)
```

The environment-setup state was therefore `failed`, not `installing`. The message is the generic non-micromamba failure from `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:1460` (`Conda environment setup failed`); the store keeps the actual provisioner transcript in `setup.error` / `components.conda.error`, but J5 prints only `setup.message`, and `real-e2e.yml` uploads `.ci-results` only. The runner's operational log at `<CI_RUNTIME_DIR>/real-standard/data/logs/runner.log` is not in the artifact, so the precise conda/provisioning error is missing.

`Account for real cases` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075589240) reports `- research-11: SHARD_FAILED`; `merge-gate` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075765132) fails with `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`; `Report the outcome` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075939143) fails with `RESULT: failure`.

## Expected behavior

The managed Python base reaches `ready` within J5's 180 s wait (the wait added by #286 / #287), J5 executes, and the shard reports planned=executed=passed=1. A setup failure must remain BLOCKED; the journey's reaction is the intended fail-closed behaviour. #286 was about the normal `installing` phase racing the first read; this run observed `failed`, so it is a different failure.

## What was checked

- The failed-step output of job 135002663249 and the `real-e2e-evidence-research-11` artifact (`14460243200`): the journey report and its blocked-step screenshot, `run.log`, `stack.log`, and `api-diagnostics`. The stack log shows three `GET /api/environment-setup 200 OK` requests and no conda/micromamba transcript. I read the artifact with `gh run download`; its origin is this run and commit, but its contents and attempt association are my observation, not independently verified.
- Source at `d57fc269`: `failSetup` (`environment-store.ts:1460`), `runManagedEnvironmentSetup` / `bootstrapStarter` / `validateStarter` (the `conda` component is entered only after micromamba is ready, so this is the Python-base create/validate phase), and `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts:73` (the BLOCKED skip).
- Previous runs: `research-11` succeeded in Nightly 44199315530 (job 134449454466) and 43984975918 (job 133711095274), both with J5 executed. In 43514552368 the job failed *after* J5 executed (a different, post-setup failure). The immediately preceding nightly, 44199315530 on `b2075e49`, ran the same provisioning path and J5 passed.
- Diff: 25 commits separate `b2075e49` from `d57fc269`; none touch `services/runner`, `packages/network`, `services/launcher`, `scripts/start-stack.sh`, `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, or `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` / `test/helpers/environment-setup.ts`. That makes a regression from this commit in the provisioning path unlikely, but it does not identify the failing precondition.
- Not checked: the runner's operational log and the `setup.error` payload, because neither is uploaded. I did not rerun the paid Nightly to try to reproduce the state.

## Uncertainty

The inner failure is unresolved. Candidates that the missing transcript would separate: conda channel/CDN/network failure while creating the Python base, a runner disk/permission problem, or a latent race in the provisioning code. The job duration (~2 min) and the `failed` state observed before J5's 180 s deadline are consistent with a setup failure during the conda step, not with a wait timeout, but they do not choose among the candidates.

## Why report this / next verification

1. Re-run `research-11` (or the Nightly) on this commit and observe `GET /api/environment-setup`; a transition to `ready` and a J5 pass would support a transient provisioning failure, while a repeat failure would justify a code investigation.
2. Preserve the evidence next time: upload the runner's operational log for the real shard, or include `setup.state`, `setup.error` and the `components.conda` transcript in the journey report on a BLOCKED precondition. That is the one missing fact that would let the next occurrence be attributed to an external channel/network problem or to a repository defect.
3. If the transcript shows an external channel failure, this report can be closed as an environment precondition; if it shows a code error, it becomes a concrete repair issue.

items.body:
Actions failure classification: **external**.

Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291 (attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`)

Head SHA: `d57fc2693e0972b5c1040d47a4b74370eb011c3f`

Upstream failing job: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135002663117 (Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-2))

## Current behavior

The only planned case in the `research-2` shard, `DRB-59 easy Swarm research integration`, was classified `PROVIDER_FAULT`. The shard reported `planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 0 / failed 0 / provider faults 1` and failed with `- e2e-real: 1 provider fault(s) — an unverified case is not a pass`. The full job log gives the case's own error:

```
Error: Main run must complete with readable, nonempty declared final artifacts; delivery_status=partial; run_status=failed; delivered_artifacts=1; run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

The job's `stack.log` identifies the failing request as `model-8f784f89-e866-486a-88b8-9d48d6063774`: HTTP 200, 12,117 SSE records / 3,716,762 bytes over 105.9 s, then `"error":{"classification":"network"}`, with `"attempts":1,"retries":0` and `"hasText":true,"hasToolCalls":true`. The next line is:

```
[jiuwenswarm-agent] run of 670fa97d-b9d0-4410-ad9f-ac0d80e75072 failed: [181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

## Expected behavior

DRB-59 completes its declared final artifacts and the shard reports `passed 1 of 1`. A live provider keeping the response open is a precondition of that journey, not a product assertion.

## Causal chain

The gateway accepted the request (`200`), streamed the answer and tool-call deltas for about 106 s, and the upstream connection was reset while answer text had already been exposed. The model gateway's bounded mid-stream retry is deliberately disabled once answer text is visible: `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:517` throws when `state.text` is true, so the turn was not replayed and the run failed with the original transport error. The accounting then correctly recorded `PROVIDER_FAULT` (the status-less transport classification from #1071 / #1076). Under the repository's documented policy a provider fault is not a pass, so the downstream jobs failed:

- **Account for real cases** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075589240) reported `Planned 21; executed 20; passed 19; provider faults 1.` and `- PROVIDER_FAULT: ...DRB-59...`.
- **Gate / merge-gate** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075765132) failed with `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`; `.ci/tier-policy.mjs:52` throws because the daily profile requires the `real-scheduled` job to succeed.
- **Report the outcome** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075939143) failed with `RESULT: failure`; it only asserts that the gate result is `success`.

The other 19 real cases in this run passed, so the endpoint was not globally down; the fault is confined to one model turn.

## What was checked and what it rules out

- The failed-step output of job 135002663117, its `error-context.md`, and the `real-e2e-evidence-research-2` artifact (id `14455408997`). The artifact's `stack.log` is the wire-level evidence quoted above. I read it with `gh run download`; the artifact belongs to this run and commit, but its contents and attempt association are my observation, not independently verified.
- Source at the failed SHA: `const MAX_STREAM_RETRIES = 4;` (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:188`) and the `state.text` guard at `:517`. The zero retries are the documented behaviour, not a missing retry loop.
- Existing Issues: #1071 / #1076 added the status-less transport classification; #898 documented that a reset after answer text starts is not replayed; #1222 recorded the same class for DRB-58 in run 44199315530. This run is a new occurrence of that class, not a new repository defect. It is not the cause reported in #1157-#1160, which describe run 43760882196 and a different failure.

## Uncertainty

The gateway diagnostics preserve only `classification: network`; the provider's own reason for closing the connection (load, edge reset, upstream timeout) is not visible. One reset in one request does not establish how widespread the provider problem was.

## Next verification

Re-run `research-2` (or the Nightly) once when the gateway is healthy and check that DRB-59 completes; a pass would separate the outage from the commit. A rerun was not requested here because the independent J5 provisioning failure in the same run (job 135002663249) is not yet established as external; see the separate report for that job. If maintainers want a turn-level retry that discards partial text, that is the enhancement space of #898, not a fix for this incident.

items.author: Birfy
items.body:
## Summary

There is no update mechanism of any kind: `autoUpdate` / `checkForUpdate` appear nowhere in the codebase. A user who installed a binary months ago has no way to learn that a newer release exists, short of visiting the repository. Comparable workbenches ship auto-updating desktop builds; we do not even notify.

## Current state

- **Version is visible, staleness is not.** `ScienceDiscovery version` prints the release version plus bundled Node/CPython/micromamba versions. Nothing ever compares that against what has since been published.
- **Releases already carry the right metadata.** `scripts/package-binary-release.sh` emits `VERSION` and `SHA256SUMS` next to the artifacts, and the binary-release flow already verifies downloads by pinned SHA-256 (that is how Node, CPython, micromamba, and the uv wheel are fetched). The building blocks for a verifiable update check exist.
- **Side-by-side versions already work.** The payload cache is digest-keyed (`~/.cache/science-discovery/payload/<payload-id>`) and "an upgrade does not overwrite an older extraction", so an older release stays runnable — rollback is feasible today.
- **Remote runners can silently drift.** The Runner SEA is versioned by the build's Git commit prefix, and a mismatch between the local control plane and an already-deployed remote runner only produces a warning; it does not block or redeploy. So a long-lived SSH target can keep running a months-old runner.
- **No documented upgrade contract.** There is no guide covering data-directory compatibility across releases, what a new binary rebuilds on first `serve`, or how to roll back (also noted in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25)).

## Proposal

### 1. Update check (the part that matters most)

An opt-in check against a published release manifest — the existing `VERSION` + `SHA256SUMS` pair is already close to one.

- **Off by default in air-gapped installs**, and settable in system configuration. No telemetry beyond fetching the manifest; do not send an install identifier.
- Route the request through the configured network proxy, since proxy settings already exist.
- Surface the result quietly: a dismissible banner in the UI, a line in `ScienceDiscovery version`, and an explicit `--check-updates` for scripts.
- Fail silent on a network error. An offline workstation must never see an error toast because an update check could not reach the internet.

### 2. Self-update (optional second step)

`ScienceDiscovery update` that downloads the new artifact, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS` (ideally a signature too), swaps it atomically, and keeps the previous binary so a rollback is one command. The digest-keyed payload cache means the old version's extracted runtime is still there.

For Docker and source mode, print the right command instead of attempting anything — `docker compose pull` / `git pull && ./scripts/start-stack.sh` — rather than pretending a binary self-update applies.

### 3. Upgrade contract

Document, and enforce in code:

- what the data directory guarantees across versions, and what the first `serve` after an upgrade rebuilds;
- refusing to open a data directory written by a newer release, rather than half-migrating it;
- redeploying the matching Runner SEA to remote hosts when the control plane updates, instead of only warning about the mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user on an outdated release is told so, in the UI and on the CLI.
- [ ] The check is opt-in/opt-out, proxy-aware, and silent on failure.
- [ ] No update path installs an artifact whose SHA-256 was not verified.
- [ ] Rollback to the previous version is documented and works.
- [ ] Docker and source-mode users get correct upgrade instructions rather than a binary self-update.
- [ ] Remote runner drift is resolved automatically or reported as an actionable error.

## Open questions

- Where would the release manifest live, given the canonical repository is on GitCode and GitHub is a mirror? It needs one stable URL.
- Should releases be signed, or is SHA-256 against a manifest over HTTPS sufficient for this threat model?
- Default for the update check on a fresh install: on or off?

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Summary and current-release boundary

Multi-agent orchestration is a core JiuwenSwarm capability. ScienceDiscovery should explicitly evaluate whether and how to reuse it, rather than silently treating our existing orchestration as the final architecture.

For this release, retain the currently validated hybrid path: **ScienceDiscovery manages delegation through `task`; JiuwenSwarm executes both the main agent and the child agents.** This RFC does not request an immediate migration or block the current release. The eventual reuse decision must be documented with implementation evidence, validation results, and trade-offs.

## Current implementation

The current debugging deployment explicitly selects the platform `task` route. This is a deployment choice, not a claim that every Swarm-backed deployment uses this route.

```text
Main agent (Swarm loop)
  -> ScienceDiscovery task orchestration
  -> Child agent (independent Swarm loop)
  -> Platform task result
  -> Main agent continues
```

ScienceDiscovery currently prepares the specialist profile, enabled MCP/skills, workspace and handoff; manages permissions, concurrency, turn/time limits and cancellation; and records child progress, results and artifacts for the existing UI. The parent receives the result when the `task` call completes.

Swarm's native route uses `subagent_spawn` and `subagent_wait`, with Swarm owning child orchestration. Its integration with ScienceDiscovery-specific bindings has not been fully validated. This does **not** mean Swarm lacks tools, permissions or lifecycle management; the question is how its mechanisms map to the platform's existing behavior.

## Problem and existing evidence

Using Swarm only as the execution engine leaves an important part of its core capability unreused, while switching delegation tools alone risks losing platform behavior. We need a deliberate ownership boundary instead of two overlapping orchestration systems.

A recent real-LLM literature-research run completed through platform `task`: two Swarm-executed children used professional literature MCP tools, returned results, and the parent produced a registered report. This validates that hybrid route only; it does not establish native `subagent_spawn` MCP inheritance, comparative quality, or benchmark-wide reliability.

## Evaluation scope

Evaluate the native route against the current hybrid baseline on the same pinned versions and comparable model/task/tool settings.

| Area | Questions to resolve |
| --- | --- |
| Delegation and scheduling | Who owns creation, concurrency, waiting, completion, and nested delegation? Can we avoid duplicate schedulers and inconsistent state? |
| Context and capabilities | How do specialist instructions, skills, model selection and enabled MCP tools reach each child's actual LLM input? What is inherited versus explicitly handed off? |
| Workspace and science outputs | How do child workspace isolation, sandbox paths, artifact registration, provenance and parent access map to Swarm? |
| Permissions and lifecycle | How are manual approval, automatic approval, cancellation, turn/time limits and partial failures preserved? |
| Results and UI | How are streaming child progress, tool events, usage, errors and final results represented in the existing UI? Does the parent reliably continue? |
| Maintenance | Which extension points already exist? Which minimal upstream fixes/hooks are missing? What platform code could actually be removed? |

Prefer native Swarm capabilities for generic agent behavior. Keep differentiated science functionality in separate modules; intrusive Swarm changes should be limited to bug fixes or necessary extension hooks, not embedding science business logic.

## Candidate outcomes — not a predetermined selection

1. **Native Swarm orchestration plus science extensions:** reuse spawning/waiting/lifecycle and adapt platform capabilities and UI events.
2. **Staged migration:** retain `task` temporarily while closing named native-integration gaps, then transfer ownership with clear exit criteria.
3. **Retain platform orchestration:** acceptable only with concrete evidence explaining why native reuse is unsuitable, its maintenance costs, and conditions for revisiting the decision.

A tool rename or a single successful demo is insufficient to choose between these options.

## Validation and required conclusion

The decision should be backed by deterministic integration tests and a small set of comparable real research runs, not only code inspection.

- Verify actual child LLM tool lists, model routing, skill/context delivery and workspace access.
- Cover parallel children, successful result collection and parent continuation, one child failing, timeout/cancellation, and both approval modes.
- Verify child artifacts remain accessible and traceable, and UI progress reaches a correct terminal state.
- Compare task completion, result quality, token use, elapsed time and resource consumption under comparable conditions; record limitations and failures.

Before closing this RFC, publish a community-reviewed conclusion containing:

- the selected architecture and the rationale for reusing or not reusing native Swarm orchestration;
- a capability/gap matrix with concrete source or test evidence;
- ownership of scheduling, context/tool binding, permissions, lifecycle and science outputs;
- required changes, migration and rollback boundaries, and code that can be removed;
- remaining limitations and follow-up issues, with an explicit distinction between current-release acceptance and the long-term decision.

Related: #84 (Swarm migration), #107 (E2E scenarios).
items.title: [Rfc] Evaluate native JiuwenSwarm multi-agent orchestration versus the current platform task integration

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Motivation

Currently, every conversation must belong to a project, and creating a project requires too much configuration before users can start chatting.

This adds friction to the first interaction: users who simply want to ask a question or explore an idea must first create and configure a project, even when they do not yet need one. It also encourages creating projects for one-off conversations, making project management unnecessarily cluttered.

Users should be able to open the application and start a conversation immediately, then organize their work into projects when needed.

## Proposed direction for discussion

1. **Make project membership optional for conversations.**
   - Provide a prominent “New chat” entry that works without creating or selecting a project.
   - Support standalone conversations for quick questions, exploration, and one-off tasks.
   - Keep project-based conversations available for ongoing research and related work.

2. **Allow users to organize conversations into projects later.**
   - Let users move a standalone conversation into a new or existing project.
   - Preserve conversation history and associated artifacts when moving it.
   - Make it clear whether a conversation belongs to a project.

3. **Simplify project creation.**
   - Require only the minimum information needed to create a project, such as its name.
   - Provide sensible defaults and make advanced configuration optional.
   - Allow users to update project settings later instead of requiring them before the first conversation.

4. **Provide clear navigation for both workflows.**
   - Make standalone conversations and projects easy to find.
   - Let users start a conversation directly from the main interface.
   - Within a project, let users create conversations associated with that project.

## Example user flows

### Start chatting immediately

Open the application → New chat → Send a message.

No project creation or project configuration is required.

### Organize an exploratory conversation

Start a standalone conversation → Decide to continue the work → Move the conversation into a new or existing project.

### Start with a project

Create a project with minimal information → Start a conversation → Configure additional project settings when needed.

## Questions to settle

- Should standalone conversations remain in chat history by default, with an explicitly ephemeral mode handled separately?
- Which project settings can use defaults, and which are genuinely required before a project-specific capability runs?
- When an existing conversation moves into a project, how should project context and settings apply to subsequent messages?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user with no projects can open the application and send a first message without creating or configuring a project.
- [ ] Users can create and continue conversations outside projects.
- [ ] Users can still create conversations directly within a project.
- [ ] A standalone conversation can be moved into a new or existing project without losing its history or associated artifacts.
- [ ] Project creation requires only minimal information; advanced settings can be configured later.
- [ ] Navigation clearly distinguishes standalone conversations from project conversations.
- [ ] Existing projects and their conversations remain accessible.
- [ ] E2E coverage verifies starting a conversation with no projects, creating a project with minimal input, and moving a standalone conversation into a project.
items.title: [Feature] Allow conversations outside projects and simplify project creation

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
The `CodeCheck (GitCode)` check run on GitHub PRs only says "GitCode labelled the merge request `ci-failed`" and links to the GitCode MR. It doesn't name the failing rule or file. The GitCode MR page/API is not reachable for every contributor or reviewer (WAF/login). So authors end up writing "CodeCheck is ignored" (e.g. #421, also failing on #412 and #391), and reviewers can't tell whether a failure comes from the PR.

## Expected
When CodeCheck fails, the GitHub check-run output lists the failing checker/rule, file:line and message (or a stable public log link), so authors and reviewers can act without GitCode access.

## Verification cases
1. **Failure details mirrored**
   - Preconditions: a PR whose head introduces a known CodeCheck violation (e.g. a lint rule the GitCode pipeline enforces).
   - Steps: push; wait for the sync; open the `CodeCheck (GitCode)` check run on GitHub.
   - Expected / pass: `output.summary` or `output.text` names the rule, file:line and message; conclusion `failure`.
2. **Clean head**
   - Preconditions: a PR with no violations.
   - Steps: push; open the check run.
   - Expected / pass: conclusion `success`; no stale failure text from an earlier head.
3. **Infra failure isn't shown as a code failure (negative)**
   - Preconditions: the GitCode pipeline fails for an infra reason (timeout/sync error).
   - Steps: trigger; open the check run.
   - Expected / pass: output says it's an infra/sync failure, not a code violation, and links to a retry path.
4. **No secret leakage (security)**
   - Preconditions: a pipeline log that contains tokens/env.
   - Steps: mirror the failure details.
   - Expected / pass: mirrored text contains no tokens, cookies or internal URLs with credentials.

## Context
Refs #421, Refs #385. Seen at #421 head f494792 (GitCode MR !296) and #412 head 29e724a.
items.title: [Feature] CI: surface GitCode CodeCheck failure details on the GitHub check run

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## User request

When I switch the model in a conversation, I want the next new conversation to start with that model automatically. I should not have to select it again or separately visit settings to make that choice stick.

Example: the configured default is model A. In session 1, I explicitly select model B in the conversation model picker. Every new conversation should initially use model B rather than returning to model A: this includes another session in the same project, a session in a different project, and the first session of a newly created project, even if the target project has a different default. If I later explicitly select model C, the next new session should start with C.

## Current behavior

The conversation picker changes a session override. New sessions inherit the project default model, falling back to the system default, so a choice made in the previous conversation is not automatically reused.

This is a request to change that behavior, rather than only explain it with a tooltip.

## Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- [ ] After an explicit, successfully saved model selection in a conversation, every new conversation starts with that selected model, across all projects and including the first session of a newly created project, without an extra confirmation or a trip to settings.
- [ ] A remembered explicit selection takes precedence over project and system model defaults when initializing any new conversation.
- [ ] A later explicit selection becomes the remembered choice for subsequent new sessions. Merely opening an older conversation does not replace the remembered choice.
- [ ] The remembered choice survives page refresh and application restart.
- [ ] Existing conversations retain their own model selection; creating a conversation does not change other conversations or an in-flight run's model.
- [ ] If there is no remembered selection, normal project-default → system-default inheritance continues to work.
- [ ] If the remembered model has been removed or is no longer selectable, creation falls back to a valid configured default, or shows actionable model configuration feedback if none exists. It must not retain a dangling model selection.
- [ ] The model shown in the new conversation matches its effective saved model. Any scope hint accurately describes the new behavior in both English and Chinese.
- [ ] Repeatable browser regression coverage verifies A → select B → create session → B within the same project, across projects with different defaults, and in a newly created project; a subsequent selection of C; persistence after reload/restart, unchanged existing conversations, and missing-model fallback.

## Selection policy

Use one last explicitly selected model for new conversations, independent of project boundaries. The user requests a Codex-style experience: choose a model once and keep using that choice when starting new conversations. This is the requested interaction policy, rather than a claim about Codex implementation details.

Project boundaries must not reset the remembered selection. Merely viewing an older conversation must not count as choosing its model. Existing conversations retain their own selection. This specifies the initialization behavior; it does not require rewriting every project's settings or changing other users' preferences. The persistence mechanism should follow the product's user/preference model.

## Related issues and current PRs

- #44 describes the same source of confusion, but its proposed solution explicitly retains session-only switching and adds a scope hint. This issue requests remembered selection for new sessions instead. Keep the two acceptance contracts distinct; a hint-only change does not satisfy this request.
- PR #289 is currently an open draft for #44. Its description explicitly says persistence/configuration/selection callbacks are unchanged. It does not implement remembered selection; its hint wording will need to be reconciled if this feature lands.
- #278 concerns configuration from within a conversation and task continuation. It does not require new sessions to reuse the last selected model.
- Closed #336 is an analogous usability request about remembering approval mode/defaults, rather than model selection.

At filing time, a search of open/closed issues and current open PRs found no exact duplicate or open PR implementing this remembered-model behavior.
items.title: [Feature] New sessions should remember the last explicitly selected conversation model

items.body:
## Purpose

Carry forward every unfinished or unverified acceptance item from #37, following the feature triage requested under #563 against release scope #249. This is an administrative split of partial delivery, not a declaration that the original feature is fully implemented.

## Existing delivery and evidence

PR535: model/project actions with 14 unit tests and 7 mocked browser journeys

Reviewed against upstream main `65eddde1` on 2026-10-27. Historical PR test results apply to their recorded candidate revisions only; no new product acceptance tests were run in this triage.

## Remaining work

Choose a license-clean bundled dataset; add one-click project/session creation, sample upload and a prefilled prompt; verify the first result in both locales, keyboard and narrow screens. Existing actions must remain covered.

## Release

Target: release/0.4.0. The sample-analysis enhancement is useful but not required for the packaging/execution/configuration deliverables in #249; completed actionable entry points remain on main.

## Completion rule

- [ ] Account for every original criterion: delivered evidence, remaining implementation, explicit approved alternative, or separately linked follow-up.
- [ ] Run matching acceptance checks on the final candidate and retain actual results; do not treat workflow presence, merged status or historical green CI as full acceptance.
- [ ] Reconcile still-open PRs and original dependencies with the successor issue before merge.

## Original specification (preserved for traceability)

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #90](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/90) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Enter the app for the first time and figure out how to start my first analysis.

## What I saw instead

With no projects yet, the home screen shows a centered empty-state card listing three steps:

1. Configure a model (go to system settings → model registry, then save a provider token);
2. Create a project (its first session opens automatically);
3. Drop a CSV and ask (analyze the CSV and plot charts).

These are plain static list items (empty-state rendering in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`) with no click handlers: clicking "Configure a model" does nothing, and so does "Create a project". There is no composer, no upload area, no sample-data button, and no guided tour.

## Why this is confusing

New users have no idea where to click; the three steps are signposts, but every one of them requires the user to find the destination on their own.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Turn each step into a real action: "Configure a model" opens the matching settings section directly; "Create a project" opens the creation dialog directly.
- Add a prominent primary button "Load sample data and try it now": automatically create an initial project and session, load a bundled sample CSV, and prefill a ready-to-send example prompt, so a new user sees their first chart within seconds.
- Open question (needs a product decision): the theme of the bundled sample CSV and its expected chart types are not decided yet — a public, license-clean scientific dataset should be picked first.

Design notes: making the empty-state steps interactive is low-risk frontend routing/dialog work; the one-click sample needs decisions on data source (bundled vs. downloaded on first run) and topic, which is why it is registered as an open question here.

items.body:
## Purpose

Carry forward every unfinished or unverified acceptance item from #55, following the feature triage requested under #563 against release scope #249. This is an administrative split of partial delivery, not a declaration that the original feature is fully implemented.

## Existing delivery and evidence

PR56/60 delivered bilingual evolve explanation/how-to/tutorial/reference; current tree has core/evolve.md, domains/evolve-a-solution.md and EN developer-docs/evolve-standalone.md

Reviewed against upstream main `65eddde1` on 2026-10-27. Historical PR test results apply to their recorded candidate revisions only; no new product acceptance tests were run in this triage.

## Remaining work

Audit all original documentation criteria against the reorganized current docs, restore missing operational how-to/index/reference coverage if needed, and record an actual supplied-example tutorial run and bilingual parity/link results. Do not recreate pages that already exist.

## Release

Target: release/0.3.0. This remaining scope supports an explicit #249 release deliverable.

## Completion rule

- [ ] Account for every original criterion: delivered evidence, remaining implementation, explicit approved alternative, or separately linked follow-up.
- [ ] Run matching acceptance checks on the final candidate and retain actual results; do not treat workflow presence, merged status or historical green CI as full acceptance.
- [ ] Reconcile still-open PRs and original dependencies with the successor issue before merge.

## Original specification (preserved for traceability)

## Summary

`/evolve` is one of the largest features in the product and has **no user documentation in either language**. A researcher cannot learn what it does, when to reach for it, or how to drive it, without reading the source. I would like an explanation page, a how-to, and a tutorial — in English and Chinese — plus the existing Chinese architecture note fixed up and made reachable.

## What ships versus what is documented

What ships:

| Surface | Size |
|---|---|
| `services/evolve` Python sidecar | 23 modules, two search engines — flat-PUCT (`puct_engine.py`) and MAP-Elites islands with ring migration (`openevolve_engine.py`) |
| Scoring modes | four domain seams: `scorecard_domain` (dataset metric), `test_gate_domain` (test suite), `script_domain` (a scorer the model writes), `judge_domain` (LLM rubric) |
| Agent tools | `create_evolve_run`, `get_evolve_run` |
| Skill | `evolve-design`, a four-checkpoint design conversation with an algorithm choice |
| Web UI | 13 components — panel, algorithm picker, candidate stream, score chart, search graph canvas and table, budget bar, cell grid |
| UI strings | 188 `evolve.*` message keys |
| HTTP API | `/api/evolve/runs`, `/runs/<id>/events`, `/runs/<id>/candidates/<hash>`, `/runs/<id>/stop` |

What is documented:

| Language | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Chinese | **one** file, `docs/zh/explanation/evolve-standalone.md` (252 lines) |
| English | **zero** — the word "evolve" appears in exactly one English file, `docs/en/reference/web-frontend.md`, in passing |

And the single Chinese file has two problems of its own:

1. **It is unreachable.** `docs/zh/explanation/README.md` does not link it. The index lists `skill-library-management.md` and `skill-self-evolution.md` but not `evolve-standalone.md`, so the only way to find it is to list the directory. (Raised as an orphan page in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25).)
2. **It answers a different question.** Its own opening says it covers the two engines' differences and what it would take to run the sidecar as a standalone backend. That is an architecture note for a maintainer. Nothing in it tells a researcher what a search is for, when scoring will actually discriminate, or how to start one.

## What to write

### 1. `explanation/evolve.md` (EN + ZH)

What an evolution search is, and the honest limits: it rewrites a candidate dozens of times and keeps what scores higher, so it succeeds or fails on whether the scoring can tell a good candidate from a bad one — a scoring function that cannot shows up as a flat run, not as an error. Cover the four scoring modes and when each applies, the two engines and when to pick which, and the frozen-scorer rule that `test_gate_domain` enforces, whose upstream note is worth quoting: *"without it the shortest path to a high score is to weaken the thing measuring it."*

### 2. `how-to/run-an-evolution-search.md` (EN + ZH)

The operational path: preparing a starting point and a dataset or test suite, what `--algorithm puct` versus `--algorithm openevolve` changes, reading the score chart and the search graph, budgets and stopping, retrieving the winning candidate, and what the approval card asks for before a run starts.

### 3. `tutorial/…-evolve-a-solution.md` (EN + ZH)

One short end-to-end run a reader can actually complete: a small starting program, a dataset with a metric, the `/evolve-design` conversation answered checkpoint by checkpoint, then what to look at while it runs and how to tell a real improvement from noise. This is the piece [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) asks for in general, applied here.

### 4. Fix what exists

Link `evolve-standalone.md` from the Chinese explanation index, give it an English counterpart, and retitle it so its scope is obvious — it is the engine-internals and standalone-deployment note, not the feature's documentation.

### 5. Reference the surface

The four HTTP endpoints belong in `reference/rest-api.md`, and the two agent tools in `reference/builtin-tools.md`, so the feature is reachable from the reference tree as well as the prose.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An English reader can learn what `/evolve` is, when to use it, and how to run one, without reading source code.
- [ ] Explanation, how-to and tutorial pages exist in both languages and are linked from their indexes.
- [ ] The four scoring modes and the two engines are each documented with the case they suit.
- [ ] The frozen-scorer rule is stated where a user designing a search will meet it.
- [ ] The tutorial runs end to end on a supplied example, and says how to judge whether the result is real.
- [ ] `evolve-standalone.md` is linked, translated, and scoped by its title.
- [ ] The evolve endpoints and agent tools appear in the reference documents.

## Open questions

- Should the tutorial evolve a program (dataset metric) or a prompt (LLM judge)? The program case is more convincing; the prompt case is cheaper to run and needs no dataset.
- Can a small example — a starting program plus a labelled dataset — be committed for the tutorial, as [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) proposes generally?
- Does the Idea Tree engine want the same treatment in the same pass? It has the same shape of gap: `idea-tree-engine.md` is also Chinese-only.

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (documentation completeness and the orphan pages), [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (the tutorial series), [#54](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/54) (RSI, which builds directly on this engine and will be much harder to explain if the engine itself is undocumented).

## Context

This tracks a staged landing for the work currently visible in #315 (GitCode !125), plus the two smaller follow-up branches for KE/trace integration and finish-gate refinements.

The current combined PR is 275 files and about +54k lines. Review feedback has correctly identified both the review/merge risk and the need for an explicit product decision about KE as a first-class ScienceDiscovery surface. I will preserve #315 as the full implementation reference, but stop refreshing it with large upstream merges and instead prepare clean, independently reviewable PRs from current `main`.

## Proposed landing sequence

### A. Independent research/runtime foundations

These do not require the KE service and can be reviewed on their own merits.

- [ ] **A1 — Tool-output trust boundary:** per-run nonce fencing, `untrustedCategory`, MCP remote classification, and the corresponding prompt contract. Raw stored output remains unchanged; fencing applies to model-visible content.
- [ ] **A2 — Research state:** session research state, project ledger hydration/promotion, and tournament ranking primitives.
- [ ] **A3 — Runtime controls:** native stall guard and the `TurnLifecycle.beforeFinish`/continuation event primitives. This will not claim equivalent native-style stall protection for JiuwenSwarm.
- [ ] **A4 — Session Plan:** versioned human approval, decision log, cancellation and recovery, with an explicit compatibility rule for the existing `update_plan` snapshot mechanism.
- [ ] **A5 — Finish-gate core:** skill audit and termination intervention for native and post-run/Swarm execution. The initial landing will include the already-developed fixes for loaded-skill-only audits, Swarm tool aliases, and self-referential gate/verifier text. KE grounding comes later.
- [ ] **A6 — Agent Memory:** candidate memories, human promotion, reviewed-only prompt injection, and background review. The KE LLM-helper dependency and process-global manager need to be removed first.

### B. Knowledge Engine core

- [ ] **B1 — Text/extraction/resolution domain:** pure text, JATS, extraction, and entity-resolution modules with unit tests.
- [ ] **B2 — Graph/growth/eval algorithms:** graph algorithms, gap discovery, growth selection, and evaluation primitives.
- [ ] **B3 — Persistence and ingestion data plane:** SQLite store/migrations, scholarly connectors, PDF/vision parsing, and background runners.
- [ ] **B4 — Orchestration and minimal REST:** orchestrator, grow, routes, and narrowly scoped bootstrap/http wiring. Agent tools, resident summary, graph mirror, and living review stay out of this first REST PR.
- [ ] **B5 — Minimal KE Web shell:** API client, KE page, graph canvas, and document reader.

### C. Agent integration and advanced KE surfaces

- [ ] **C1 — Consumption tools and kbScope:** KE search/expand/grep tools, session binding, web-search restrictions, resident summary, and picker. Scope enforcement lands with the first exposed tool.
- [ ] **C2 — Citation and anti-hallucination runtime:** citation verification, novelty checks, evidence ledger, report polish, and finish-gate grounding. Includes the no-available-KB advisory behavior rather than an unachievable hard lock.
- [ ] **C3 — Reports, DRIFT, and memory-graph bridge:** community reports, DRIFT search, KE-to-memory-graph mirroring, and KB deep links.

### Small follow-ups from the former KE/trace and finish-gate PRs

These can land as soon as their specific dependencies are present; they do not all need to wait for the entire base series.

- [ ] Paper presence lookup and KB badge (after minimal REST + Web).
- [ ] Explicit Paper-to-KB re-ingest (after presence lookup).
- [ ] Reviewer citation checks with a bound-KB short circuit (after citation verification + kbScope).
- [ ] KB reader back-link to the current session memory graph (after graph mirroring).
- [ ] `gap_candidates` to deduplicated `research_state` open questions (after research state + observer wiring).
- [ ] Quoting-discipline skill updates and catalog/version pins with their corresponding gate/skill stages.

## Per-stage requirements

- Each PR is cut from current `main`; mixed files such as `store.ts`, `runs/index.ts`, `http/index.ts`, and `App.tsx` are ported by focused hunks rather than copied wholesale.
- Unit/integration tests and the relevant journeys land with their feature, not in a final test-only PR.
- Current-main behavior is preserved, including catalog transaction/rollback semantics, deletion-settling shutdown, response identity, and Swarm skill-selection behavior.
- Tool trust is field-aware: deterministic verdicts must not implicitly make corpus titles, abstracts, snippets, or entity descriptions trusted.
- The fenced evidence-ledger path, post-run terminal-event ordering, and no-engine kbScope behavior receive explicit integration coverage.
- Runtime-affecting stages receive a clean deployment and real E2E validation before the next stage.

Unless maintainers prefer a dedicated integration branch, the default is small PRs directly to `main`, with at most one or two open at a time. Feedback on the staged product scope and on starting with **A1 + B1** would be appreciated.

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 9d9ba398ccce4763b47f946f890661f6
Branch: dev2/fix/777-named-entity-decoding
Base: 7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204
At: 2026-11-03T02:07:55Z

## ScienceDiscovery evidence-backed issue

**Live main:** `7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204` (`test(cas): cover the multi-chunk intact layout and align the materialize contract with #708`)
**Area:** `packages/data-source` — HTML text extraction used by the free search engines
**Filed by:** ScienceDiscovery Product

### Problem

`decodeEntities` resolves only five named references (`amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`) and leaves every other named reference literal, so search-result titles and snippets reach the model and the report as `café`, `5–10`, `—`, `…`, `O'Brien`.

### Reproduction on live main

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

Actual output (main `7942ad1f`):

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

Expected (browser-equivalent text): `café — 5–10 … O'Brien`, `<b> stays text` (single pass preserved), `♦ … ’`.

### Evidence (file:line on this main)

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:27-33` — `NAMED_ENTITIES` contains exactly `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:46-53` — `decodeEntities` matches **any** named reference (`([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)`) and returns `NAMED_ENTITIES.get(name) ?? match`, i.e. everything else falls through as literal text.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:55-58` — `textOf` (strip tags → decode → collapse) is the shared extractor.
- Call sites that turn this into user-visible text: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/free-engines.ts:64`, `:69`, `:136`, `:141`, `:183`, `:192` (titles/snippets), plus `:68`, `:135`, `:181` for result URLs.

### Impact

DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave result titles and snippets are what `web_search` returns to the model and what reports cite; a page title like "Café culture — a review" is rendered literally, so the evidence shown to the user (and fed back into the prompt) carries entity codes instead of text. Entity-heavy pages are exactly the older/European and encyclopedia sources a science search hits often.

### Expected vs actual

- Expected: named references decode the same way a browser renders them (at minimum the typographic and Latin-1 names that appear in titles: `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `rsquo`, `lsquo`, `ldquo`, `rdquo`, `eacute`, `egrave`, `ouml`, `apos`, `middot`, `times`, `deg`, `plusmn`, …).
- Actual: only 5 names decode; the rest stay literal.

### Acceptance

1. `decodeEntities` resolves the named references it matches (full HTML5 named set, or a documented bounded table that covers at least the names listed above).
2. The single-pass guarantee from #672 is preserved: `&lt;` → `<`, `&amp;` → `&`; decoded output is never rescanned.
3. Surrogate / non-character rejection stays as it is (`�` etc. remain literal).
4. `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts` gains cases for the named references above, and the existing five keep passing.
5. No change to numeric-reference behavior (`A`, `A`, `😀`).

### Not a duplicate

Open-issue search for `entity`, `entity decode`, `html text extraction`, `named entity` returns no open report; the only entity issue is closed #672 (double decoding), whose fix this preserves. No open PR touches `html.ts` (`#663`/`#678` are the UTF-16 truncation family in other modules).
