The repository already contains skills, specialists and connectors, but they are only discoverable by reading the tree, and a research session package (`.sdresearch`) has no home at all once it is produced. This adds the hub. A build-time exporter projects the tracked sources into download artifacts and an import catalogue; the database is the source of the site's browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`); nginx serves the site beside the API, so page, catalogue and downloads share one origin. Accounts, uploads, version history, review and short-lived download links live behind `/api/v1`, modelled on the openJiuwen Agentic Hub reference, and the importer carries the existing catalogue across.

Earlier this was two pull requests (#1225 and #1243); they now ship as one change, because the site switch and the importer only make sense with the service.

## The site (`apps/hub`)

Five tabs — skills, team skills, specialists, connectors and session packages — share one category tree, a searchable list and a detail view. Routes are real paths (`/skills/<id>`, `/teams/<id>`, `/sessions/<id>`), so a refresh or a shared link resolves to the same asset. Every asset exposes its README and a download. The UI is bilingual (zh/en) and follows the Agentic Hub reference: gradient hero, per-tab counts, segmented tabs, a pill search, an icon-led rail that becomes a chip strip below 900 px, and the reference's 1600 px container with a 1536 px detail card.

Downloads open the browser's save dialog where the browser has one (Chrome and Edge), so the file goes to the folder the person picks; the bytes come from a same-origin `/api/v1/artifacts/{id}/content` endpoint, which a private bucket needs no CORS rule for, and the plain navigation to the presigned URL remains the fallback. Session headers show a localized run time and the model the package recorded; obvious placeholders such as `local-*` are not shown as if they were a model.

Detail pages carry the tile, name, category, version pill and the primary download; beneath them a reading column (description, Readme and Files tabs) sits beside a "Basic information" card that shows only fields the catalog carries. Files is a two-pane browser: the left pane lists exactly what the archive holds — SKILL.md plus every resource, with its size — and the right pane renders the selected file in place, markdown for `.md`, a source listing for text files, a note instead of a preview for binaries.

## The exporter (`scripts/hub`)

`pnpm hub:export` reads only tracked sources — `skills/`, `packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`, `packages/mcp-sources/src/*` and `extensions_config.json` — and writes `apps/hub/public/`, which is gitignored because every input is tracked. Skill and specialist archives are built in memory (`fflate`), so an export needs no network and no temporary directory. Each skill's files are also copied to `skills/<id>/<path>` (44 files, 0.42 MB) so the Files tab never unpacks a zip in the browser.

## External skills and session packages

`pnpm hub:sync-skills` freezes a snapshot of the MindScienceSkills tree (364 skills) from GitCode into `snapshot.tar.gz` and `index.json`; extraction refuses absolute paths and `..` entries.

A session drop is `<id>.sdresearch` plus an `<id>.json` sidecar, and publication is all-or-nothing: one bad package aborts before the first byte is written. Verification enforces the contract — 50 MiB cap, whole-file sha256, the manifest inventory, `records.json` hashed but never parsed. The published `sessions/index.json` is the persistent index; a run merges by id, a package leaves only through an explicit `unpublish`, and unpublishing leaves the uploaded file in place so old links keep working.

## Deployment

The site is served by nginx at `/`, which proxies `/api/` to the service, so page, catalogue and download content share one origin. `docker-compose.yml` runs MySQL, the API and nginx on one host; `pnpm hub:build:api --root` builds the site without the exporter, and the database is the source of the browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`).

The static publishing workflows are gone: a production write is a deployment, not a push to `main`. The exporter remains as the importer's input, and `pnpm hub:sync-skills` remains a manual snapshot step.

## The backend (`services/hub-api`)

FastAPI + SQLAlchemy. The reference establishes the shape: an asset row carrying what the site shows, a version row carrying what a download serves, review state on the version, and `public_latest_version` deciding what is listed. This keeps that contract and differs where our data does: five asset kinds in one lifecycle (`skill`, `team`, `specialist`, `connector`, `session`) instead of six per-type models; no plugin-specific schema validation; stateless HMAC session tokens instead of Redis, so the database is the only stateful dependency; and the reference's `{code, message, data}` envelope and `/api/v1/...` paths.

Uploads are validated before anything is written: the 50 MiB cap measured on the bytes rather than `Content-Length`, path traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, encrypted and duplicate entries, an uncompressed-size ceiling, and a per-entry sha256 inventory that becomes the Files tab. Downloads resolve through `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`, which checks visibility and returns a short-lived presigned URL. Registration closes after the first account, which is the administrator; later accounts come from the administrator.

## Storage and data placement

One private bucket; keys are `assets/<kind>/<publisher>/<asset>/<version>/<filename>` composed in one function. Nothing is anonymously readable, and a bucket listing is refused. Metadata — assets, versions, manifests, users, review state, audit — lives in the database; the bytes live in the bucket; the site and its `catalog.json` remain static files served by the front end.

## Importer and site switch

`scripts/import_catalog.py` reads the exporter's `catalog.json` and writes the same data into the database and the bucket: it preserves catalogue ids, verifies each artifact against the catalogue's sha256 before uploading, wraps single-file specialists and connectors in a one-entry archive while checking the digest against the file rather than the wrapper, marks imported versions approved, and is idempotent. `--dry-run` validates without writing.

The site gets one build-time switch: with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE=/api/v1` the download button asks the API for a URL before navigating, which a private bucket requires; if that call fails the anchor still points at the catalogue URL, so a static deployment is unchanged.

## CI

`hub-api.yml` runs the service's tests and builds its image on changes under `services/hub-api`; it is informational and not part of `merge-gate`. The hub's exporter and site checks run in the UT layer, which builds the workspace: L1 stays the static slice (install only), matching the repository's layering.

## Screenshots

Taken from the built site against the local stack (Chromium, 1440 and 390 CSS px):

| Home, 1440 | Detail with the Files tab, 1440 |
|---|---|
| ![Home at 1440](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-1440.png) | ![Detail Files tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-files-1440.png) |

| Detail in Chinese, 1440 | Home at 390 |
|---|---|
| ![Chinese detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-zh-1440.png) | ![Home at 390](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-390.png) |

## Validation

- `pnpm hub:test`: 44 passed (4 suites), including the case asserting every served skill file matches the repository byte for byte.
- `python -m pytest` in `services/hub-api`: 18 passed — registration and its closing, login, tampered tokens, administrator-created accounts, upload → pending → hidden, approval → listed and downloadable with matching sha256, rejection, owner-only uploads, the Files listing and text preview, path-shaped ids through the `%2F` encoding, the size/traversal/non-zip refusals, and the importer end to end including idempotence and a checksum mismatch.
- Importer against the real catalogue: 387 assets, 385 versions, two session packages skipped because their `.sdresearch` files were not in the site tree.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and the hub build with and without the API switch.
- The earlier static-hub layers (UT 7718 planned / 7687 executed / 7670 passed, ST 63 planned / 62 passed, mocked E2E 188 planned / 181 passed) were measured on `de624faa`; the failures are this host's known constants and are itemised in the commit history of the branch. UI-only commits after that re-ran typecheck, build and `hub:test`.

## E2E user journeys

**Static site — PASS.** Driven in headless Chromium at 1440, 768 and 390 CSS px in English and 390 in Chinese: `document.scrollWidth` equals `clientWidth` on home and detail pages, the rail becomes a chip strip below 900 px, deep links resolve after a reload, session READMEs are fetched from the sibling prefix, and the Files browser lists and previews the archive's contents. A publication increment kept the entries it did not deliver (1 → 2 → 3 packages, every earlier URL still 200), and unpublishing removed only the named id while its file still returned 200.

**Backend — PASS on a local stack.** MySQL 8.0 (container) + the service + the built site + the real bucket, driven over HTTP and in Chromium; not yet on a deployment host.

- Import into MySQL and OBS: 387 assets, 385 versions; two sessions skipped as above.
- `http://127.0.0.1:8612/site/skills/antibody-design`: the button's static `href` is `/site/packages/antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`; the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/antibody-design?version=1.0.0` and the presigned URL serves 109171 bytes whose sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- The path-id external skill `astronomy/astronomical_analysis/astropy`: the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/astronomy%2Fastronomical_analysis%2Fastropy?version=snapshot-20261117` and the download's sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- Over HTTP, not the test client: administrator login, create, upload (`201`, `pending`), approve, download; the bytes match, and the test asset and object were removed.
- The bucket is private: an unsigned `GET` of an object returns `403`, as does a bucket listing.
- The save dialog path was driven in Chromium with the picker stubbed (headless cannot show the dialog): suggested name `antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`, 109171 bytes written, equal to the catalogue's size; the session header reads `Run at Nov 17, 2026, 6:38 AM` and `Model DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, with no `local-smoke`.

Building against the real bucket surfaced three fixes now in the branch: boto3 1.36+ adds a CRC32 trailer OBS rejects (`XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch`); external skill ids are paths up to 88 characters (84 exceed 64), so columns are 191 and routes use a path converter; and the development host's clock is 28 minutes fast, which SigV4 rejects — the smoke tooling compensates, the service deliberately does not, and its README states that the deployment host must run NTP.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` — the GitHub label is pending a maintainer, because this account has no write access to the upstream repository's labels.

User impact: a static site lists the repository's skills, specialists, connectors and session packages with READMEs and downloads; assets can also be published into a service with accounts, review and version history, served from a private bucket through short-lived links.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing behaviour. New app, new service, new scripts and three workflows. The database schema is created at startup and the importer is the migration path from `catalog.json`; the static publishing pipeline keeps working while the backend is introduced.

CSV 重复 ID 处理生成的后缀可能与输入中已有的 ID 相同，导致多条记录共用一个内部标识。点击值为 `333` 的记录时，会同时高亮两行，详情面板却显示 `111`。

## 保证 CSV 记录的内部标识唯一

- 为记录分配内部标识时，检查其是否与已分配的标识冲突；缺少原始 ID 时生成的标识也执行相同检查。
- 为每个基础标识记录下一次可尝试的后缀，避免大量重复 ID 反复扫描已占用的后缀。
- 保留原始 CSV 单元格值和解析结果的确定性，每条受影响的记录只计入一次重复 ID 警告。

复现数据：

```csv
id,value
sample#4,111
sample,222
sample,333
```

打开 CSV 可视化，切换到 **Data table（数据表）**，点击值为 **333** 的记录。修复后只高亮这一行，详情面板显示 **333**。

## 验证结果

测试提交：`82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7`，基于 `main` 的 `c33c1ae2b7100ab86de451afb02aefe0bd7a3045`。

- CSV 测试：**通过 29 / 失败 0 / 跳过 0**。其中三项 ID 冲突回归用例在修复前均失败。
- 性能回归：包含 20,000 个已占用后缀 ID 和 20,000 个重复 ID 的 40,000 行 CSV，在加入后缀游标前超过子进程的 10 秒时限；加入游标后，本地测试约 287 毫秒完成。
- UT（`pnpm ci:ut`）：计划 **3723**，执行 **3723**，通过 **3723**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- ST（`pnpm ci:st`）：计划 **2**，执行 **2**，通过 **2**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 静态检查（`pnpm ci:l1`）：计划 **4**，执行 **4**，通过 **4**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 使用模拟模型的浏览器 E2E（`pnpm ci:e2e`）：计划 **71**，执行 **71**，通过 **71**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 加入后缀游标后，独立代码审查未发现仍需处理的问题。

此前测试失败及原因：

- 首次 UT **3721/3723** 通过：本机 bubblewrap 0.6.1 不支持 `--disable-userns`，且克隆固定版本的研究评估器时发生 TLS 连接中断。
- 另一次 UT **3720/3723** 通过。其中两项评估相关失败在未修改的 `main` 上同样出现（**3717/3719** 通过）：Python 3.14 与固定版本的 SciPy 不兼容，以及全局评估器路径覆盖使另一项契约检查暴露出依赖缺失。将固定版本的评估器准备到预期缓存位置，并使用 Python 3.12.13 后，两项问题均解决。其余一项权限队列断言属于间歇性失败：该用例在 `main`、较早的修复分支测试，以及使用全新服务状态的最终完整测试中均通过。
- 首次完整浏览器测试执行 **71** 项，**通过 70 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**；CSV 流程已通过。唯一失败是 J3 的托管 Python 环境前置条件，Conda 下载依赖时出现 `SSL routines::unexpected eof while reading`。未修改的 `main` 执行 **70** 项，**通过 69 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**，复现了相同问题。修复分支重新测试时使用单独复制并补齐的依赖缓存。

## E2E 用户流程

提交 `82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7` 在浏览器和本机进程运行的产品环境中验证**通过**。完整模拟模型浏览器测试 **71/71** 通过，**失败 0 / 阻塞 0 / 跳过 0**。

CSV 流程的 **4/4** 个用户步骤全部通过：通过真实沙箱生成并声明 CSV 产物、打开可视化、点击 **333**，再依次切换 **111 → 222 → 333**。预期与实际结果一致：始终只高亮一条记录，选中数量为 1，详情值与所选记录一致，并保留原始 ID。同一操作也已在正在运行的本地产品中手动验证。

可复用用例位于 `test/journey-inspect-csv-records.spec.ts`，纳入 `pnpm ci:e2e`。该流程使用独立的本地模拟模型，覆盖无需真实模型凭据的 PR 测试场景。最终完整测试使用单独复制并补齐的科学计算依赖缓存，J3 的环境创建、使用、审计和删除流程也全部通过。

## 发布说明

发布类别：`release:fix`

用户影响：选择存在 ID 冲突的 CSV 记录时，详情面板显示该记录的数据，并且只高亮所选行。

兼容性与迁移：无需迁移。原始 CSV 值保持不变；重新打开 CSV 时，受影响的内部行标识会重新生成为唯一值。

贡献者账号没有上游仓库写入权限，GitHub 的 `release:fix` 标签需由维护者添加。

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
Closes #1271

## The defect

The release-version gate read `application/package.json`'s `version` from the **working tree**. On a `pull_request` event the checkout is the **merge commit** — the head merged into the current base — while the comparison point came from `pull_request.base.sha`. A branch based on an older `main` was therefore compared against a tree it never wrote.

The incident: #1264, based on `222e7b06` (0.4.1) while `main` had moved to `0c3d4d52` (0.4.0-rc1, from #1258). The branch changes only `services/api/**`, but the merge tree carried `0.4.0-rc1`, so the gate reported a release change:

```
CI policy failed: application/package.json moves 0.4.1 -> 0.4.0-rc1, which is a
release change, but the title "fix(api): tell /distill-session it has nothing to
distil" does not start with "chore(release):".
```

`Select CI policy` fails first, so L1, UT and ST are skipped and `merge-gate` fails: **nothing on that head is validated**. Rebasing the same head onto current `main` made it pass, which is what identified the trigger as the stale base rather than the change.

Impact: every pull request whose branch is behind `main` is blocked before L1 by a rule it does not violate, and the only workaround — rebase — is undiscoverable and clears approvals.

## The fix

Both sides of the comparison now come from git objects:

```js
const headVersion = versionOf(showFile(head, VERSION_FILE));
const baseVersion = versionOf(showFile(base, VERSION_FILE));
...
const files = Object.fromEntries(RELEASE_METADATA.map(path => [path, readFromHead(path)]));
```

The working tree is not consulted at all. `pull_request.head.sha` is now required alongside `base.sha`, and its absence is a named error rather than a silent pass. The success line prints the version it accepted **from the head commit**, so a stale checkout can no longer make a green gate look like it verified something else:

```
release version OK: application/package.json at 0.4.1 (head 222e7b06a418)
```

## Verification

- **The incident, on real commits:** with the working tree at current `main` (`0.4.0-rc1`) and an event whose `base` and `head` are both `222e7b06` (`0.4.1`), the check now answers `release version OK … at 0.4.1 (head 222e7b06a418)`, rc=0. Before the change the same shape produced the failure above.
- **New regression case** (`a branch behind main is not a version bump (#1271)`): base and head both 0.4.1, and it asserts that no metadata file is even read. Plus `every metadata file is read from the pull request head, and the base from the base`, and a case asserting an event without `head.sha` is refused.
- **Mutation check:** restoring the working-tree read fails three cases, including the #1271 one (`22 pass, 3 fail`); restored, 25/25. So the regression case is load-bearing, not decorative.
- `.ci/*.test.mjs` — the whole selftest including the contract test: **178/178**.
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check`: catalog OK.

## Note on the gate's placement

This changes `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` only — no workflow file, no job in the graph. The placement of the gate itself was settled on #1258 (`policy` job) and is not reopened here.

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
Closes #1265

A provider that refuses `temperature` failed every run with the generic `semantic-error [181001]`, even though the same endpoint served another model fine. The request was always retryable — the field the provider named simply was not on the list of fields this client is willing to drop.

## Root cause

Verified on `main` `a117ae99`, not taken from the report:

- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:346` copies whatever sampling the swarm request carries into the model policy (`temperature`, `top_p`).
- `packages/model/src/client.ts:1574` (`:1594`, `:1614` for the OpenAI Responses and Anthropic variants) writes it into the provider request whenever the policy has it.
- The only 400 recovery is `rejectedControlFallback` (`packages/model/src/client.ts:938`). It gated on a hardcoded thinking-control regex — `/(thinking|reasoning|enable_thinking|chat_template_kwargs)/i` — so a detail that named only `temperature` never reached the per-field check, and `retryWithoutRejectedFields` returned `undefined`. The error was rethrown and the run ended.
- Two further reasons it would still have failed after adding the field to the list, both found while implementing:
  - `rejectedControlWording` (`:833`) is the vocabulary that proves a *parameter* was rejected. It read `unsupported|not supported|…|not allowed|not permitted|no such parameter`, and **`deprecated` was not in it** — which is exactly the word this provider used.
  - the candidate list the retreat is built from was the thinking controls only (`thinkingControlFields`, `:815`).

## What changed

- `temperature` and `top_p` join the retry candidates: `samplingControlFields` is added to a new `retryableControlFields`, which is what the pre-filter, the per-field wording check, the stripped retry, and the retry budget now use.
- `deprecated` and `no longer supported` are added to the rejection vocabulary, so "`temperature` is deprecated for this model" is recognised as a parameter rejection.
- The pre-filter no longer hardcodes thinking words: it asks whether the detail names any field this client can drop.
- The helpers that were thinking-only are renamed to say what they do now (`rejectedRetryableControlFields`, `carriedRetryableControls`, `withoutNamedFields`, `rememberRejectedControls`, …); their two consumers (`services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`, and a doc reference in `completion.ts`) follow.
- The existing safety rule is untouched: a complaint about a control's **value** or the **state** it was sent in still strips nothing. `valueComplaintWording` keeps `when … is enabled/on/set` out of the rejection path, so "temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled" still fails the call rather than silently changing the requested mode.

## Tests

Two new cases in `packages/model/src/client.test.ts`, both with a stub server:

- **the fix**: the server answers `400 {"message":"`temperature` is deprecated for this model."}` when `temperature` is present and streams a normal turn when it is not. The first turn succeeds after the strip, `top_p` (which the 400 never named) survives, and a second turn sends no `temperature` — the rejection is remembered for the endpoint.
- **the guard**: a 400 saying "temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled" is still not a rejection — the call fails once and `temperature` is never stripped.

Mutation-checked, each revert turning the first case red and the file restored afterwards:

| Reverted | Result |
| --- | --- |
| sampling fields dropped from the retry list | `not ok — a 400 that deprecates a sampling field strips it…` |
| `deprecated` removed from the wording | same case red |
| pre-filter restored to the thinking-only regex | same case red |

## Verification

- `packages/model` `node --import tsx --test src/client.test.ts`: **49/49**, including the two new cases. Run on this Windows host with the suite's `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run only — the file declares `os:linux`, and the tag was restored before pushing, so CI is what reports the tagged run.
- `tsc -p packages/model/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repository root): clean.

## Deliberately not in this PR

- **The gateway keeps forwarding sampling to endpoints that never asked for it.** `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:346` could stop passing `temperature`/`top_p` for endpoints the user configured no sampling for, which would avoid the 400 entirely. That is a behaviour change for every provider — a model that currently receives the swarm's own defaults would stop receiving them — so it belongs in its own change with its own evidence. This PR fixes the failure, not the habit.
- **`services/evolve` is untouched.** `completion.py:116-121` already omits `temperature` by default for the same reason; that is a separate path and a separate fix history.
- **Where `temperature: 0.95` / `top_p: 0.95` come from is not claimed.** The swarm log states it produced those numbers, and `GET /api/models` on the reporting install carries no sampling fields, so it is a JiuwenSwarm/openJiuwen default — and that source is not in this repository. **I could not locate it**, so this description does not name one.

## Risk

The retry only happens after a `400` that names a field the request actually carried, and it stops as soon as the field is accepted. A provider that accepts `temperature` sees exactly the request it saw before.

## Summary

Fixes #264.

Make proxy setup usable from one **Network and proxy** settings entry, and keep local application transport independent of outbound proxy failures. Reuse the existing proxy registry, downloader cache/retry, and environment-readiness mechanisms rather than adding an automatic external-network startup gate.

## Changes

- Offer environment configuration, a custom HTTP(S)/SOCKS5 proxy, or direct access. Keep named proxies, bypass hosts and Web/MCP overrides under advanced settings; existing model overrides remain compatible.
- Stage proxy changes across settings tabs. The footer saves them; Cancel/X discards unsaved changes. Add an authenticated, non-persisting download-source connection diagnostic.
- Declare and lock Python HTTP/WebSocket SOCKS dependencies. Adapter loopback HTTP/WebSocket connections explicitly bypass outbound proxies; external HTTP clients are initialized lazily.
- Add small source-loadable shared routing/download helpers. Resolve model requests against their actual target, respect bypass rules, and pass the global policy to managed environment setup/create/install operations without mutating process-wide environment variables.
- Wire the saved global route into both Runner clients: the control plane's own local Runner, and every remote Runner that `RemoteComputeClient` deploys or installs into. Environment mode resolves on the remote Runner itself; a custom URL pointing at the control host's loopback is refused with the reason and the two ways out, because forwarding it would make the remote Runner call itself.
- Refuse proxy settings that cannot be applied instead of degrading silently: a `url` policy without an address, and a proxy URL carrying a path or query (rejected at save time as well, so a stored value cannot fail only per request). The generated `NO_PROXY` lists `::1` rather than `[::1]`, which no consumer matches against a bare hostname.
- Preserve underlying, redacted network errors and existing pinned versions, SHA-256/TLS verification, caches and retries. Update English/Chinese configuration, architecture and REST documentation, including the settings-projection contract change (environment summaries now mask credentials and query strings).

## Rebase onto `main` (`b31f74eb`)

- The branch was 699 commits behind and conflicted in three files. `packages/model/src/client.ts`, `services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`, `packages/executor` and the gateway tests were re-derived from `main`, then the PR's own deltas re-applied one hunk at a time.
- `normalizeUsage` is gone from this PR: `main` moved it to `packages/model/src/usage.ts` and already reads the protocol field per dialect with alias fallback, so the bug this branch started from is fixed upstream. Keeping the branch copy would have reverted that.
- The branch's `services/adapter/uv.lock` is dropped because `main` deleted the lockfile (`feat(sizeopt)`).
- The branch's last commit (`a49f92ed`, "preserve current runtime interfaces after rebase") is dropped: it reverted `model-connectivity.ts`, `client.ts` and the adapter `network.py` to the branch's older shape, i.e. it undid upstream work rather than preserving the PR. Its only real purpose was to make the stale branch compile, which the re-application above now covers.

## Validation

No real LLM API calls or paid tokens were used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter` builds: `schema`, `data-source`, `model`, `executor`, `runner`, `api` | Passed |
| `pnpm --recursive typecheck` plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | Passed |
| Proxy transport, resolver, connectivity (`packages/data-source`, `services/api`) | 14 passed |
| Model client and dispatcher regressions (`packages/model`) | 46 passed |
| Runner client proxy propagation (`packages/executor`) | 7 passed |
| Web settings component suite (`apps/web`) | 258 passed |
| `pnpm architecture:check` / `pnpm ci:selftest` | 43 / 16 passed |
| `services/runner` environment-store, `services/api` store/server suites | Not runnable on this Windows host (`os:linux` tags, bubblewrap, SQLite unlink); CI covers them |
| Adapter hermetic pytest | Not runnable here (no usable Python); CI covers it |

The browser journeys use a real local API/Swarm stack, not mocked settings storage. They cover basic defaults; custom proxy save/cancel; cross-tab drafts; reload persistence; NO_PROXY; Web/MCP overrides and inheritance; rejection of deleting an in-use proxy; and removing references plus deleting the proxy in one save. Only the first journey's connection-test response is browser-mocked; transport ST tests exercise local HTTP/SOCKS proxy fixtures and authentication failures without external access.

The legacy layout E2E is adapted but remains quarantined and was not run. No production service was restarted.

## Scope and boundaries

- This does not grant sandbox network access or add an automatic direct fallback when a configured proxy fails.
- The manual diagnostic checks one download source, not every provider or model credentials. There is no new startup preflight framework or traffic dashboard.
- Saving multiple settings sections is sequential, not a cross-section transaction: a later failure does not roll back earlier successful requests. Unsaved changes remain drafts.
- SOCKS5 support in Undici remains experimental. Remote end-to-end proxy reachability, binary installation and real external providers have not been newly exercised by this PR.

recent_closed_unmerged.author: ink999107
recent_closed_unmerged.body:
The hub currently publishes and downloads, but a merged PR is the only way to add anything: there is no account, no upload, no review, no version history, and no way to keep an asset invisible until someone approves it. This adds the backend those four requirements need, modelled on the openJiuwen Agentic Hub reference, and the two pieces that make the switch a deployment step rather than a rewrite: an importer for the existing catalogue and one build-time switch in the site.

**Stacked on #1225.** The static hub is that pull request. This branch is based on its head, so until #1225 merges the diff below includes it; the backend itself is the four commits on top.

## The service (`services/hub-api`)

FastAPI + SQLAlchemy. The reference establishes the shape: an asset row carrying what the site shows, a version row carrying what a download serves, review state on the version, and `public_latest_version` deciding what is listed. This keeps that contract and differs where our data does:

- Five asset kinds in one lifecycle (`skill`, `team`, `specialist`, `connector`, `session`) instead of six per-type models.
- No plugin-specific schema validation; a version is a zip or `.sdresearch` plus an inventory. The server validates what a server must: the 50 MiB cap measured on the bytes rather than `Content-Length`, path traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, encrypted and duplicate entries, and an uncompressed-size ceiling. Every entry's size and sha256 become the manifest the Files tab renders.
- Stateless HMAC session tokens instead of a Redis-backed store, and scrypt password hashing, so the database is the only stateful dependency.
- The response envelope (`{code, message, data}`) and the public paths (`/api/v1/assets`, `/api/v1/artifacts/{id}`) match the reference, so a client can be repointed.

Endpoints: register/login/me (`{id, username, display_name, role}` payloads), asset list/detail/create/update, version upload/list/detail, the files listing with `with_content`, `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}?version=` returning a presigned URL, and an admin review queue with approve/reject. Registration closes after the first account; that account is the administrator, and later accounts come from `POST /api/v1/auth/users`.

## Storage and access

One private bucket; keys are `assets/<kind>/<publisher>/<asset>/<version>/<filename>` composed in one function. Nothing is anonymously readable: a download resolves through the API, which checks visibility and returns a URL that expires (`HUB_PRESIGN_SECONDS`, default 10 minutes). External skill ids are paths (`chemistry_and_materials/real_world_workstations/…`), so storage keys validate the id segment by segment and the API routes it with a path converter.

## The importer

`scripts/import_catalog.py` reads the exporter's `catalog.json` and writes the same data into the database and the bucket. It preserves catalogue ids, verifies each artifact against the catalogue's sha256 before uploading, wraps the single-file specialists and connectors in a one-entry archive while checking the digest against the file rather than the wrapper, marks each imported version approved, and is idempotent. `--dry-run` validates without writing.

## The site

One build-time switch: with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE=/api/v1` the download button asks the API for a short-lived URL before navigating, which is what a private bucket requires. If that call fails the anchor still points at the catalogue URL, so a static deployment behaves exactly as before. Listing, README and the Files tab still come from `catalog.json`.

## CI

`hub-api.yml` runs the service's tests and builds its image on changes under `services/hub-api`.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest` in `services/hub-api`: **13 passed**. Covers registration and its closing, login, tampered tokens, administrator-created accounts, upload → pending → hidden, approval → listed and downloadable with matching sha256, rejection, owner-only uploads, the Files listing and text preview, path-shaped ids through the `%2F` encoding the site sends, the size/traversal/non-zip refusals, and the importer end to end (including idempotence and a checksum mismatch).
- `python -m scripts.import_catalog --dry-run` against the real catalogue: 387 assets, 385 versions, two session packages skipped because their `.sdresearch` files are not in the site tree.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub build`, with and without the API switch.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS on a local stack** — this host's MySQL 8.0 (container) + the service + the built site + the real OBS bucket, driven over HTTP and in Chromium. Not yet on a deployment host; that is the next step when one is available.

- Import into MySQL and OBS: `assets: 387 created`, `versions: 385 imported`, the two sessions above skipped. Keys land under `assets/<kind>/…` in the bucket.
- Chromium, `http://127.0.0.1:8612/site/skills/antibody-design`: the button's static `href` is `/site/packages/antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`; the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/antibody-design?version=1.0.0` and the presigned URL serves 109171 bytes whose sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- Chromium, the path-id external skill `astronomy/astronomical_analysis/astropy`: the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/astronomy%2Fastronomical_analysis%2Fastropy?version=snapshot-20261117` and the download's sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- HTTP, not the test client: login as the administrator, create an asset, upload (`201`, `pending`), approve (`200`), download; the bytes match, and the test asset and object were removed afterwards.
- The bucket is private: an unsigned `GET` of an object returns `403`, as does a bucket listing.

Building the real service against OBS surfaced two fixes that are in this branch: boto3 1.36+ adds a CRC32 trailer that OBS rejects (`XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch`), so checksum calculation is `when_required`; and asset ids longer than 64 characters (88 is the maximum, 84 exceed 64) needed wider columns and path-aware routes.

The host clock is 28 minutes ahead, which SigV4 rejects. The smoke tooling compensates for a drifting development host; the service deliberately does not, and its README says the deployment host must run NTP.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` — the GitHub label is pending a maintainer, because this account has no write access to the upstream repository's labels.

User impact: accounts, uploads, version history and review can exist behind the hub; downloads can come from a private bucket through short-lived URLs.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing behaviour. The static exporter and the public-read publishing workflow are unchanged; the site only changes shape when built with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE`. The database is new and its schema is created at startup; the importer is the migration path from `catalog.json`.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
An Idea Tree stage gets exactly one correction when its answer is malformed. An empty or truncated answer did not: `research.py:351` raised before the branch that re-asks with `correction` and `previousResponse`, so `ask()` saw a failed activity and `run()` settled the whole research `interrupted` after a single call — a call that spent model tokens and could have been retried.

`transport()` returns the provider's `choices[0].message.content` verbatim (`research.py:279`), so an HTTP 200 whose content is empty or `null` is exactly what reaches this check. It is stage-agnostic: `design`, `ideate`, each assessor, `aggregate` and `propagate` all go through `_ask`.

## The change

The empty check now sits inside the same `try` as validation, so an empty answer takes the single correction: the model is told its previous answer was empty (`correction: empty or truncated model output; stage cannot continue`) and may answer again. A second empty answer still fails the stage, with `reason` naming the role, exactly as a malformed answer does.

```python
try:
    if raw is None or isinstance(raw, str) and not raw.strip():
        raise ValueError('empty or truncated model output; stage cannot continue')
    result = validate_result(role, parse_json(raw), {...})
```

## The policy behind it

This is the remaining half of #1327; the over-depth half was fixed in #1297 (trim to the ceiling, keep the removed direction as `trimmedDirection`), and a bad ideation round is already skipped at run level there. The issue asked which policy to take for an empty answer, and the release owner chose the first option on 2026-11-25: **route it through the existing single correction**. The two rejected alternatives, and why:

- **A separate retry budget for empty content** (2-3 resends with backoff): extra tokens and a second kind of retry to account for, for a failure that the existing correction already covers.
- **Degrade to `completed` when the answer stays unusable**: that turns a genuinely broken model into an apparent success. A second unusable answer still settles the research `interrupted` with the stage in `reason`, which is what keeps the failure visible.

## Tests

One test changes with the behaviour, deliberately and visibly, and two cases are added:

| Test | What it pins |
| --- | --- |
| `test_empty_or_truncated_stage_consumes_the_correction_and_preserves_usage` (was `…_preserves_usage_without_format_correction`) | `None`, `''` and `'  '` are each asked **twice**, the correction carries `empty or truncated`, both calls' tokens land (28), `reserved` returns to 0, the persisted activity is still `failed` and names the stage |
| `test_an_empty_answer_is_retried_once_and_can_succeed` | empty once, then a valid answer: `ask('design')` returns the result instead of raising, two calls, 28 tokens |
| `test_a_research_survives_an_empty_ideation_answer` | run level: the ideate stage answers empty once, the correction is enough, and the research settles `completed` with no budget or round loss |

## Cross-service artefacts this changes with it

The old contract was pinned outside `services/evolve` and both places move here:

- `services/api/src/protocol-compatibility.test.ts`, case `truncated-idea-stage` (tagged `category:st`, so it is the ST gate): it drives the real Python client through the real proxy, and now expects two upstream calls instead of one, 28 persisted tokens instead of 14, and the corrected failure message. `upstreamCalls` is per kind — 2 for this shape and for `transient-provider-error`, still 1 for `invalid-shape` and `truncated-hidden-reasoning` — and the case also asserts that both calls report their usage. The loop title no longer claims every deterministic shape is never retried.
- `docs/en/model-api-compatibility.md` and `docs/zh/model-api-compatibility.md`: the compatibility contract said an empty or truncated stage is stopped without a correction. Both now state the correction it actually gets and that a second empty answer still fails the stage, with the role in the reason.

## Validation

| Layer | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engine UT | `pytest services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py` on a tree rebuilt from main `9c74af8b` | **44 passed** (42 on main + these two new cases) |
| Mutation | revert `research.py` to main and rerun the three cases | **3 failed** — the fix is what makes them pass |
| ST case, Python half | the `truncated-idea-stage` script run directly against a local 200 with `content: null`, `usage.total_tokens: 14` | 2 requests, 28 tokens, `reserved == 0`, activity `failed`, and the second request carries the new correction text — matches the updated assertions |
| `pnpm ci:st`, `tsc` | not run here | no `node_modules` on this host; the TypeScript half of the ST case is for CI |

Not claimed: no live L5 run (this file has no UI and no journey change).

Fixes #1327.

Turns the millisecond instrumentation the shell, start-stack and jiuwenswarm already emit into a two-layer timing budget gate, mirroring the pyc-budget pattern (pure functions + tests pinning the REAL measured numbers).

Design doc: mac-design perf-guard design P1 (issue #1165 follow-up: "Release CI policy" acceptance item).

## What changes

Six pure additions, no runtime behavior change:

- `application/scripts/lib/parse-perf-timeline.mjs`: parses shell.log perf lines (timestamped relay lines, bare pipe-flush lines, multi-word shell events, warmup 200). Splits sessions at module-load; detects session kind (first/warm) from the provisioning flag. Component durations are event-PAIR values that respect clock domains: same-domain pairs subtract domain-local offsets, cross-domain pairs (api-spawn->HEALTH-200, AGENT-READY->warmup) use the ISO wall clock.
- `application/scripts/lib/perf-verdict.mjs`: three verdicts - ok / hang (over hangMs or a missing pair: the ready/healthy event never arriving IS the hang signal) / regression (over baseline x 1.4, warn-first, 2-strike hard fail upstream). First and warm sessions get separate budget tables (the unpack tax only exists in first sessions).
- `application/scripts/perf-budget.json`: single source of truth for budgets (H1-H9 hang / R1-R12 baselines from the design doc). Baselines measured on the 2026-11-24 three-session log of the signed v0.4.0 build (first 18.8s / warm 8.5s & 8.2s to AGENT-READY); agent-ready hangMs equals AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS so the gate and the runtime timeout blow together.
- `application/scripts/perf-gate.mjs`: the CLI entry the build smoke step (build-mac.sh step 6, future P3) will call. Exit 0 (ok / regression-warn) / 1 (hang) / 2 (usage). Flags: --json, --fail-on-regression (release runs and the two-strike counter).
- `application/scripts/README-perf-budget.md`: maintainer docs - quick start, mechanism, verdict rules, budget-editing discipline, honest known-limits list.
- `application/test/perf-budget.test.ts`: 21 tests. Fixtures pin the REAL 2026-11-24 measured values (any parser change that stops extracting them turns red by name); W25-shaped inputs (missing-healthy, 2x regression) must NOT pass; fool-proofing: hang lines must sit above regression lines, tolerance locked to the 1.2-2.0 band, every budgeted component must exist in the parser's pair table.

## Impact to review

None at runtime: the gate is read-only over logs, never mutates them, and is not yet wired into any build step. Wiring into build-mac.sh step 6 is the follow-up (P3), gated on owner sign-off of the budget values.

## Validation

- `node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --test test/perf-budget.test.ts`: 21/21 pass.
- End-to-end on the real 2026-11-24 shell.log: 3 sessions (1 first + 2 warm) all ok, exit 0.
- JSON output machine-verified; usage-error paths exit 2.
- No runtime / product code changed: pure additions, gate runs read-only.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable: no app behavior changes. The gate consumes existing logs only.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: None. CI/build tooling only.
Compatibility and migration: Additive only; the gate activates when build-mac.sh step 6 wires it (separate PR, P3).


## Linked issues

- **Relates to #1165** — the macOS desktop adaptation tracker. This PR is the follow-up to its **"Release CI policy"** acceptance item: it adds the machine-checked macOS timing gate (the `macos-desktop` CI job now smoke-launches the packed `.app` and judges the first-run `shell.log` against `perf-budget.json` in `--hang-only` mode, uploading the measured log as an artifact). The concrete v1 policy answer: manual real-Mac evidence stays the baseline source; the CI gate covers the silent-hang class on every PR/push. Evidence summary posted on the issue.
- P2 (wizard/reuse-path instrumentation) and P3-2 (baseline collection from release-run logs, per `README-perf-budget.md` rule 2) remain follow-ups by design.

## Status after merge

Merged as `9c74af8b` (2026-11-25). The body above describes the first review round; final merged state: 11 commits, **19 findings (F1-F19) resolved across 8 review rounds**, **33/33 tests** green, and the CI wiring (`ci.yml` `macos-desktop` smoke + log-artifact upload, shown in the files tab) is **included in this PR** — verified green end-to-end on a real macOS runner before merge (fork Package@macos run 45541198600: ok 10 / hang 0 / exit 0).

Packaged macOS first runs re-point `<dataDir>/envs/*/bin/python*` at the bundled interpreter with a relative symlink computed by `posix.relative`. When the data dir arrives in a symlinked spelling (`/tmp`, `/var`) while `resourcesPath` is the resolved spelling (`/private/tmp`, `/private/var`), the two strings share no textual prefix, `relative()` counts the shorter textual depth, and the link lands one directory short (`/private/private/...`) — the stack then fail-fasts with `SHARED_ENV is missing` (#1374 saw this live).

## Change
- `application/src/bootstrap.ts`: the darwin `fixVenvLaunchers` branch computes the hop target from `realpathOrSelf(venvBinDir)` and `join(realpathOrSelf(<python>/bin), "python3")`. The new `realpathOrSelf` helper falls back to the given spelling when realpath cannot resolve a side, so first run never throws. The target remains relative, preserving the relocation property W17 exists for.
- The realpath-based idempotence gate is unchanged, so an install already carrying the broken target is rewritten on its next launch (the short-circuit path always re-runs this fix). The new test's second phase proves that self-heal.

## Validation
- `cd application && node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --test test/*.test.ts`: 363 tests, 361 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped (win32/darwin-only process-tree tests).
- New POSIX-gated test: alias-spelled data dir under a symlink that adds a component, platform `darwin`; fails on the unpatched code (`python must resolve`), passes with the fix. It also asserts via `readlink` that each written target — first run and healed — stays relative (`posix.isAbsolute` false); an absolute-target mutation fails it with `python target must stay relative`. A second phase stores the old textual target with a valid stamp and asserts the relaunch heals all three links.
- `cd application && pnpm typecheck`: clean.
- Where the test runs: `application/test` is not collected by the Linux ut layer; `pnpm --dir application test` runs in the windows-desktop job (this POSIX case skips there) and on macOS via `application/scripts/build-mac.sh`. The existing W17 darwin cases are macOS-gated and did not run here; their fixtures are untouched.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED: requires a packaged macOS `.app`, unavailable in this environment. The regression is exercised through the real `bootstrapPackaged` entry point with the darwin platform argument in the POSIX test above.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: packaged macOS first runs, and relaunches of affected installs, no longer leave dangling venv launchers.
Compatibility and migration: none; affected installs self-heal on the next launch.

Closes #1376

The L3 Desktop real smoke intermittently failed when the model provider returned HTTP 429. The model connectivity case failed in 2 of 20 baseline runs. The UI displayed the provider error while the test waited 60 seconds for the success message.

## Desktop model connectivity smoke

- Wait for the current model's probe response after each click. Check the success indicator when the probe succeeds.
- Retry an upstream HTTP 429 up to twice, with a random three-to-five-second delay before each retry. A third 429 records `BLOCKED` and keeps the gate non-green. Other probe failures surface immediately.

## Validation

No local suites were rerun for this PR submission. The local L1, UT, ST, and mocked E2E slices were not run on the submitted commit. The E2E results below are from the same test patch before it was applied to the current upstream `main`.

## E2E user journeys

recent_merged.body:
Idea Tree has no release-only real-model journeys for multi-round assessment and recovery. This adds two L5 browser/API journeys and fixes the two engine defects that stopped them from completing.

## The defects this also fixes

**1. A raw control character in the model's JSON.** `parse_json()` rejected a raw control character inside a JSON string, so a model that wrote an unescaped newline into a multi-line field ended the stage. A stage gets exactly one correction, so the whole research was settled as `interrupted`:

```
research settled as "interrupted": propagate: invalid model result after one correction:
Invalid control character at: line 1 column 1204 (char 1203)
```

Measured on a `standard` run: round 3 of 3, phase `propagate`, 15 nodes at depth 3, **585,428 tokens already spent**, all three candidates' design, three assessments and aggregate complete — it failed on candidate node 2's second propagation.

`parse_json()` now calls `json.loads(body, strict=False)`, which keeps that character as text. Truncated or non-JSON answers still raise, and a regression test pins both halves: the raw newline is read as text, and `{"text": ` still raises.

**2. A proposal one refinement past `maxDepth`.** `proposal_path()` raised `Proposal exceeds maxDepth`, and the one correction was not enough because nothing told the model how many refinement steps the ceiling still allowed — at depth 3 under `standard` the allowance is zero:

```
research settled as "interrupted": ideate: invalid model result after one correction: Proposal exceeds maxDepth
```

`maxDepth` is documented in the ideate prompt as "a safety ceiling", so the path is now trimmed to what fits — `path[:max(depth - parent['depth'] - 1, 0)]` — and the parent and candidate legality checks are unchanged; a proposal that fits keeps every step. When the parent already sits at `maxDepth - 1` the allowance is zero, so no direction node fits: the candidate attaches directly under that parent and **records the direction it could not place** as `trimmedDirection` rather than discarding it. Tests pin all three shapes.

## A behaviour change this PR makes on purpose

A stage gets one correction, and when the corrected answer is still invalid the engine settled the whole research as `interrupted`. That made one bad field fatal for a run that had already spent minutes of model time, and it was measured four times in one day:

| Failure | Where |
| --- | --- |
| a raw control character inside a JSON string | `propagate` |
| a proposal one refinement past `maxDepth` | `ideate` |
| two consecutive JSON objects | `ideate` |
| `targetedWeakness must contain 1-2000 characters` | `ideate` |

The first three are tolerated in `parse_json` / `proposal_path`. The fourth is why ideation is now retried at the run level: **a bad ideation round is skipped, not fatal.** `round` still advances, the failed `ideate` activity keeps the error, and the next ideation continues. A research that never produced a candidate still settles `interrupted` with the model's error, so a genuinely broken model still fails.

**Two unit tests that pinned the previous one-shot behaviour were updated with it**, deliberately and visibly: `test_invalid_response_corrected_once_without_partial_tree` now expects six calls and 30 tokens instead of two and 10 (three skipped rounds), and `test_an_unusable_ideation_round_is_skipped_not_fatal` is new: two invalid answers in the first round, a skip, then a successful round that completes with a candidate. Removing the skip makes that new test fail.

## What the journeys add

Both use standard exploration (three rounds of three candidates) and a two-hour per-case safety timeout.

**Release-gate role, decided by the release owner on 2026-11-25:** a `standard`-intensity research is the intended L5 gate, so both cases keep `@tier:l5` with the default `reviewed` status and no `@status:quarantined` tag. A failing case blocks the draft Release and its assets by design; the creating stage retries up to three times before the case fails, and a fourth miss is still a failure.

## What the current head changes

- **Polls survive a transient read failure.** The reads inside the waits cover 20–30 minutes of a paid run, so passing every read through `RunPollRecovery` lets three 502/503/504/ECONNRESET/timeout failures be retried instead of ending the case; writes (create, pause, continue) are never replayed.
- **`blocked` is a wait, not a terminal state.** `runs/index.ts` resumes the same run once a card is decided, so a `blocked` run only fails the step when a pending permission or configuration card actually needs a person; otherwise the step keeps polling.
- **A settled run names the card it is waiting on.** When a run reports a terminal status without a research, the step reads `GET /api/permission-requests?sessionId=` and `GET /api/sessions/:id/configuration-requests`, filters them to the states that still wait, and fails with those summaries or capability ids. A failed card read is reported in that message rather than dropped as "no pending card". `expect.poll` retries any non-matching value, so the terminal case throws instead of returning a value the matcher would retry.
- **The Session allows the governed tools a standard research needs.** A three-round standard research prepares its inputs with governed tools, and the default approval mode parks the run as `blocked` on the first one — measured twice, both cases, ~10 minutes each, no research created. The Session is created with `approvalMode: "always_allow"`; approval surfaces have their own journeys (`journey-governed-download-approval`, `journey-sandbox-network-consent`).
- **The exploration override is session-scoped, not deployment-wide.** The previous revision rewrote `/api/settings/idea-tree` and restored it in `finally`, so a killed worker could leave a shared stack on the wrong template, and a failed restore replaced the real failure. The journey makes one write, `PATCH /api/sessions/:id` with `ideaTreeOverride`, which dies with the Session. It sets exactly two of the five fields the override accepts (`templateId`, `explorationIntensity`, out of `templateId`/`explorationIntensity`/`maxDepth`/`maxNodes`/`scoreDirection`); nothing outside that set (`designSystemPrompt` and the other system-level fields) is written anywhere, so both cases stay session-local. The tag moves from `@isolation:global` to `@isolation:session`. `research.settings` is asserted against `{ templateId, explorationIntensity: "standard" }`.
- **The waits are ordered under the case budget instead of summing past it.** The previous revision summed 300s + 1800s + 6600s = 8700s of polls inside a 7200s case timeout, so a hang reported as a case timeout with no step name. The stage caps now total 3 x 600s to create + 120s running + 480s paused + 300s resumed + 4200s terminal = 6900s. They are stage caps, not a bound on the case: `openSession()` alone can spend about 340s per attempt, so the real limit is the 7200s case timeout, and the caps above only decide how long each wait may take before it gives up by name.
- **The creation budget is sized from a measured attempt.** A run of the recovery prompt spent more than 300s preparing its inputs — still on turn 5, that turn carrying 142K input tokens — before it could call `create_idea_research`, while another run of the same prompt completed the whole research in 23.4m.
- **The pause only fires while the engine is running.** Sending `operation: "pause"` the instant a research appears could race a research that had already settled; the paused budget then waited on a state that could never arrive. The step waits for `running` first, and after `continue` polls until the status leaves `paused`.
- **The reload step checks the page, not only the API.** After `page.reload()` the journey asserts the user-visible Idea Tree control region is back, then reads the API; asserting only the API would pass even if the page had dropped the research.
- **A non-`completed` settlement names its reason.** Every wait stops on any terminal status (`completed`, `paused`, `ended`, `interrupted`) and the assertion reports `research.reason`.
- **The creating stage is retried up to three times, and that has already saved a case.** The agent starts the research only about half the time (see below), so `Start research` makes up to three attempts, each on a fresh Project and Session, and only fails after the third miss. Measured once on the recovery journey: attempt 1 timed out after 600s waiting for a research, attempt 2 created it, and the case went on to pass — the log shows `[l5-start] attempt 1/3 did not create a research` followed by `[l5-start] created on attempt 2/3`. Assertions after that step are never retried, so a real regression still fails immediately. Whole-case retries would be simpler but four attempts at ~105 minutes do not fit the 240-minute research-worker ceiling; three create attempts plus the terminal cap come to 6900s inside the 7200s case budget, so a third miss still fails by name instead of dying as a case timeout with the cleanup unfinished.
- **`.ci/README.md` real case counts** updated for the two new identities: L5 64 → 66.

## Validation

| Layer | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E2E metadata | `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs` | 128 spec files, 0 errors |
| Collection | `npm --prefix .e2e run test:real:list` | 70 tests in 13 files; both L5 identities listed once each |

Local UT, ST and mocked E2E are **not** claimed here: they do not exercise this file, and the Windows host cannot run the suite's postinstall. `UT` and `ST` do run in this PR's CI now that it is ready — a draft skips them by policy (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:227,403`) — and both are green on `0a123f08`.

## Real L5 execution

Recorded on `7dfc8529` and `8de4cc92`. The current head (`dd9148f0`) has not been executed; `0a123f08`, the commit under the rows below, differs from it by one cleanup log line, an explicit merge counter with identical behaviour, and one unit test. Stack built from main, WSL Ubuntu / linux-amd64 on `http://127.0.0.1:4310` (default port and repository-default data directory, not isolated), backend `legacy` (`--no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`), model `http://113.46.219.251:8080/v1` with `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, Playwright `workers: 1`. The synced tree has no `.git`, so the fixed `skills/idea-tree-team/SKILL.md` description (the #1312 fix) identifies the code that ran.

| Head | Case | Result | Wall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `7dfc8529` | L5 Idea Tree: Multi-round water treatment research | **passed** | 22.2m |
| `7dfc8529` | L5 Idea Tree: Resume a materials research | **passed** | 31.7m |
| `8de4cc92` | L5 Idea Tree: Multi-round water treatment research | **passed** | 19.5m |
| `8de4cc92` | L5 Idea Tree: Resume a materials research | **passed** | 33.7m |
| `0a123f08` | L5 Idea Tree: Multi-round water treatment research | **passed** | 22.9m |
| `0a123f08` | L5 Idea Tree: Resume a materials research | **passed** | 34.9m |

`7dfc8529` gave `2 passed (54.0m)` and `8de4cc92` gave `2 passed (53.2m)`, both with `exit=0` and every journey report PASS, and in both runs `[l5-start]` never fired — the creating stage succeeded on the first attempt. `8de4cc92` is also the head that added the panel guard; its run passed through the old visibility check rather than the current `aria-expanded` one. The `0a123f08` rows were produced on a tree rebuilt from this PR's base `d13cead9` with the five files from that head — the head that changes the guard, the budget arithmetic and the ideation-skip behaviour — and both cases passed there. Read these rows next to the ~50% record below, not as a settled rate.

Both `0a123f08` rows are clean, uninterrupted runs. The water case completed 3/3 (57.1s / 1301.0s / 743ms) inside one pass of the whole file; the resume case was run on its own and completed 4/4 (72.5s / 59.2s / 1916.8s / 816ms), 34.9m total. In both, `[l5-start]` never fired — the creating stage succeeded on the first attempt — and the run log carries no skipped ideation round; the Projects the cases created were removed, so no `L5 Idea Tree` leftover remained on the stack.

The numbers above are read from each run's own artifacts rather than from a summary: the journey report (`结果 **PASS**`, `耗时 2050.6s`, 4/4 steps at 72.5s / 59.2s / 1916.8s / 816ms) and `run.log` (`1 passed (34.9m)`, `exit=0`, wall 2054s) for the resume case; `1360.2s` and 3/3 for the water case. Both runs were executed on the shared stack by the campaign that owns it, not by me.

The slowest observed step is the resume case's terminal wait at 1916.8s, about 46% of the 4200s `terminalBudget`. That is the number to look at first if the cap is ever tightened.

## Known coverage gaps

1. **A live-model empty or truncated answer can still settle a research as `interrupted`.** That is the engine's designed behaviour (`research.py:318-319`); the case reports the reason rather than retrying it.
2. **Approval and configuration interactions are not covered here.** The Session runs with `always_allow`, so an approval card cannot appear; those surfaces are covered by their own journeys.
3. **Cost is not recorded.** The case's `finally` calls `cleanupJourney`, which deletes the Project and with it the research record, and no usage rows survive that window — a passing run's token ledger is not recoverable, so no cost figure is quoted.
4. **No `maxTokens` cap is set.** A standard research legitimately needs three rounds of three candidates with three assessors each; a cap low enough to bound cost would stop the run before the multi-round assertion.
5. **Backend.** The runs use `legacy`; the daily profile defaults to `jiuwenswarm`. Whether `jiuwenswarm` passes is not covered.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: two engine fixes users can see — a research that used to settle `interrupted` mid-run (a raw control character in the model's JSON, or a proposal one refinement past `maxDepth`) now completes, and the direction a ceiling trim cannot place is kept on the candidate. The rest of the diff is test coverage.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Running the release profile from the general CI entry point can share its concurrency group with other CI runs. The Release workflow can now be dispatched on demand and runs the same L5 test plan, including UT/ST coverage reporting, without requiring a release tag.

## Release gate

- Add manual dispatch to Release, using the selected ref's application version to stamp build artifacts. Pass through the backend and worker limit to the existing reusable CI workflow.
- Give L5 runs a concurrency group per workflow, ref, and event. Keep an in-progress L5 run from being cancelled by a later run in its group.
- Collect and report UT/ST coverage from both manual entry points. A version tag push runs L5 with coverage disabled and still creates the draft Release after a successful gate.

## Validation

| Check | Planned | Executed | Passed | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Local `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 | 4 | 4 | Passed |
| Local CI self-tests (`node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`) | 222 | 222 | 222 | Passed |
| GitHub PR gate L1 | 4 | 4 | 4 | Passed |
| GitHub PR gate UT | 8,368 | 8,368 | 8,368 | Passed |
| GitHub PR gate ST | 69 | 69 | 69 | Passed |
| GitHub PR gate mocked E2E | 6 | 6 | 6 | Passed across both shards |

`actionlint` passed on the original head before the documentation-only follow-up. On `53a81ad2`, GitHub Actions passed Coverage, both Linux binary builds, Docker, and `merge-gate`. CodeCheck and CLA also passed. The full L5 suite is outside the PR profile.

[GitHub Actions run 45421640225](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45421640225)

## E2E user journeys

**Product E2E: not applicable.** This change only affects GitHub Actions entry points and coverage artifacts. The workflow contract tests cover L5 concurrency and the manual versus tag-triggered paths.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`

User impact: Release maintainers can run the L5 gate manually and inspect its coverage report. The application is unaffected.

Compatibility and migration: None.

GitHub creates the 16:00 UTC Nightly run hours late, so the normal start is a project dispatch and the cron is only a fallback. The guard that decides whether the cron run is still needed asked `gh run list` for a successful dispatch without a branch filter, so a dispatch created at any ref could suppress the fallback at another ref, even though the `concurrency` group is already scoped per ref.

## What changed
- The guard's `gh run list` now passes `-b "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"`. The other flags are unchanged: `-w nightly.yml -e workflow_dispatch -s success --created ">=${since}" --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq 'length'`.
- `.ci/nightly-guard.test.mjs` passes `GITHUB_REF_NAME` to the extracted guard script, reads flags back from the recorded `gh` argv, asserts `-b main` on the no-dispatch and pre-16:00 lookback cases, and adds a `ci/l5-biomnibench-da` case so a hard-coded `main` cannot pass.

This revision changes no file content: both files are byte-identical to the previous head (blobs `82c869ce`, `5aa6d1ac`). The branch is only rebased onto `main` at `77b3a938`, so L1's changed-path check no longer compares this pull request against a base that predates its own changes. `git diff | git patch-id --stable` is `84ab5a11` before and after.

## Validation
- `node --test .ci/nightly-guard.test.mjs`: 9 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm ci:selftest`: 229 passed, 0 failed.
- `.ci/changed-path-check.mjs` with base `a8573558` and head `230837a7` (the failing L1 run) exits 1 with 7 unmapped added sources; with base `77b3a938` and the rebased head it prints `OK: 0/0 mapped` and exits 0.
- Product UT/ST/E2E layers were not rerun: only the Nightly workflow and its hermetic test are touched.

## E2E user journeys
Not applicable: no user-observable product path changed; the guard's behaviour is covered by the bash test above.

## Release
Release category: release:internal
User impact: none; Nightly builds the same artifacts and reports the same outcome.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Refs #1237

The Issue stays open on merge: its first acceptance criterion — the project scheduled task, including its "no run queued or in progress" pre-check — is not evidenced by this workflow's run history, and this pull request only makes the cron fallback safe when that dispatch does not run.

### Tests

```
node --test .ci/nightly-guard.test.mjs && pnpm ci:selftest
```

recent_merged.body:
A `necessary` export materialised every run event and then walked the same streams again for the trajectory; CAS sizing streamed (and hashed twice) payloads whose length was already in metadata. The dialog re-walked the session tree repeatedly, and an export task walked it twice.

## What changed
- `necessary` no longer calls `exportRunStreams`. Its omitted-event count reuses the trajectory walk and counts only streams that walk did not open, so it matches `complete` exactly for orphan tool streams and legacy main arrays. The builder-only count is stripped before records are written.
- Added `ContentStore.storedSize` for preview sizing. It declines ambiguous multi-layout objects; the preview then uses a verified read so it sizes the same intact copy the writer emits. The writer still verifies every object.
- A panel request now takes one revision snapshot: `watch` only registers, `defaults` builds. The build reports when its own reconcile wrote provenance; only then does the request take a second walk, adopt it and retry. Cache entries are published under the final revision, and queued profiles remove pre-adoption keys on both success and ready paths.
- Added `research-package.stage` timing for route preflight, enumerate, records, trajectory, summarize, CAS sizing and write.

## Measured performance
Committed script `scripts/measure-research-package-export.mjs`, run as `node --import tsx scripts/measure-research-package-export.mjs --events <N> --cas-bytes <B> --rounds 5`. One warm-up, median of 5 rounds, baseline `e61b1d29` detached worktree vs this head on the same host. The reporter's 189 KB/1.8 GB data is unavailable, so this is a synthetic fixture: 1 session, 1 completed run, 0 workspace files, 3 referenced CAS objects (50% code, 25% stdout, 25% stderr).

| Fixture | preview | export build+write | exportRunStreams | cas.stream (preview) | revision walks | omitted = complete |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 500k events, 1 MiB CAS | 2682 → 1573 ms | 2841 → 1526 ms | 1 → 0 | 3 calls / 1,048,576 B → 0 / 0 | 11 → 1 | 500000 = 500000 |
| 200k events, 112 MiB CAS | 1349 → 657 ms | 1783 → 1325 ms | 1 → 0 | 3 calls / 117,440,512 B → 0 / 0 | 11 → 1 | 200000 = 200000 |

Export `cas.stream` stays 6 calls (hash + write) in both, because the writer still verifies. Packages stayed ~4.3 KB and ~117.4 KB. The earlier "up to 15 walks" was inferred from the code (3 per profile); the measured baseline for the five-profile request is 11, and this head is 1.

## Validation
- Local: `pnpm typecheck`; CAS 60 pass / 2 skipped; research preview/necessary/export/listing/replay/store/trajectory 184 pass; `research-package-http` 29 pass; full API 2514 pass / 9 fail / 2 skipped (unrelated: six need bubblewrap, one dirty-worktree guard, two model.usage assertions reproduce on baseline); `pnpm ci:selftest` 220 pass, `pnpm docs:lint` clean, `pnpm architecture:check` 121 pass plus one unrelated jiuwenswarm relative-path assertion.
- GitHub Actions on head `10a2e7015` (same production code; this update adds only the measurement script): L1, UT (11m46s), ST, both mocked L2 E2E jobs, Docker, both binary builds and merge-gate passed; Coverage was still running.
- Local tagged UT/ST/E2E are BLOCKED at preflight `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE` (bwrap absent, non-root); the GitHub layers above ran them.

## E2E user journeys
Passed in GitHub Actions: L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config) and L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys). Locally the tagged layer is BLOCKED by the missing bwrap preflight, so no local journey ran.

## Release
Release category: release:performance
User impact: the export dialog and necessary package build no longer pay for the full run history twice.
Compatibility and migration: none; the package format and omitted-count semantics are unchanged.

## Remaining risk
`sessionTrajectory` still makes one index pass over run events, so the work stays linear in that pass but no longer repeats `exportRunStreams`. A preview that writes workspace provenance takes the documented second walk, and each queued profile re-checks `canWarm` (11 probes in the five-profile test). An external evidence change during a build returns that request's snapshot; the next poll recalculates, and export is still stopped by its post-write revision check.

Closes #1365

pnpm typecheck && pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/cas test && pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api exec node --import tsx --test src/research-package-necessary.test.ts src/research-export-previews.test.ts src/research-package-exports.test.ts src/research-package-http.test.ts
```

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
The session-level Idea Tree settings card stored parameters but started nothing, and the research card could go missing. Both are fixed, and the card now works the way the rest of the composer does: it puts a command token in the box instead of acting on it.

## 1. The card offers 确认 / 取消 / 覆盖全局设置, and says what they mean

`apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaTreeOverrideDialog.tsx` drew four actions: 取消, 只用于本次会话, 跟随全局设置, 覆盖全局设置. 跟随全局设置 is gone; the card now draws exactly 确认, 取消 and 覆盖全局设置, and the hint states the contract: confirming applies these values to this conversation, puts the Idea Tree command in the composer, and leaves the global defaults alone; only 覆盖全局设置 writes the defaults.

The undo the removed button provided is visible instead of implicit: every row shows the deployment value it inherits (`全局：5`) and marks the ones this conversation has moved away from (`已覆盖`), so putting a field back to that value and confirming releases the pin — `saveSession`'s empty-diff path writes `{}`, which the Session normalizer reads as no override.

## 2. Confirming seeds the command; the reader sends it

Confirming used to close the card and send the message itself. That made it answer for things it cannot know — a turn already running drops the send without a word, and there was no objective yet — and it made the card the only place the research could start.

It now places `/idea-tree-team` in the composer as the existing blue command token, with the task the reader had already written under it. They complete the task and press send; that send starts the research, and the parameters are read at creation (`services/api/src/idea-tree/research.ts` calls `resolveIdeaTreeSettings(sessionId)`).

- A typed `/idea-tree` keeps its own command in the token, so the token never claims a different command than the one typed.
- A draft that is only a command contributes no task (`ideaTaskOf`), so `/idea-tree-team` followed by 会话设置 can no longer send `/idea-tree-team /idea-tree-team …`.
- A sent token is the confirmed pass: `sendMessage` composes the token and the task and never defers back into the card.
- With nothing written the token cannot be sent at all: the composer's send button and Enter both require a task, so the reader writes the question before anything leaves the box. The box asks for one in the token's own words.

## 3. Confirming is refused when it could not write

From the settings row the confirm is also the write, so it is offered only with a conversation open and a draft that was actually read: no Session, or a failed settings read, leaves 确认 disabled rather than placing a token that would run on the deployment values while the hint promises "these values". A command the reader typed still comes back to them as a token even when the read failed — that path writes nothing by design.

## 4. The research card no longer goes missing

`idea_research.created` sat in the run-stream reducer's deferred list, so the desktop ignored it. The list was only re-read while the command's five-minute waiting window was open, and a real model spends that long on preparation before it calls `create_idea_research` — after which nothing re-read the list and the card at the transcript's foot never appeared. The event is now counted (`run-stream/model.ts`, `reducer.ts`) and the app re-reads the list when it arrives, the same way `evolve_run.created` already did.

## 5. Documentation matches the card again

Both `docs/{zh,en}/developer-docs/desktop-frontend.md` described 只用于本次会话 and 跟随全局设置 → `null`. They now describe the three actions, the inherited-value rows, the release-by-reverting path, and the token the confirm seeds.

## Screenshots

Component-level renders of the repository's own `IdeaTreeOverrideDialog` and `Composer` with the app's own stylesheet, driven by stub clients — not the full application journey, and the Electron window is not automated in this environment.

- before = `77b3a93883408c84dc11205f3f0f9553fc4c3068` (main), after = `4f64d464cc7e89b8f1f4859e78944d68facc2e76`
- all pinned to the storage commit `135d1a77e36105d2d585fb596e05be9a78bb1ea5` (`shots/idea-tree-params/`)

| | zh-CN | en |
|---|---|---|
| before (four actions) | ![before zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/135d1a77e36105d2d585fb596e05be9a78bb1ea5/shots/idea-tree-params/before-zh.png) | ![before en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/135d1a77e36105d2d585fb596e05be9a78bb1ea5/shots/idea-tree-params/before-en.png) |
| after (three actions) | ![after zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/135d1a77e36105d2d585fb596e05be9a78bb1ea5/shots/idea-tree-params/after-zh.png) | ![after en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/135d1a77e36105d2d585fb596e05be9a78bb1ea5/shots/idea-tree-params/after-en.png) |

A conversation that pins 最大深度 3 — the deployment value and the `已覆盖` badge are the visible replacement for the removed button:

![after pinned zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/135d1a77e36105d2d585fb596e05be9a78bb1ea5/shots/idea-tree-params/after-pinned-zh.png)

The token the confirm leaves in the composer, with the task under it and its ✕ to drop it:

| | zh-CN | en |
|---|---|---|
| composer, task written | ![token zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/135d1a77e36105d2d585fb596e05be9a78bb1ea5/shots/idea-tree-params/composer-token-zh.png) | ![token en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/135d1a77e36105d2d585fb596e05be9a78bb1ea5/shots/idea-tree-params/composer-token-en.png) |
| composer, no task yet — send disabled | ![empty zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/135d1a77e36105d2d585fb596e05be9a78bb1ea5/shots/idea-tree-params/composer-empty-zh.png) | ![empty en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/135d1a77e36105d2d585fb596e05be9a78bb1ea5/shots/idea-tree-params/composer-empty-en.png) |

## Tests

Run on `apps/desktop` against this tree, with the linux-tagged cases executing rather than skipping:

- `tests/idea-send-gate.test.ts` — the token is the command the gate knows; `ideaCommandOf` / `ideaTaskOf` keep the typed command and its task apart; a command-only draft carries no task; `composeIdeaMessage` with and without a task
- `tests/idea-tree-override.test.tsx` — three labels and no 跟随全局设置, the hint, the inherited value and badge, confirm refused with no Session and after a failed read, confirm writing then seeding, the failed-write retry
- `tests/composer.test.tsx` — the idea-tree row hands the composer's draft to the card, and a seeded token sends the command with the task written under it
- `tests/evolve-model.test.ts` — `idea_research.created` counted, the two counters kept apart
- full desktop suite: **1494 tests, 1494 pass, 0 fail**; `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` (that project already includes `tests/**`) and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` at the repo root exit 0; `markdownlint-cli2` clean on both docs

Still hand-verified: the App-level press of 确认 (the dialog, the command helpers and the composer handoff are each tested; the glue between them is not), and no research was run against a real model.
